bugs_issues.title: Two redactions of different targets can run at once, and each one's audit and receipt then describes the other's work
bugs_issues.body: ### Two redactions of different targets can run at once, and each one's audit and receipt then describes the other's work Severity: High · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Also recorded as: F-1303 (playbook arm, S1, reproduced-live; [13.json](../../experiment/playbook-completion/findings/audit/13.json)). (crosswalk) Found by: [witness_concurrent_targets_break_the_marker](results/ledger_redaction/20261114T044401Z-prove/receipt.json) in [redaction.rs](models/ledger_redaction/redaction.rs) (Variant serial: false): the marker names target A while run B writes tombstones; B's final step removes the marker while A is unfinished and a commit into A is then admitted. [witness_race_then_resume_loses_attribution](results/ledger_redaction/20261114T044401Z-prove/receipt.json) is a classification fact, not a trace of the lifecycle model (review R1-core R1-1; round2-core R2-2): with the knowledge another target's final step removes, `Matches` answers Unknown for A's remaining qualifier records. Reproduced by: [redaction_concurrent_targets](receipts/native/redaction_concurrent_targets.json) (final, hash-stamped run) — while an ordinary long commit held the head lock, `redact(None, prefix="tA")` and `redact(None, prefix="tB")` both passed their entry checks. B completed: its single redaction revision (seq 6, target digest of `tB|`) names revisions 2 (tenant A's) and 3, and its receipt reports 20 records tombstoned, 2 revisions' metadata cleared and 2 idempotency keys removed, tenant A's included. B's final step removed the marker while A was still running, and a commit into A's target was then accepted (seq 7). A went on to tombstone that commit's records and ended with `RedactionTargetLiveError` (the late commit made `tA|` content live), leaving its own marker in place. The model witness's mid-run commit window was hit natively. Expected: ADR-0013 "A redaction of a different target is refused until the first one finishes"; spec 256 Decision 1 (Tom, 2026-10-22): the redaction revision names *the* redacted revisions; Decision 3: while a redaction runs, nothing may be written into its target. Observed: `LedgerRedact.Redact` compares the marker before taking any lock (LedgerRedact.cls:202-205); the marker is written lazily by the first batch that finds a match (:322-324) and never compared by `BatchInLock` or `FinalInLock`; the counters and redacted-revision list under `^IVG.Ledger("redacting")` are shared by every run (:343-344, :423-428); `FinalInLock` kills the marker whoever owns it (:439). Consequence: an audit trail that names the wrong tenant's revisions and a receipt that reports the other tenant's work as its own; a window, observed natively, in which a commit into the unfinished target is admitted, after which the run tombstones that commit's records while their content is live, ends refused, and leaves its marker blocking readers, verify and every other target until the content is erased again. The two-call tenant recipe (`redact(graph)` + `redact(None, prefix=)`) invites running both at once. By code reading (`FinalInLock` kills the whole `("redacting")` subtree, whoever owns the marker) and that classification fact, B's final step also removes the statement endpoints A's earlier calls learned, so a resumed prefix run of A can leave its remaining qualifier records in clear under a `complete` receipt. That knowledge loss was not observed natively (the native race showed the commit-admission consequence); a single paused and resumed prefix run without the race attributes correctly ([redaction_prefix_resume](receipts/native/redaction_prefix_resume.json)). Repair proposal (not implemented): [simp-001](design_simplification.md#simp-001). Governing statements: [redaction.batches.competing](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.batches.competing), [redaction.audit](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.audit).

B completed: its single redaction revision (seq 6, target digest of `tB|`) names revisions 2 (tenant A's) and 3, and its receipt reports 20 records tombstoned, 2 revisions' metadata cleared and 2 idempotency keys removed, tenant A's included. B's final step removed the marker while A was still running, and a commit into A's target was then accepted (seq 7). A went on to tombstone that commit's records and ended with `RedactionTargetLiveError` (the late commit made `tA|` content live), leaving its own marker in place. The model witness's mid-run commit window was hit natively.

bugs_issues.title: A redaction completes while its target's content is still uncommitted-deleted, and the caller's rollback brings the content back with its history tombstoned
bugs_issues.body: ### A redaction completes while its target's content is still uncommitted-deleted, and the caller's rollback brings the content back with its history tombstoned Severity: High · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Also recorded as: F-C1201 (playbook arm, S1, reproduced-live; [12.json](../../experiment/playbook-completion/findings/audit/12.json)); F-C1301 (playbook arm, S1, reproduced-live; [13.json](../../experiment/playbook-completion/findings/audit/13.json)). (crosswalk) Found by: source review (`LiveRows` reads without locks and the Eraser takes no ledger lock; `aad50087` makes `erase_graph` nest in the caller's transaction on a plain connection) and the native probe below (review R1-core R1-12). Reproduced by: [erasure_caller_transaction](receipts/native/erasure_caller_transaction_redaction.json) — connection 1: `START TRANSACTION`; `erase_graph("gA")` (nested, `$TLEVEL=1`); connection 2: `redact("gA")` completed with 2 tombstones; connection 1: `ROLLBACK`. Afterwards gA has 1 live edge row, its create records are tombstones, and `verify()` reports `diverges`. Expected: ADR-0013 "Redaction only follows erasure. It is refused while any row of the target is live"; CONTEXT.md "Erasure either completes or leaves the graph untouched". Observed: `LedgerRedact.LiveRows` (LedgerRedact.cls:149-178) counts rows with `%SQL.Statement` at the process default isolation and sees the uncommitted deletes as gone; nothing serialises erasure with redaction. Consequence: the history of content that is live again is destroyed; verify never returns to equal for it. Repair proposal (not implemented): read liveness under the same lock or isolation that erasure commits under (e.g. take the ledger head lock in the eraser, or a target lock shared by erase and redact), or refuse redaction while an erase of the target is uncommitted. Open contract: [q-004](open_questions.md#q-004). Governing statement: [redaction.after-erasure](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.after-erasure).

Afterwards gA has 1 live edge row, its create records are tombstones, and `verify()` reports `diverges`.

bugs_issues.title: Deleting one of several parallel edges through the ledger removes the adjacency of the edges that remain
bugs_issues.body: ### Deleting one of several parallel edges through the ledger removes the adjacency of the edges that remain Severity: High · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: [witness_ledger_delete_rel_drops_survivor_indexed and witness_ledger_delete_rel_drops_survivors_non_indexed](results/graph_structure/20261114T000451Z-prove/receipt.json) in [graph_structure.rs](models/graph_structure/graph_structure.rs) (B-structure O5/F3; control `as-built-delete-rel-without-line-689` attributes the witness to line 689); A-structure F3 and S4 ([intent](../uplift/ivg-verus-initial/intent/graph-structure.md)); A-ops hazard (a)6 ([operations](../uplift/ivg-verus-initial/intent/operations.md)); review R2-data R1-2. Reproduced by: [graph_structure_parallel_delete_rel](receipts/native/graph_structure_parallel_delete_rel.json) — in the default graph and in a named graph of an indexed namespace, two parallel `s-p-o` edges, ledger `delete_relationship` of one: before, 2 rows, children `[0,1]`, `#` = 2, degree 2; after, one row remains, but the index has no entry for the triple and the degree and a recount read 0 (expected: a bare leaf and degree 1), while Cypher `MATCH` still returns the neighbour through the SQL row. Expected: every row change moves `out`/`in` in the same transaction and no row is left without adjacency (spec 252 FR-001/FR-016); the multigraph layout keeps one leaf while one edge remains and degree counts live edges (spec 234 FR-003/FR-004; CONTEXT.md:90-95, 103-107). Observed: `LedgerApply.DeleteRelInternal` deletes the chosen row by `%ID` (`LedgerApply.cls:678`); in an indexed namespace the row's functional-index callback (`RemoveKeyed`) already collapses the triple to the survivor's bare leaf, and then `If $Data(^KG("out",...)) Do Adjacency.Remove(...)` (`LedgerApply.cls:688-689`) kills that leaf and any children. Line 689 predates spec 252 (`fa67b2b3`) and lacks the `Indexed()` guard that `OpCreateRel` has (`LedgerApply.cls:508`). In a non-indexed namespace line 689 alone removes every parallel edge's entry. Consequence: the surviving relationships are invisible to traversal, native Cypher and degree until `sync()` or a rebuild; reachable whenever the ledger is enabled in non-strict mode on a multigraph graph (parallel edges come from Cypher `CREATE`). Repair proposal (not implemented): skip line 689 when `Adjacency.Indexed()`, and in a non-indexed multigraph call `RemoveKeyed` with the deleted row's `ekey` (proved: `theorem_repaired_delete_rel_keeps_layout`; single-edge deletes unchanged, `witness_ledger_delete_rel_single_edge_is_right`). Related decision: [q-str-004](open_questions.md#q-str-004). Governing statements: [structure.multigraph.layout](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.multigraph.layout), [structure.multigraph.count](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.multigraph.count).

bugs_issues.title: A cached algorithm answer computed over a write that later rolls back stays current
bugs_issues.body: ### A cached algorithm answer computed over a write that later rolls back stays current Severity: High · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Also recorded as: F-0402 (playbook arm, S2, reproduced-live; [04.json](../../experiment/playbook-completion/findings/audit/04.json)). Severity differs: here High, playbook S2; both are kept. (crosswalk) Found by: [witness_rolled_back_write_poisons_algo_cache](results/graph_structure/20261114T000451Z-prove/receipt.json) in [graph_structure.rs](models/graph_structure/graph_structure.rs) (B-structure O4/F1; repair `theorem_repaired_algo_cache_sound` with `witness_bump_after_rollback_refuses_the_poison`); A-structure F1 and S2; A-platform F-A1 ([intent](../uplift/ivg-verus-initial/intent/platform.md)); A-ops hazard (c)7; review R2-data R1-3. Reproduced by: [graph_structure_algo_cache_rollback](receipts/native/graph_structure_algo_cache_rollback.json) — connection 1 opens a transaction and adds edge `c→a` (token 655000→655001); connection 2 computes WCC (miss, put) and sees `c` joined to `a`; connection 1 rolls back (no `c→a` row); connection 3's WCC is a cache hit at token 655001 and still joins `c` to `a`. Expected: a cached result is valid only while the token it was computed under is current, and a reader caching an uncommitted edge that then rolls back is the unsafe case (CONTEXT.md:118-119; ADR-0012:23-26; spec 236 Story 4; the token audit's fix 3, which bumps after `TRollback` in `BuildKG` for this reason). Observed: writers bump `^KG("__version")` inside their transaction (`Adjacency.cls:92`) and `$Increment` is not rolled back; `_cached_algorithm` reads the token and stores the answer with no writer-lock probe (`iris_sql_store.py:958-981`; `AlgoCache.cls:27-51`); no rollback path bumps the token (`_write_txn.py:234-253`; `Txn.cls:49-58`; Eraser catches at `Eraser.cls:260, 459, 630`). Consequence: PageRank, PPR, WCC and CDLP answers include an edge that never committed and are served as current until the next adjacency write anywhere in the namespace. Severity is High because the answer served is wrong, not merely stale, it is served as current, and the native run reaches it with ordinary public calls; on a quiet analytic namespace it can persist for a long time (review round2-domains R2-6 asked for this reason). Repair proposal (not implemented): bump the token after every rollback, as `BuildKG` does (proved for the model, but a rollback IRIS performs for a dead process does not bump), or give the cache the degree cache's discipline: probe `^IVG.AdjW` exclusively with no wait before computing and refuse to store if the probe failed or `^IVG.AdjNoLock` is set. Governing statements: [structure.rebuilt.valid](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.rebuilt.valid), [structure.rebuilt.rollback](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.rebuilt.rollback), [algorithms.cache.concurrency](../ontology/features/algorithms.g5.md#algorithms.cache.concurrency).

bugs_issues.title: A temporal write whose structural step fails keeps its raw entry, cannot be finished by a retry, and the bulk fallback reports it written
bugs_issues.body: ### A temporal write whose structural step fails keeps its raw entry, cannot be finished by a retry, and the bulk fallback reports it written Severity: High · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: [witness_partial_write_is_not_repaired_by_retry and witness_bulk_fallback_reports_success](results/temporal/20261114T001508Z-prove/receipt.json) in [temporal.rs](models/temporal/temporal.rs) (B-temporal O1/F2; valid outcome `witness_assert_first_repairs_the_retry`); A-temporal F2, S2, S3 ([intent](../uplift/ivg-verus-initial/intent/temporal.md)); reconstruction check gap G32; review R2-data R1-6. Reproduced by: [temporal_write_modes](receipts/native/temporal_write_modes.json) — `bulk_fallback_insert`: an insert batch with one edge whose endpoint ID IRIS refuses (over 256 characters) returned `written=2, collisions=0` and no error, while the store holds one structural row and the statistics disagree with the raw edges; `bulk_fallback_update`: after the fallback the whole-bucket count/sum/velocity are 2/2.0/4 against the raw store's 2/6.0/2. `partial_write_retry`: a single-edge write refused at its structural step left 1 raw edge and bucket 1 with no statistics, and the insert retry returned without error and wrote nothing more. Expected: a temporal edge implies its structural edge (ADR-0009); a refused write "writes nothing" (`create_edge_temporal` docstring, `temporal.py:260-261`); first-write-wins with counts that match the raw store (spec 254 FR-003); a failed bulk write reports the count written (R203). Observed: `TemporalIndex.WriteStores` writes `tout`, `tlast`, `tin` and `$Increment(bucket)` before `AssertTemporalRow`, with no transaction (`TemporalIndex.cls:95-111`; `temporal.py:12-17` admits the residue); a throw leaves no row, aggregate or attributes, and an insert-mode retry then hits `$Data(tout)` and is a silent collision (`TemporalIndex.cls:84-85`; `InsertEdge` answers 1 for every outcome, `:64`). `bulk_write_temporal_edges` catches the batch failure and re-sends every edge one by one (`iris_sql_store.py:2759-2786`), counting each collision as inserted; in update mode it re-increments the statistics of edges already written. Consequence: a caller is told every edge was written while one has no structural edge, statistics or attributes, and no retry can complete it; windowed statistics disagree with the raw store. Repair proposal (not implemented): run the structural step before the first Set in `WriteStores`, or wrap `WriteStores` in its own `TSTART`/`TROLLBACK 1`; make the bulk fallback raise, or re-send only the edges not yet written. Open choice: [temporal.write.partial-failure](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.write.partial-failure). Governing statements: [temporal.write](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.write), [temporal.structural](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.structural). Iteration 8 strengthens completed-prefix then whole-batch replay with the known F-0502 time carrier: after actual native full success followed by an injected reply error, raw0 can leave both current-time and epoch0 events while count1 is reported. retry_replay derives completed prefix state, entire fallback and final points; positive and prewrite neighbors remain. [Scope and controls](models/retry_replay/NOTES.md). Partial effects within one write, real transport faults, failing fallback items and other modes remain open; no repair or new bug count.

bugs_issues.title: An update at an occupied temporal coordinate counts the edge twice in the statistics
bugs_issues.body: ### An update at an occupied temporal coordinate counts the edge twice in the statistics Severity: High · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Also recorded as: F-0501 (playbook arm, S2, reproduced-live; [05.json](../../experiment/playbook-completion/findings/audit/05.json)). Severity differs: here High, playbook S2; both are kept. (crosswalk) Found by: [witness_update_double_counts](results/temporal/20261114T001508Z-prove/receipt.json) in [temporal.rs](models/temporal/temporal.rs) (B-temporal O1/F1; Q1 option (b) proved consistent by `theorem_stats_repaired_total`); A-temporal F1; A-ops candidate finding and test gap (d) (`test_254_collisions_e2e.py:104-110` asserts no aggregate after an update); review R2-data R1-6. Reproduced by: [temporal_write_modes](receipts/native/temporal_write_modes.json) case `update_double_count` — after an insert and an update of one coordinate, one raw edge (w=9) but the whole-bucket count=2, sum=11.0, velocity=2 (the raw-exact reading expects 1/9.0/1, the docstring 1/2.0); `bulk_fallback_update` shows the same inflation through the bulk path. Expected: the statistics after an update "remain based on the original value" (`temporal.py:273-279`; `TemporalIndex.cls:77-79`; CHANGELOG 4669-4670 and 4914-4915 "tagg not adjusted"); under the raw-exact reading they equal the surviving raw edges. The model shows the as-built result breaks both readings. Observed: with `pMode="update"` `WriteStores` has no early return (`TemporalIndex.cls:82-86`) and runs `$Increment(bucket)` (`:102`) and the count and sum increments (`:117-118`), widening min/max; a later delete rebuilds `tagg` but decrements `bucket` by one only (`:357`). The ledger's `create_temporal_edge` defaults to "update" (`LedgerApply.cls:628`). Consequence: insert w=2 then update w=9 gives count 2, sum 11, bucket 2 for one raw edge; a window aligned to the bucket and one that cuts it answer differently; after the delete the bucket counts an edge that no longer exists. Repair proposal (not implemented): on an update, rebuild the bucket's statistics from the raw edges (as delete does) and leave `bucket` alone. Open choice: [temporal.write.update-statistics](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.write.update-statistics). Governing statement: [temporal.stats](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.stats).

bugs_issues.title: A rolled-back temporal write leaves its statistics counted, so a retry counts the edge twice
bugs_issues.body: ### A rolled-back temporal write leaves its statistics counted, so a retry counts the edge twice Severity: High · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: [witness_refused_changeset_leaves_counts, witness_blocked_changeset_leaves_counts, witness_throw_in_changeset_leaves_bucket, witness_caller_rollback_leaves_counts and witness_caller_rollback_of_ledger_commit_leaves_counts](results/temporal/20261114T001508Z-prove/receipt.json) in [temporal.rs](models/temporal/temporal.rs) (B-temporal O6/F3, with `lemma_refused_commit_restores_journaled`); A-temporal F3. Reproduced by: [temporal_rollback_counters](receipts/native/temporal_rollback_counters.json) — R1 a refused changeset: no raw edge, but the whole-bucket count=1, sum=2.0, velocity=1, and the retry leaves one raw edge with count=2, sum=4.0, velocity=2; R2 a caller's rollback of a ledger commit and R3 of a direct `create_edge_temporal`: no raw edge, count=1; R4 a throw inside a changeset: velocity=1 with no edge. Expected: if a changeset fails, none of its temporal writes may remain, statistics included (spec 224 "atomically with all structural ops", `changeset.py:321-336`; ledger FR-047, a revision exists iff its mutations are visible); USER_GUIDE "Writes inside your transaction" says a caller's rollback removes both and leaves only the version token and generations (`USER_GUIDE.md:236-275`). Observed: `WriteStores` counts with `$Increment` (`TemporalIndex.cls:102, 117-118`), which IRIS does not undo on `TROLLBACK` (ADR-0010 "Context"), while the raw stores are journaled Sets and are undone. Consequence: windowed counts, sums and velocity include edges that do not exist, and every retry of a failed changeset inflates them further, with no error. Repair proposal (not implemented): replace the statistics `$Increment`s with journaled `Set x=$Get(x)+1` (which needs a lock against concurrent writers, see [q-tmp-001](open_questions.md#q-tmp-001)), or rebuild the bucket's statistics from the raw store after a rollback; at minimum list the statistics in the USER_GUIDE's rollback residue. Model comparison: `witness_counters_undone_keep_exact` (counters undone keep the rule). Governing statements: [temporal.ledger.atomic](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.ledger.atomic), [temporal.stats](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.stats).

bugs_issues.title: A rolled-back temporal delete or node erase leaves the bucket's event counter decremented
bugs_issues.body: ### A rolled-back temporal delete or node erase leaves the bucket's event counter decremented Severity: High · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: [witness_rolled_back_delete_undercounts](results/temporal/20261114T001508Z-prove/receipt.json) in [temporal.rs](models/temporal/temporal.rs) (valid outcome `witness_rolled_back_delete_exact_if_counters_undone`); review R2-data R1-9 (the mirror of [bug-tmp-003](#bug-tmp-003)). Reproduced by: [temporal_rollback_counters](receipts/native/temporal_rollback_counters.json) — R5, a caller's rolled-back delete of the only edge: the raw edge is back with whole-bucket count 1 and sum 2.0, but velocity 0 and the raw bucket 0 (expected 1/2.0/1); R5b, one of two edges: velocity 1 and bucket 1 (expected 2); R6, a rolled-back node erasure: velocity 0 and bucket 0 (expected 1). Expected: node erasure keeps the remaining statistics exact and runs inside the erasure's transaction; a failed or rolled-back erase leaves the content untouched (ADR-0004; CONTEXT.md "Erasure"); "if a changeset fails, none of its temporal writes may remain, statistics included". Observed: `RemoveTemporalRow` decrements the bucket with `$Increment(bucket,-1)` (`TemporalIndex.cls:357`), which a `TROLLBACK` does not undo, while its Kill at zero is journaled and restored; since 4.6.4 `delete_edge_temporal` and `delete_node` (→ `TemporalIndex.EraseNodes`) nest in a caller's transaction. Consequence: after a caller rolls back a delete or a node erase, velocity and bucket counts under-count events that still exist. The bucket node is left holding 0 instead of being killed, and `FindBursts` lists every source present in a bucket, so with a threshold of 0 or less it reports a velocity-0 burst (`TemporalIndex.cls:355-357, 784-803`; review round2-domains R2-4). Repair proposal (not implemented): the same as [bug-tmp-003](#bug-tmp-003): journaled updates of the counters, or a rebuild of the bucket after a rollback. Governing statements: [temporal.erase](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.erase), [temporal.delete](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.delete).
bugs_issues.reproduced: [temporal_rollback_counters](receipts/native/temporal_rollback_counters.json) — R5, a caller's rolled-back delete of the only edge: the raw edge is back with whole-bucket count 1 and sum 2.0, but velocity 0 and the raw bucket 0 (expected 1/2.0/1); R5b, one of two edges: velocity 1 and bucket 1 (expected 2); R6, a rolled-back node erasure: velocity 0 and bucket 0 (expected 1).

bugs_issues.title: Search indexes keep answering with content that was erased, and a re-created node inherits the erased text
bugs_issues.body: ### Search indexes keep answering with content that was erased, and a re-created node inherits the erased text Severity: High · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: [witness_erase_leaves_bm25](results/search/20261114T000543Z-prove/receipt.json) in [search.rs](models/search/search.rs) (B-search O5/F1; repair `theorem_repaired_erase_removes_answers`); A-search F1 and S2 ([intent](../uplift/ivg-verus-initial/intent/search.md)); A-ops hazard (a)3; reconstruction check 2(b)12 and correction 6; review R3-platform R1-7. Reproduced by: [search_bm25_erase](receipts/native/search_bm25_erase.json) — a BM25 index built for graph `g5probe_bm25_erase` over one node; `erase_graph` removed the node, yet `bm25_search` still answered `g5p:erase:1` (score 0.288); after the node was re-created with other text, the erased text still scored it. Expected: an erase removes graph content "from every store that holds it" (ADR-0004:10-12, 79-80); `GraphStores.cls:1-16` claims to be the one inventory; `^IVG.AlgoCache` is erased because "no answer outlives erased content" (`GraphStores.cls:113-116`); the Eraser's own reason for erasing `docs` is that text otherwise attaches to whoever re-creates the ID (`Eraser.cls:138-144`). Observed: `^BM25Idx`, `^IVF`, `^PLAID` and `^VecIdx` are in neither inventory list and no erase or delete path touches them (no reference in `Eraser.cls`; `index_protocol.py:41` is the only `bm25_insert` caller). A BM25 index records its graph (`cfg graph`, `BM25Index.cls:168`), and fusion prefers the index recorded for the graph (`vector.py:204-206`). Consequence: erased or deleted content stays retrievable through BM25, fusion and the vector indexes until a rebuild, and a node re-created under an erased ID is ranked by the erased text. Repair proposal (not implemented): let `EraseGraph` drop or empty the BM25 indexes whose `cfg graph` is the erased graph, and list `^IVF`, `^PLAID` and `^VecIdx` in the inventory as unscoped derived stores to rebuild after an erase (proved for BM25 with a frame clause: other graphs' indexes unchanged). The rule is decided for erasure by CONTEXT.md "Erasure", ADR-0004 and ADR-0013 ("cover everything IVG can reach"); upkeep after ordinary node deletes stays the caller's (`bm25_insert`/`bm25_delete`, USER_GUIDE). A replacing restore has the same gap ([bug-plt-024](#bug-plt-024)). Governing statements: [search.erasure.indexes](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.erasure.indexes), [erasure.scope](../ontology/features/erasure.g5.md#erasure.scope), [search.erasure](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.erasure).

bugs_issues.title: A failed BM25 insert or delete rolls back the caller's whole transaction
bugs_issues.body: ### A failed BM25 insert or delete rolls back the caller's whole transaction Severity: High · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Also recorded as: F-C0702 (playbook arm, S1, reproduced-live; [07.json](../../experiment/playbook-completion/findings/audit/07.json)). (crosswalk) Found by: A-search F3 and S3 ([intent](../uplift/ivg-verus-initial/intent/search.md)); B-search S-c and `witness_caller_txn_rollback` (W-O1d) in [search.rs](models/search/search.rs), whose lost-update branch needs premise P_unlock_in_txn ([prove receipt](results/search/20261114T000543Z-prove/receipt.json)); review R3-platform R1-2. Reproduced by: [search_bm25_caller_txn_rollback](receipts/native/search_bm25_caller_txn_rollback.json) — on an engine over a plain DB-API connection, the caller opened a transaction, created a node, then called `bm25_insert` with a document whose ID is too long for a subscript; the insert raised `` and `$TLEVEL` went from 1 to 0, and after the caller's commit its node is gone. [search_bm25_caller_txn_lock](receipts/native/search_bm25_caller_txn_lock.json) showed IRIS keeps the index lock until the caller's transaction ends, so W-O1d's lost-update trace (which assumes the lock is released at the inner `TCommit`) is not reachable; the finding rests on the rollback alone. Expected: an IVG write that fails takes back only its own part; the caller's commit or rollback decides the rest (`_write_txn.py` 4.6.4 docstring; the Eraser's `While $TLevel > tTxnLevel { TROLLBACK 1 }`); a failed index write leaves the index as it was (ADR-0007). Observed: the Insert and Delete catch blocks run `If $TLevel > 0 TRollback` (`BM25Index.cls:487, 508`), which rolls back every level; the under-lock `RequireWritable` refusal (`BM25Index.cls:459`) throws before `TStart` and also lands there. Consequence: a caller that handles the indexing error and commits silently loses every write it made earlier in its transaction. Repair proposal (not implemented): roll back to the entry level only (`TROLLBACK 1` while `$TLevel` exceeds the level found on entry), as the Eraser does. Governing statements: [structure.write](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.write), [search.bm25.write_lock](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.bm25.write_lock).

[search_bm25_caller_txn_lock](receipts/native/search_bm25_caller_txn_lock.json) showed IRIS keeps the index lock until the caller's transaction ends, so W-O1d's lost-update trace (which assumes the lock is released at the inner `TCommit`) is not reachable; the finding rests on the rollback alone.

bugs_issues.title: Claiming the default embedding table for a model that already has a default-graph route makes that model's stored vectors unreadable
bugs_issues.body: ### Claiming the default embedding table for a model that already has a default-graph route makes that model's stored vectors unreadable Severity: High · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: [witness_claim_after_route_splits_pair](results/search/20261114T000543Z-prove/receipt.json) in [search.rs](models/search/search.rs) (B-search O3/F9, W-O3c); A-search F9 and S5. Reproduced by: [search_route_split](receipts/native/search_route_split.json) — a declared model stored a default-graph vector while `kg_NodeEmbeddings` was unclaimed (its own `kg_emb_…` route was created); after `kg_NodeEmbeddings` was claimed for the same model, two registry rows answer `('', model)` and `get_embedding` returns nothing although the vector is still in the `kg_emb_…` table. Expected: one route per (graph, model) pair; a graph's vectors are never split across two tables (FR-011 as quoted at `embeddings.py:270-273`); every reader of a pair reads where its writer stored. Observed: the registry has no uniqueness on `(graph_id, model_key, kind)` (`schema.py:143-160`); `set_embedding_identity`/`initialize_schema` claim `kg_NodeEmbeddings` without moving an existing route (`schema.py:1177-1215, 1512`), and `_read_route`'s preference then picks `kg_NodeEmbeddings` (`embeddings.py:455`; `_route_preference` `:107-118`). Consequence: vectors stored before the claim disappear from reads and search for that model, and undeclared vectors already in the legacy table are read as the model's. Repair proposal (not implemented): enforce uniqueness of `(graph_id, COALESCE(model_key,''), kind)`, or migrate the existing route when the legacy table is claimed (or refuse the claim while a route for the pair exists), so `_route_preference` stops being load-bearing. Governing statements: [search.routes](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.routes), [search.embedding.claim](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.embedding.claim).

bugs_issues.title: The 4.0.0 documents migration can drop the documents table after its copy failed with a tolerated error
bugs_issues.body: ### The 4.0.0 documents migration can drop the documents table after its copy failed with a tolerated error Severity: High · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** No run has produced a copy failure whose message matches the tolerated list; the control flow is read from source (`docs_and_edge_vectors.py:89-97, 647-657` re-read for this entry). Severity is lowered one level from Critical (data loss) for the unconfirmed trigger. Found by: A-platform F-S7 ([intent](../uplift/ivg-verus-initial/intent/platform.md)). Reproduced by: none Expected: the 3.2.0→4.0.0 steps are re-runnable and delete nothing that was not moved first (spec obligation O-MIGRATE; the step order exists because "each step reads what the one before it wrote"). Observed: `_run_tolerantly` treats any error whose text contains `already`, `not unique`, `-201`, `not found`, `does not exist`, `-30>` or `-315` as work a previous pass already did and continues (`docs_and_edge_vectors.py:89-97, 647-657`). `DOCS_FINISH` runs `docs_copy_placed` (`INSERT … SELECT` into the staging table), then `docs_drop_original` (`DROP TABLE docs`) and the rename (`statements.py:102-115, 257-264`). A copy failing with, for example, a unique-constraint (`not unique`) or a "field not found" error is skipped and the source table is dropped. Consequence: documents that were never copied are deleted irreversibly during an upgrade. Repair proposal (not implemented): tolerate errors per statement name (only `docs_staging_create` may meet "already exists"; the copy may never be tolerated), or verify the staging row count before the drop. Governing statements: [install.migration.steps](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.migration.steps), [install.migration](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.migration).

bugs_issues.title: A caller with Cypher read access can forge a CRC-32 collision so that another shape's queries run its compiled code
bugs_issues.body: ### A caller with Cypher read access can forge a CRC-32 collision so that another shape's queries run its compiled code Severity: High · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Proved on the model (collisions exist by `lemma_crc_collision_exists`); not probed natively because forcing a collision of real shapes needs a test hook or a crafted shape. Severity is lowered one level from Critical (an integrity breach other users cannot see) for the unconfirmed trigger. Found by: [witness_collision_swaps_the_class_mid_run and witness_collision_leaves_another_shapes_code_under_an_ok_entry](results/platform/20261114T002651Z-prove/receipt.json) in [platform.rs](models/platform/platform.rs) (B-platform P1, W-O2a, W-O2b); A-cypher F2; review R3-platform R1-3, whose scratch check Adv-2 (`$RUN_DIR/agents/R3-platform/adv/adv2_platform_pshape*.log`) shows that requiring the entry's shape in `Build` closes W-O2b but not W-O2a, and that only unique class names remove the dependency on P-NO-COLLISION. Reproduced by: none Expected: a compiled class answers exactly as the interpreter does, and a stale entry is never run (ADR-0014:16-23; spec 257 US1). Observed: the class name is `IVGC.P<$ZCRC(shape,7)>` (`Gen.cls:69, 183`). `For` detects a colliding shape by its stored shape (`:71`) and rebuilds the same class name for the new shape (`:80-101, 183-207`); `Build` checks the lines' digest but not that the entry's shape is the one the lines were written for (`:177-207`); `RunA` checks the entry once per run (`Exec.cls:158`) and calls `Walk1` per anchor (`:199, 258`). W-O2b needs no run overlap: two first runs of colliding shapes in job mode leave b's entry marked ok over a's code until a deploy or stamp change. Consequence: wrong Cypher answers for every later run of the victim shape, until a deploy or stamp change. Accidental collisions are rare (about 1.2×10⁻⁴ for 10³ distinct shapes between deploys, 1.2% for 10⁴, mostly as recompile thrash), but adversarially the attack is practical: CRC-32 is affine, four free bytes in a label or property name hit any target, the shape text can be reproduced from the open-source planner, and the attacker can run both shapes until the W-O2b ordering lands. Reads write compiled plans, so this needs only Cypher read access through a server whose IRIS login can write `^IVG.CypherCompiled`, including an `IVG_READ_ONLY` server on the default `_SYSTEM` login. `query.compiled.integrity` and `query.compiled.never-stale` hold only under P-NO-COLLISION, which nothing establishes. Repair proposal (not implemented): [simp-cyp-001](design_simplification.md#simp-cyp-001). Governing statements: [query.compiled.integrity](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.compiled.integrity), [query.compiled.never-stale](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.compiled.never-stale), [query.compiled.equal-answers](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.compiled.equal-answers).

bugs_issues.title: Erasing a tenant by prefix leaves its temporal-only events, and the redaction that follows completes while they stay readable
bugs_issues.body: ### Erasing a tenant by prefix leaves its temporal-only events, and the redaction that follows completes while they stay readable Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Also recorded as: F-C1203 (playbook arm, S1, reproduced-live; [followup.json](../../experiment/playbook-completion/findings/audit/followup.json)); F-C1308 (playbook arm, S1, reproduced-live; [followup.json](../../experiment/playbook-completion/findings/audit/followup.json)). Severity differs: here Medium, playbook S1/S1; both are kept. (crosswalk) Found by: [witness_prefix_erase_leaves_temporal_only_content](results/ledger_redaction/20261114T044401Z-prove/receipt.json) (W5) in [redaction.rs](models/ledger_redaction/redaction.rs), with control [prefix-erase-reaches-temporal](results/ledger_redaction/20261114T044554Z-control-prefix-erase-reaches-temporal/receipt.json) (EXPECTED_FAIL); review round2-core R2-1 (scratch witnesses d1/d2 showed the model's earlier erase over-approximated the product). Reproduced by: [erasure_prefix_temporal_only](receipts/native/erasure_prefix_temporal_only.json) — tenant `tE|` had two temporal-only events, one whose endpoint `tE|1` had a node row and one whose endpoint `tE|x` had none; `delete_nodes_by_prefix("tE|")` removed 1 node row; the `tE|x` event stayed readable after the erase and after the redaction, which reported `complete` with 4 records tombstoned; `verify()` was `equal`. Expected: an erase removes graph content from every store that holds it, the temporal index included (ADR-0004; CONTEXT.md "Erasure"); a redaction is refused while any of the target's content is live (CONTEXT.md "Redaction"). Scope (review round 3 R3-reader H2): ADR-0013:37 documents the full tenant redaction for a tenant "whose relationships live in its own graph", and spec 256 ("Not in this spec", `spec.md:161-163`) put off "a tenant-scoped erase of the temporal tiers inside a shared graph" because "with one graph per tenant, `EraseGraph` covers it". The failing case — a tenant's temporal-only events in a shared graph — is therefore outside the documented recipe, but `delete_nodes_by_prefix` still promises erasure from every store (ADR-0004) and the redaction reports `complete` without saying anything is left. Observed: `Eraser.EraseNodes` collects the IDs to erase from `Graph_KG.nodes` rows (`Eraser.cls:331-349`), and `TemporalIndex.EraseNodes` then erases temporal edges only for those IDs (`TemporalIndex.cls:400-440`). A temporal-only predicate writes no node row (`TemporalIndex.cls:103-114`; ADR-0015), so its events whose endpoints have no node row survive. `LiveRows` does not read the temporal index and verify ignores it, so neither notices. Consequence: after an erase by prefix and a prefix redaction of a tenant that shares a graph the tenant's events stay readable through the window reader while the redaction reports complete, verify is equal, and the events' history is tombstoned. The documented prefix recipe misses them; removing them needs their endpoint IDs, then an explicit-id erase (`delete_node(id, graph=…)` or the store's `delete_nodes(ids)`, whose `EraseNodeIds` erases events incident on a named ID with or without a node row, `Eraser.cls:352-389`, `TemporalIndex.cls:421`) or `delete_temporal_edge` per event (review round 3 R3-3, code reading; not run natively). Why Medium: lowered from High in review round 3, because the governing spec deferred this case and the documented recipe assumes one graph per tenant; it stays Medium because the incompleteness is silent (`complete`, `verify()` equal) for a privacy operation. Repair proposal (not implemented): let `EraseNodes` and `TemporalIndex.EraseNodes` also select temporal endpoints by ID prefix, not only IDs that have node rows; count temporal entries as live content in redaction ([q-009](open_questions.md#q-009)). Without the first change, [simp-003](design_simplification.md#simp-003)'s full live-content check would turn every as-built prefix erase of such a tenant into a refusal until the events are removed by ID. Open part: [redaction.after-erasure.temporal](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.after-erasure.temporal). Governing statements: [erasure.scope](../ontology/features/erasure.g5.md#erasure.scope), [erasure.prefix-match](../ontology/features/erasure.g5.md#erasure.prefix-match).
bugs_issues.reproduced: [erasure_prefix_temporal_only](receipts/native/erasure_prefix_temporal_only.json) — tenant `tE|` had two temporal-only events, one whose endpoint `tE|1` had a node row and one whose endpoint `tE|x` had none; `delete_nodes_by_prefix("tE|")` removed 1 node row; the `tE|x` event stayed readable after the erase and after the redaction, which reported `complete` with 4 records tombstoned; `verify()` was `equal`.

bugs_issues.title: Redacting the whole default graph ignores node rows in named graphs and destroys the history of nodes that are still live
bugs_issues.body: ### Redacting the whole default graph ignores node rows in named graphs and destroys the history of nodes that are still live Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Also recorded as: F-1304 (playbook arm, S1, reproduced-live; [13.json](../../experiment/playbook-completion/findings/audit/13.json)). Severity differs: here Medium, playbook S1; both are kept. (crosswalk) Found by: [witness_default_graph_target_is_not_graph_blind](results/ledger_redaction/20261114T044401Z-prove/receipt.json) (W3); `witness_full_check_refuses_the_gaps` shows the stricter check refuses it and still admits the valid run. Review R1-core R1-7 and R1-8: the model's `Erase` removes named-graph node rows for a default-graph target, which the product's does not, so W3 builds the state directly. Reproduced by: [redaction_default_graph_whole](receipts/native/redaction_default_graph_whole.json) — ledger commit of nodes X, Y and an edge X→Y in graph `gN` (the ledger registers X and Y in `gN`); `erase_graph(None)`; nodes X and Y are still rows in `gN`. `redact(None)` completed and tombstoned 4 records of X and Y; `verify()` diverges afterwards. Expected: spec 256 plan.md "The node-liveness check for a default-graph target is graph-blind" (node records and verify ignore graphs); ADR-0013 refusal while any row of the target is live. Observed: `LiveRows` applies graph-blindness only with a prefix (LedgerRedact.cls:155-165); with no prefix it counts `graph_id = ''` rows only, while `Matches` takes every node record (graph "") (:93-94). Consequence: an operator who erases the whole default graph and redacts it with no prefix (a narrow, operator-initiated trigger; the tenant recipe uses a prefix) loses the history of nodes that are still live in other graphs. Verify, which already diverged after the erase, can be returned to equal by an adoption, but the tombstoned history of those live nodes cannot be restored. The Eraser refuses the analogous empty prefix (Eraser.cls:314-318). Repair proposal (not implemented): [simp-003](design_simplification.md#simp-003). Governing statement: [redaction.after-erasure.default-graph](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.after-erasure.default-graph).

bugs_issues.body: ### A redaction reports complete while records it could not attribute still hold the target's content Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: [witness_unattributed_qualifier_survives](results/ledger_redaction/20261114T044401Z-prove/receipt.json) (W4) and `lemma_complete_run_removes_every_target_record`, which needs premise P_ends. Reproduced by: [redaction_unattributed_qualifier](receipts/native/redaction_unattributed_qualifier.json) — an edge written by `engine.create_edge` (allowed outside strict mode), then qualified through the ledger by tuple (statement assigned, `set_qual` record only), then the tenant erased by prefix and redacted: receipt `complete=True`, `records_tombstoned=2`, `unattributed_records=1`, and one `set_qual` record still holds `uSecretQualifier`. Expected: `ledger.redact` docstring and ADR-0013 "Every record of the target becomes a tombstone"; spec 256 FR-001 "MUST replace every record". Observed: `LedgerRedact.Matches` answers -1 when a qualifier record's statement endpoints are unknown (no create/delete record, statement entry removed by the erase) (LedgerRedact.cls:101-110); `BatchInLock` skips it and counts it (:317-320); the run still completes. `unattributed_records` is not documented anywhere. Consequence: tenant strings survive a "complete" redaction; only the undocumented receipt count reveals it. Repair proposal (not implemented): [simp-002](design_simplification.md#simp-002); at minimum refuse completion (or report incomplete) while the count is above zero. bugs_issues.title: A degree cached before a node is deleted and re-created can be served afterwards as current
bugs_issues.body: ### A degree cached before a node is deleted and re-created can be served afterwards as current Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** The model trace is proved, but the race is not natively reproducible without a stall hook (for a small node the recount takes microseconds while the three writer transactions take milliseconds); severity is lowered one level from High. Found by: [witness_aba_delete_and_recreate_serves_stale_degree](results/graph_structure/20261114T000451Z-prove/receipt.json) in [graph_structure.rs](models/graph_structure/graph_structure.rs) (B-structure O3/F2 route 1; repair `theorem_repaired_cache_sound` and `witness_repair_refuses_the_aba_store`; route 2 `witness_rolled_back_kill_restores_stale_entry` is model-only, its product reachability open); A-structure F2; review R2-data R1-8 and R1-10, now in the model: `witness_gen0_erase_alone_serves_stale_degree` (the generation-0 route, non-indexed namespaces only) and the kill-bump repair `theorem_kill_bump_cache_sound` with `witness_kill_bump_refuses_the_aba_store` and `witness_gen0_kill_bump_refuses`. Reproduced by: none yet — [graph_structure_degree_aba](receipts/native/graph_structure_degree_aba.json) ran 3 readers for 120 s (3,129 rounds, about 2.1 million degree calls) with no stale entry: INCONCLUSIVE, not evidence of absence; the reader count is bounded by Community's connection licence. Expected: a cached degree equals a recount at the time it is served, and no count cached before an erase may be served after it, even when later writes bring the generation back to an earlier value (ADR-0012:12-17 and "the cache is derived"; spec 248 spec.md:76-77). Observed: `RemoveSource` kills `^KG("gen")` and `degc` (`Adjacency.cls:376-377`; also `RemoveGraph`/`RemoveAll` and the non-indexed restore, `snapshot.py:1688-1691`), and writers restart the generation from 0 with `$Increment`. The reader's store test and post-store re-read compare equality only (`Adj.cls:75, 78-80`), so a history A→kill→…→A passes both. The generation is killed by `delete_node` (`Eraser.RemoveNode`), by the purge's default `retire_bare_nodes=True` (`Eraser.ForgetNodes` → `RemoveSource`, `Eraser.cls:1320-1327`), by `erase_graph` (`RemoveGraph`, `Adjacency.cls:437`) and by `%BuildIndices`' `PurgeIndex` (`RemoveAll`, `:461`); after a non-indexed `BuildKG`/`sync()` (no generation bump, `Adjacency.cls:826-830`) a single erase completes it. The spec 248 text and the `Adj.cls:46-48` comment claim the re-read closes the erase window; the model shows the re-read is redundant when generations are monotone and insufficient when they are not. Consequence: degree (and so Cypher `size()`/degree answers and degree-ordered plans) for a deleted or re-created node reads an old count until the next write to that node. Repair proposal (not implemented): stamp each cache entry with a never-killed epoch that every kill of `gen`/`degc` increments first, and compare it on a hit (proved for committed kills at any time); or, in `RemoveSource`, `$Increment` the generation instead of killing it (proved: `theorem_kill_bump_cache_sound`; leaves one residue node per erased source, and `RemoveGraph` and `RemoveAll` still need the epoch). Drawing generations from the version token is not a repair ([simp-str-005](design_simplification.md#simp-str-005)). Correct the spec 248 and `Adj.cls` claims. Governing statements: [structure.degree.cache.erase](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.degree.cache.erase), [structure.degree.cache](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.degree.cache).

bugs_issues.title: verify_graph reports healthy parallel edges as missing adjacency and cannot see lost multiplicity
bugs_issues.body: ### verify_graph reports healthy parallel edges as missing adjacency and cannot see lost multiplicity Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: A-structure F7 (source arithmetic; open task T036, `tasks.md:198`; unmet SC-005, `spec.md:355-356` of spec 234). Reproduced by: [graph_structure_parallel_delete_rel](receipts/native/graph_structure_parallel_delete_rel.json) (`f7_verify_before`) — before any delete, a default graph holding two parallel edges reports `ok: 0` with "missing" drift of 1 row in `^KG("out")` and 1 in `^KG("in")` (`sqlEdges` 2, `outEdges` 1). Expected: `verify_graph` reports rows with no adjacency entry and entries with no row, and its `ok` answers whether the graph's adjacency agrees with its rows; in a multigraph the layout holds one leaf plus children for two or more edges (spec 234 FR-004, SC-005). Observed: `GraphVerify` computes `missing = rows − matched distinct triples` (`GraphVerify.cls:78, 104, 128`), so every extra parallel edge counts as missing, and a triple that lost its children still matches. Consequence: an operator sees false drift on every multigraph and may rebuild for nothing, while real multiplicity loss (for example [bug-str-001](#bug-str-001)) goes unreported. Repair proposal (not implemented): compare each triple's row count with its leaf, children and `#` count. Governing statement: [structure.verify](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.verify).

bugs_issues.title: create_edge stores the raw graph name in SQL, so a name with a NUL becomes a second SQL graph sharing one adjacency entry
bugs_issues.body: ### create_edge stores the raw graph name in SQL, so a name with a NUL becomes a second SQL graph sharing one adjacency entry Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: [witness_raw_sql_name_splits_one_index_graph](results/graph_structure/20261114T000451Z-prove/receipt.json) in [graph_structure.rs](models/graph_structure/graph_structure.rs) (B-structure O1/Q5; the model proves the key half only, and is injective only modulo `canonical`); A-structure Q5; review R2-data R1-4. Reproduced by: [graph_structure_keys](receipts/native/graph_structure_keys.json) case K4 — `create_edge` in graph `'g5k'` and in `'g5k'+NUL` gave two `rdf_edges` rows and one adjacency entry; `delete_edge(graph='g5k')` left the NUL row with no `^KG` entry, and `verify_graph("g5k")` then answers `ok` with no SQL edges, so the orphan row is invisible to it. Expected: a graph key is derived from the canonical name and NUL is a transport artifact that is stripped (ADR-0003; `GraphKey.cls:23-37`; CONTEXT.md:50-58). Observed: `create_edge` derives the index key from the canonical name (`nodes_edges.py:1197`) but binds `gid = graph or ""` to SQL (`nodes_edges.py:1213`), so the duplicate guard (`COALESCE(graph_id,'') = ?`, `:1217`) admits a second row; `create_node` binds the raw name with no validation (`nodes_edges.py:1019`). Consequence: one index graph spans two SQL graphs; deleting through either name leaves a row without adjacency that traversal cannot see and `verify_graph` does not report. Repair proposal (not implemented): bind `GraphKey.ForName` (the canonical name) to every SQL `graph_id` and validate in `create_node`. Governing statements: [graph.key.derive](../ontology/concepts/graph-scope.g5.md#graph.key.derive), [graph.names](../ontology/concepts/graph-scope.g5.md#graph.names).

bugs_issues.title: A temporal write creates endpoint nodes that the ledger never recorded, so verify diverges after the ledger's own temporal operation
bugs_issues.body: ### A temporal write creates endpoint nodes that the ledger never recorded, so verify diverges after the ledger's own temporal operation Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: [witness_direct_temporal_write_makes_verify_diverge, witness_ledger_temporal_op_makes_verify_diverge and witness_changeset_op_order_decides](results/temporal/20261114T001508Z-prove/receipt.json) in [temporal.rs](models/temporal/temporal.rs) (B-temporal Q4/F4; valid outcomes `witness_known_endpoints_in_named_graph_keep_verify`, `witness_optout_temporal_write_keeps_verify`); A-temporal F4 and Q3. Reproduced by: [temporal_endpoint_nodes_verify](receipts/native/temporal_endpoint_nodes_verify.json) — V1 a direct write and V2 a ledger `create_temporal_edge` with a new endpoint ID: `verify()` diverges with `unrecorded_writes` on that node; V3 a temporal op followed by `upsert_node` in one changeset: diverges; V4 `[temporal, create_node]` is refused `node_exists` while `[create_node, temporal]` commits; V5 the same under strict mode. Controls C0 (known endpoints) and C1 (temporal-only predicate) stay equal. Expected: commit `43efd473` ("Decided with Tom"): temporal writes create no revisions and "a temporal mirror is no longer an unrecorded write", the mirror including "its endpoints in the edge's graph"; verify reports divergence only for writes that bypassed the ledger. Observed: `AssertTemporalRow` inserts missing endpoint nodes with no record (`Adjacency.cls:597`), also inside `OpCreateTemporalEdge`; `read_canonical` reads every `nodes` row graph-blind (`replay.py:598-600`), and `OpCreateNode` is graph-blind, so an upsert of such a node records nothing and a create is refused (`LedgerApply.cls:215-250`). The purge's `retire_bare_nodes` (default since 4.7.0) deletes bare nodes with no ledger check (`Eraser.cls:1333-1352`). Consequence: a ledger user who writes temporal edges to new IDs gets permanent `diverges` from verify (V3 cannot be fixed by a later upsert), including in strict mode, and the order of operations in a changeset decides between refusal and divergence. Repair proposal (not implemented): either exclude temporal-asserted endpoint nodes from verify as the marked rows are, or record them (or refuse the temporal op) when an endpoint is missing; make `retire_bare_nodes` skip ledger-recorded nodes. Open choice: [temporal.structural.ledger-nodes](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.structural.ledger-nodes). Governing statements: [temporal.structural.ledger](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.structural.ledger), [ledger.verify](../ontology/features/ledger.g5.md#ledger.verify).

bugs_issues.title: Making a temporal-only predicate structural again before dropping its rows strands marked rows that nothing removes
bugs_issues.body: ### Making a temporal-only predicate structural again before dropping its rows strands marked rows that nothing removes Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: [witness_optin_strands_marked_row](results/temporal/20261114T001508Z-prove/receipt.json) in [temporal.rs](models/temporal/temporal.rs) (B-temporal O3/F8, with `lemma_stranded_row_survives_purge`; recovery `witness_optin_strand_recovery_by_drop`; repair `theorem_rows_optin_guarded`); A-temporal F8 and Q4. Reproduced by: [temporal_marked_row_lifecycle](receipts/native/temporal_marked_row_lifecycle.json) case F8 — a marked row of a re-opted-in predicate with no timestamp survives delete, purge, drop (refused: the predicate is structural) and backfill. Cases K1–K3 (marker lifecycle, adoption, temporal-only write) behaved as specified. Expected: a marked row means "this edge exists at some time" and goes with its last timestamp (ADR-0009 and its spec 254 amendment); ADR-0015's migration guidance assumes the drop runs before any toggle back. Observed: the purge skips registered predicates (`TemporalIndex.cls:966`), so after opting out and purging, the rows stay as decided; after `set_temporal_structural(p, True)` `DropRows` refuses a structural predicate (`TemporalPolicy.cls:132-134`), delete finds no timestamp, and no purge range selects the row. Consequence: traversal and `MATCH` keep showing edges whose every event was purged, until an operator re-registers the predicate, drops its rows and opts in again. Repair proposal (not implemented): refuse the opt-in while marked rows of the predicate have no timestamp (proved sufficient), or let `DropRows` accept those rows. Open choice: [temporal.optout.stranded](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.optout.stranded). Governing statement: [temporal.structural.end](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.structural.end).

bugs_issues.title: A temporal aggregate read of min, max or avg over an empty window raises ValueError, although the method promises 0.0
bugs_issues.body: ### A temporal aggregate read of min, max or avg over an empty window raises ValueError, although the method promises 0.0 Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: review R2-data R1-5 (seen in six probe traces); the same error first stopped two cases of the earlier temporal probe runs. Reproduced by: [temporal_write_modes](receipts/native/temporal_write_modes.json) and [temporal_rollback_counters](receipts/native/temporal_rollback_counters.json) — `get_temporal_aggregate(..., "min"/"max"/"avg")` over a window with no raw edge (empty, or holding only counts a rolled-back or refused write left) raised `ValueError: could not convert string to float: 'None'`. Expected: "An empty window or an unknown metric gives `0` or `0.0`, never `None`; a failed server call raises" (`_engine/temporal.py:950-951`). Observed: the store converts the server's answer with `val = str(...)`, so a missing value becomes the text `None`, which is truthy, and then returns `float(val) if val else 0.0` (`iris_sql_store.py:2977-2987`); the engine also returns `None` when no row comes back (`_engine/temporal.py:959`). Consequence: dashboards and callers that read min, max or average over a quiet window get an exception instead of 0.0. Repair proposal (not implemented): test the server value for None before converting, and return `0.0` in the engine's no-row branch, as documented. Governing statement: [temporal.stats](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.stats).

bugs_issues.title: A temporal write that races a purge or delete of the same triple can leave a live timestamp with no structural edge
bugs_issues.body: ### A temporal write that races a purge or delete of the same triple can leave a live timestamp with no structural edge Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Known to the project (spec 254 sign-off) and proved as model traces; not probed. Severity is lowered one level from High. Found by: [witness_purge_write_race_drops_row, witness_delete_write_race_drops_row, witness_purge_write_race_rowless_route and witness_purge_write_race_strands_new_triple](results/temporal/20261114T040433Z-prove/receipt.json) in [temporal.rs](models/temporal/temporal.rs) (W-RACE-1, W-RACE-3, W-RACE-4, W-RACE-5; valid outcome `witness_purge_then_write_reasserts_row`); the repair shape is proved as `witness_recheck_closes_race_row_at_decide`, `witness_recheck_closes_race_rowless_route`, `witness_recheck_closes_delete_race` and `witness_recheck_closes_kill_window` (premise P-LOCK); review R2-data R1-7 (check C) and round2-domains R2-2 (its scratch witness is integrated as W-RACE-4); spec 254 `tasks.md:80-81`; R2-data expectation E18. Reproduced by: none Expected: a temporal edge of a structural predicate implies its structural edge while any of its timestamps exist (ADR-0009's decision; the spec 254 amendment only adds the reverse, that a marked row goes with the last timestamp). Observed: `RetireExpired` (or `DeleteTemporalEdge`) decides that no timestamp survives and then retracts the row; a concurrent `InsertEdge` for the same triple sees `^KG("out")` present, trusts it and skips `AssertTemporalRow`'s insert; the retract then deletes the row. The decide step also puts every structural candidate with no surviving timestamp into `^||IVG.TPurge` whether or not it has a row (`TemporalIndex.cls:956-1013`), and `RetractTemporalRows` tests the marker only at its DELETE (`Adjacency.cls:674`), so a triple that had no row when the purge decided (reachable through the ADR-0015 opt-out/opt-in window or [bug-tmp-001](#bug-tmp-001)'s throw) loses the marked row a concurrent writer asserts before the retraction; the model's decide step takes only triples with a marked row and so hides this route. `TemporalIndex` takes no lock. The 254 sign-off lists the race as open: "A temporal write racing a purge on the same triple can leave a new timestamp without its row … `DeleteTemporalEdge` has the same window." Consequence: a newly written event's edge is invisible to traversal and `MATCH` until another write of the triple asserts the row again. Repair proposal (not implemented): re-check for surviving timestamps under a per-triple lock before the retract, for every candidate, including triples that had no row when the purge decided, or have the writer assert the row without trusting `^KG("out")` while a purge is running. Related question: [q-tmp-001](open_questions.md#q-tmp-001). Governing statements: [temporal.structural](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.structural), [temporal.purge](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.purge).
bugs_issues.reproduced: none

bugs_issues.title: Building or dropping a BM25 index while documents are inserted leaves its counters inconsistent
bugs_issues.body: ### Building or dropping a BM25 index while documents are inserted leaves its counters inconsistent Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: [witness_build_insert_breaks_n, witness_build_insert_double_df and witness_drop_inside_insert](results/search/20261114T000543Z-prove/receipt.json) in [search.rs](models/search/search.rs) (B-search O1/F2; repair `theorem_locked_build_preserves`); A-search F2 and S3; review R3-platform R1-8, after which the model splits Insert and Delete into their steps, so W-O1c is a trace of the model (it fails with Drop disabled), and the repaired Drop and Build wait for an in-flight writer. Reproduced by: [search_bm25_build_insert_race](receipts/native/search_bm25_build_insert_race.json) — 209 inserts committed inside Build's 0.39 s window; afterwards, with no Build in flight, 94 terms had a document frequency that disagreed with their postings (for example `df(beta0)=416` with 420 postings). The drop-inside-insert trace (W-O1c) was not probed. Expected: every index write runs under the index's write lock in a transaction, and the counters are consistent at every committed point (ADR-0007; spec 044 FR-016/FR-018). Observed: `Build` kills and rewrites the index with no lock and no transaction (`BM25Index.cls:97-175`); an Insert after Build's Kill finds no N and starts a new index (`:387`), Build's `IndexDoc` adds the same document's df again, and Build finally publishes its local N, totalLen and vocab_size (`:160-164`). `Drop` kills with no lock (`:587-591`), so an Insert in flight can resurrect a schema-less index. Consequence: BM25 scores use wrong document frequencies and N until the next Build; a resurrected index refuses writers as "schema 1". Repair proposal (not implemented): build under a temporary name and swap under the write lock, or take the lock for Build and Drop. This proves counter consistency only; it does not stop a delete issued during a Build from being lost ([bug-srch-016](#bug-srch-016)). Governing statements: [search.bm25.write_lock](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.bm25.write_lock), [search.bm25.counts](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.bm25.counts).

bugs_issues.title: A second or re-run BM25 upgrade rebuilds an index that is already upgraded, and searches answer nothing meanwhile
bugs_issues.body: ### A second or re-run BM25 upgrade rebuilds an index that is already upgraded, and searches answer nothing meanwhile Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: [witness_concurrent_upgrades and witness_crash_after_flip_rerun](results/search/20261114T000543Z-prove/receipt.json) in [search.rs](models/search/search.rs) (B-search O2/F4; repair `theorem_repaired_upgrade_preserves`, valid outcome `witness_repair_rerun_keeps_index`); A-search F4. Reproduced by: [search_bm25_upgrade_concurrent](receipts/native/search_bm25_upgrade_concurrent.json) — two `Upgrade` calls on a 6,000-document schema-1 index both ran (`upgraded: 1` each); 205 of 210 searches for a term present in every document answered nothing while they ran; the final index was consistent. The crash-after-flip re-run (W-O2b) was not probed. Expected: a search never observes an incomplete schema-2 index (spec 044 FR-023, SC-012). Observed: `Upgrade` tests `already` before it sets the flag and takes the lock (`BM25Index.cls:528-533`) and never re-checks under the lock, so a waiting second call, or a re-run after a death between the flip and the flag's clear, kills `df` and `doc` on a schema-2 index (`:542`). After such a death writers are refused with "is being upgraded" rather than told to re-run the upgrade (`:388-389`). Consequence: transient empty or partial search answers during a duplicate upgrade; a misleading refusal message after an interrupted one. Repair proposal (not implemented): re-read `schema` under the lock and skip the rebuild of a schema-2 index. Governing statement: [search.bm25.upgrade](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.bm25.upgrade).

bugs_issues.title: The engine's fusion gives a result missing from one leg a non-zero, length-dependent score
bugs_issues.body: ### The engine's fusion gives a result missing from one leg a non-zero, length-dependent score Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Derived from source arithmetic; no run compared the rankings. Severity is lowered one level from High. Found by: A-search F5 and S1 ([intent](../uplift/ivg-verus-initial/intent/search.md)). Reproduced by: none Expected: "each hit scores 1/(c+rank)" and "legs not yet searched contribute nothing" (engine docstring and API reference). Observed: the engine's RRF scores an absent item at a rank derived from the leg's length (`vector.py:1444-1446`), the SQL procedure uses 1e9 (`schema.py:2536-2537`), and `ivg.retrieve` and `fusion.py` use 0 (`translator.py:3342-3352`; `fusion.py:56-58`). Consequence: with c=60 and legs of 200, an item at vector rank 1 only (1/61 + 1/320 = 0.01952) outranks one at rank 50 in both legs (2/110 = 0.01818), the reverse of standard RRF; the four entry points rank the same inputs differently. Repair proposal (not implemented): [simp-srch-001](design_simplification.md#simp-srch-001). Open choice: [search.fusion.absent](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.fusion.absent). Governing statement: [search.fusion](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.fusion).

bugs_issues.title: The embedding queue checks identity against the wrong table, and its IRIS worker writes default-graph entries with no identity check
bugs_issues.body: ### The embedding queue checks identity against the wrong table, and its IRIS worker writes default-graph entries with no identity check Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** The native probe could not run on Community (no `%Embedding.Config` at the table's width); severity is lowered one level from High. Found by: [witness_queue_default_graph_misroutes and witness_queue_writes_into_claimed_table](results/search/20261114T000543Z-prove/receipt.json) in [search.rs](models/search/search.rs) (B-search O3/F8; control `queue-routes-default-graph`); A-search F8 and S4. Reproduced by: none yet — [search_queue_default_graph](receipts/native/search_queue_default_graph.json) is INCONCLUSIVE (no `%Embedding.Config` with VectorLength 768). Expected: 4.0.0 routing (one table per graph and model; "never derive a name to find a route"); `ClaimPendingBatch` carries `config` so the queue is not "the one write path that escapes the embedding identity registry" (`EmbedQueue.cls:108-111`). Observed: `enqueue_for_embedding` checks every request against `kg_NodeEmbeddings` of the default graph whatever its graph (`embeddings.py:1838-1842`), refusing a named-graph request that `store_embedding` would route — the check the Python worker's docstring calls the 3.2.0 error (`:1993-1998`). `EmbedQueue.ProcessBatch` sends every default-graph entry to `kg_NodeEmbeddings` whatever its `config`, with no check (`EmbedQueue.cls:278-283, 316`). Consequence: a model B vector can land in model A's table (read back as A's and compared with A's queries), and valid named-graph requests are refused. Repair proposal (not implemented): resolve default-graph entries through the registry like named ones (or refuse them unless the entry's model owns `kg_NodeEmbeddings`), and check the target route at enqueue. Governing statements: [search.embedding.queue](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.embedding.queue), [search.embedding.check_on_write](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.embedding.check_on_write).

bugs_issues.title: A failed vector leg makes the engine's fusion answer an empty list instead of an error
bugs_issues.body: ### A failed vector leg makes the engine's fusion answer an empty list instead of an error Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: A-search F5 (second part); the product's own [KNOWN_ISSUES](../../docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md) entry "`kg_RRF_FUSE` answers `[]` when an index search fails" (`docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md:171-178`, planned for 4.7.1). Reproduced by: none — the behavior is recorded by the product (KNOWN_ISSUES, measured during 4.7.0); not re-run here. Expected: a leg that fails is reported as a failure that names the leg, not read as an empty ranking. Observed: `kg_RRF_FUSE` runs the vector leg and then the BM25 leg inside one `try` and only logs a failure (`vector.py:1382` onward), so a failed vector leg answers `[]` and the BM25 leg never runs. `IRISGraphOperators.kg_RRF_FUSE` defaults `query_vector="[]"` (`operators.py:37`), which fails the vector leg on every text-only call against a declared-width table (`vector.py:487-502`). Consequence: text-only fusion through the operators answers "nothing matched". Repair proposal (not implemented): raise naming the failed leg (the planned 4.7.1 change), and skip the vector leg when no query vector is given. Governing statement: [search.fusion.failed_leg](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.fusion.failed_leg).

bugs_issues.title: Bolt sessions never close the IRIS connection their engine opened
bugs_issues.body: ### Bolt sessions never close the IRIS connection their engine opened Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Source reading only; whether garbage collection closes the connection was not observed. Severity is lowered one level from High (an outage of every IRIS client once a Community instance's connection licence is exhausted). Found by: A-platform F-H6 ([intent](../uplift/ivg-verus-initial/intent/platform.md)); re-read for this entry: `BoltSession._get_engine` (`bolt_server.py:391-393`) builds an engine through `cypher_api._make_engine` (`cypher_api.py:137, 157-170`), and the session's `finally` closes only the socket (`bolt_server.py:420-425, 954-960`). Reproduced by: none Expected: a server releases what each session acquired; the operator guide sizes Community deployments by connection count. Observed: each Bolt session (WebSocket or TCP) creates its own engine and IRIS connection on first use and never closes it. Consequence: a long-running Bolt listener can hold one IRIS connection per finished session; on Community the licence then refuses new connections for every client. Repair proposal (not implemented): close the session's engine connection in the session's `finally`, or share a pooled engine. No ontology statement covers server resource lifetime; nearest: [access.surfaces](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.surfaces).
bugs_issues.reproduced: none

bugs_issues.title: Two concurrent first setups can both record their IVG Schema, and the loser keeps writing to its own tables
bugs_issues.body: ### Two concurrent first setups can both record their IVG Schema, and the loser keeps writing to its own tables Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Proved on the model; not probed natively because it needs a throwaway namespace and a second schema. Severity is lowered one level from High. Found by: [witness_concurrent_first_setups_overwrite_the_record and witness_deploy_refusal_is_swallowed](results/platform/20261114T002651Z-prove/receipt.json) in [platform.rs](models/platform/platform.rs) (B-platform B1; `witness_reraise_alone_is_not_enough`, `witness_lock_refuses_the_second_setup`); A-platform F-S1; review R3-platform R1-4, now in the model as `witness_cas_alone_still_releases_the_second_engine`: a compare-and-set record write alone still lets the second setup release its engine and write. Reproduced by: none Expected: the first `initialize_schema()` records the name and any engine asking for another is refused (ADR-0016:11; spec 262 FR-005/FR-006); two schemas in one namespace would share one adjacency index and one ledger (ADR-0016:17). Observed: `_record_and_initialize` reads the record (`_engine/schema.py:2222`), runs a setup ADMIN_GUIDE:102-103 measures at 44-62 s, and writes the record unconditionally if it saw none (`:2309-2312`, `schema_name.py:194-198`), with no lock or compare-and-set. The deploy's own re-check raises `IVGSchemaError` but is caught as a best-effort deploy failure (`_engine/schema.py:2591-2594`). Each engine's guard is released once and never re-checked (`engine.py:1874-1885`). Consequence: the record names whichever setup wrote last, both engines are accepted, and both write the shared `^KG`, `^NKG` and `^IVG.*` from different tables. Repair proposal (not implemented): hold `LOCK +^IVG.Deploy("schema")` from the read to the record and re-read before writing; re-raising the deploy refusal alone, or a compare-and-set without a raise that keeps the engine refused, is not enough. The outcome is decided by FR-005, FR-006, SC-006 and ADR-0016 ("instead of sharing globals silently"). Governing statements: [install.schema.concurrency](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.schema.concurrency), [install.schema.record](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.schema.record).

bugs_issues.title: A merge restore keeps at most one row per graph in the core tables and reports every row restored
bugs_issues.body: ### A merge restore keeps at most one row per graph in the core tables and reports every row restored Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Depends on the live export column order; not run. Severity is lowered one level from High. Found by: A-platform F-B1 (sub-reader b, re-read by A-platform). Reproduced by: original two-edge/column-order scenario not rerun; iteration 5 real IRIS parent-key/vector consequence via [snapshot binding](models/snapshot_routes/binding.py) and its retained [receipts](results/snapshot_routes/). Expected: a merge restore adds the archive's rows that are not already present; the v4.1.0 CHANGELOG (3926-3932) names this dedupe defect and fixes it for the FHIR tables. Observed: the generic merge guard is `WHERE NOT EXISTS (… WHERE {cols[0]} = ?)` and the count is incremented regardless (`_engine/snapshot.py:1287-1298`); export drops `edge_id` (`snapshot.py:872-874`), so for `rdf_edges` (and `rdf_labels`, `rdf_props`, `docs`) the first column is `graph_id`. Consequence: saving two edges in G, erasing G and merge-restoring gives one edge, and the report says two were restored. Repair proposal (not implemented): dedupe on each table's key columns, and count only rows actually inserted. Governing statement: [install.snapshot](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.snapshot). Iteration 5: the first-column guard root is also F-1802, whose earlier live evidence is retained. A new native shared-ID/other-graph parent witness loses graph A's parent, so its routed vector fails FK and the final reader is empty; the original complete-archive prediction and DISAGREES receipt are preserved. The Verus restore_parent/load/read chain derives this consequence. This strengthens the inherited root, not a new discovery or a repair.
