bugs_issues.title: The sample API's Cypher endpoints run translated SQL on a raw cursor, bypassing strict mode and the engine's statement protocol
bugs_issues.body: ### The sample API's Cypher endpoints run translated SQL on a raw cursor, bypassing strict mode and the engine's statement protocol Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: `theorem_strict_paths` (path `ApiSampleCypher`) and `witness_undocumented_bypasses_break_the_contract` in [platform.rs](models/platform/platform.rs) ([prove receipt](results/platform/20261114T002651Z-prove/receipt.json); B-platform W2); A-platform F-H3; A-cypher F3 ([intent](../uplift/ivg-verus-initial/intent/cypher.md)); A-ops candidate finding; reconstruction check 2(a)13 and 2(b)16; review R3-platform R1-11 (an undocumented bypass that contradicts the spec 213 contract). Reproduced by: [platform_strict_api_sample](receipts/native/platform_strict_api_sample.json) — with the ledger enabled and strict, `POST /api/cypher` of `api.main` committed a `CREATE` (row present, HTTP 200) while the same query through the engine raised `LedgerStrictModeError` and wrote nothing. Expected: under strict mode `execute_cypher` with an updating clause is refused and changes nothing (spec 213 `contracts/ledger-api.md:82-92`); `read_only.py:3-7` lists these routes under the one write rule; each server call should do what an engine method does. Observed: `api/routers/cypher.py:130-166` and GraphQL `executeCypher` (`api/gql/schema.py:174-200`) execute `translate_to_sql(...).sql` statement by statement on a bare cursor, skipping `_ledger_check("cypher_dml")` (`_engine/query.py:2300`), `write_txn`, the statement protocol (`__capture_ids__`, `__pin_stage__`, `__GRAPH_*` and others, handled only in `iris_sql_store.py:1617-1777`), result decoding and the native path. The same app mounts example GraphQL mutations such as `updateProtein`, a raw `UPDATE rdf_props` with no graph scope or guard. Consequence: unrecorded structural writes under strict mode; Cypher `DELETE`, pinned `SET` and all-graphs writes in a multi-graph namespace cannot execute correctly on these routes. Repair proposal (not implemented): route both through `engine.execute_cypher(read_only=…)`, keeping the hop cap and error redaction. Related: [query.routes](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.routes). Governing statements: [access.ledger_strict.bypasses](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.ledger_strict.bypasses), [access.surfaces](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.surfaces).

bugs_issues.title: The migrations' schema-check waiver also releases the refusal of a mismatched schema
bugs_issues.body: ### The migrations' schema-check waiver also releases the refusal of a mismatched schema Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: `witness_waiver_releases_a_mismatch` (W-S2) in [platform.rs](models/platform/platform.rs) ([prove receipt](results/platform/20261114T002651Z-prove/receipt.json); control `s-waive-checks`); A-platform F-S2; review R3-platform R1-5 (the mismatch case is decided by FR-006, which has no exception; only the no-record case stays open). Reproduced by: [platform_schema_waiver](receipts/native/platform_schema_waiver.json) — in a namespace recorded `Graph_KG`, an engine on `IVGPROBE` was refused (control), but the migrations' waived engine on `IVGPROBE` was not: its dry runs went ahead (one failed only because `IVGPROBE.RDF_EDGES` does not exist). No table or routine was written. Expected: a mismatch is refused on first database access, before any write (spec 262 FR-006; ADR-0016:11); the waiver's recorded intent is only "may run before any 4.6.0 setup recorded the schema". Observed: `graph_scoped_embeddings.py:287-288` and `temporal_structural_rows.py:85-89` build `IRISGraphEngine(conn)` from `IVG_SCHEMA_PREFIX` or the default and call `_waive_schema_check()` → `_schema_check_passed()` (`engine.py:1875-1890`), which releases any pending refusal, a mismatch included. Consequence: where the other schema's tables exist (spec 262 FR-009's explicit two-schema case), `backfill_structural_rows` would write that schema's `rdf_edges` and the namespace's shared `^KG`, and the 4.0.0 embeddings and `^KG` steps, which address the default schema (`upgrade.py:145-152`), can rebuild the shared `^KG` from the other schema's rows. Repair proposal (not implemented): waive only when no record exists, or build the migration engine on the recorded schema. Related question: [q-plt-011](open_questions.md#q-plt-011). Governing statements: [install.migration.schema](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.migration.schema), [install.schema.refusal](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.schema.refusal).

bugs_issues.title: Neo4j-compatible transactions are not transactions: Bolt ROLLBACK keeps the writes and the HTTP transaction endpoint commits statement by statement
bugs_issues.body: ### Neo4j-compatible transactions are not transactions: Bolt ROLLBACK keeps the writes and the HTTP transaction endpoint commits statement by statement Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Source reading only; no driver session was run. Severity is lowered one level from High. Found by: A-platform F-H1 and F-H2; A-ops candidate finding and test gap (d) (no test references Bolt `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK`). Reproduced by: none Expected: a client that rolls back a transaction keeps none of its writes; a transaction batch is atomic (Neo4j semantics the surfaces imitate). No IVG document says otherwise. Observed: Bolt answers `BEGIN`, `COMMIT` and `ROLLBACK` with SUCCESS only and every `RUN` commits (`bolt_server.py:500-510`); `/db/neo4j/tx/commit` runs each statement as its own `_run_cypher` (`cypher_api.py:391-398`). Consequence: a driver's `tx.rollback()` reports success while the writes stay; a failing statement in an HTTP batch leaves the earlier ones committed. Repair proposal (not implemented): map an explicit transaction onto one IVG transaction, or refuse explicit transactions with an error and document per-statement commits. Open part: [access.transactions](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.transactions).
bugs_issues.reproduced: none

bugs_issues.body: ### The sample environment file sets IRIS_USER, but the server reads IRIS_USERNAME and silently connects as _SYSTEM Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Source reading only (re-read: `.env.sample:30`, `cypher_api.py:170`, `cli.py:47`). Reproduced by: none Expected: the operator guide tells operators to give the server a non-superuser login; the IRIS login is the real privilege boundary. Observed: `.env.sample:30` sets `IRIS_USER=_SYSTEM`, while `cypher_api._make_engine` and the CLI read `IRIS_USERNAME` with default `_SYSTEM` (`cypher_api.py:170`; `cli.py:47`). Consequence: an operator who follows the sample and changes `IRIS_USER` to a restricted login still runs the server as `_SYSTEM`, a `%All` superuser, with no warning. Repair proposal (not implemented): read one documented name (accept both with a warning), and fix the sample. Governing statements: [access.defaults](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.defaults), [access.iris_boundary](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.iris_boundary).

bugs_issues.title: The native interpreter tells used relationships apart by CRC-32, so a hash collision drops a legitimate match
bugs_issues.body: ### The native interpreter tells used relationships apart by CRC-32, so a hash collision drops a legitimate match Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Source reading only; severity is lowered one level from High. Found by: A-cypher F1. Reproduced by: none Expected: the compiled walk, the interpreter and the SQL path give the same answer (ADR-0014; spec 257 US1); the generated walk compares endpoints and key exactly (plan.md l. 24-26) and SQL compares `edge_id`. Observed: `Neighbours` keeps the edges a match has used as a comma string of `$ZCRC($ListBuild(src, p, dst, ekey), 7)` and skips an edge whose hash is already there (`Exec.cls:1243-1244`). Consequence: `MATCH (a:P)-[:K]->(b)-[:K]->(c) RETURN count(*)` over two edges whose tuples collide answers 0 in mode `off` and 1 in `sync` and SQL; node IDs are free text, so collisions can be constructed. Repair proposal (not implemented): key used edges by the full `$ListBuild`, or hold them in a local array subscripted by the tuple. Governing statement: [query.native.equal-answers](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.native.equal-answers).

bugs_issues.body: ### Text shortcuts meant for Neo4j Browser answer unrelated queries with canned rows Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Source reading only; severity is lowered one level from High. Found by: A-cypher F4. Reproduced by: none Expected: IVG answers the fixed Neo4j Browser metadata queries without running them and gives those answers to no other query. Observed: any non-write text whose upper-cased form contains `MATCH ()`, `COUNT(*)` and `UNION ALL` answers node and relationship counts over every graph; any text containing `RETURN DISTINCT`, `UNION ALL` and `ENTITY` answers 25 node IDs and 25 predicates (`query.py:1829-1856`, from `9c683292`, v1.47.0). The tests are substring tests over the whole text, string literals included, and ignore `USE GRAPH`; `read_only.answered_without_parsing` does not list them. Consequence: `MATCH (e:Entity) RETURN DISTINCT e.name AS x UNION ALL MATCH (e:Entity) RETURN DISTINCT e.kind AS x` (an ordinary GraphRAG query) answers canned rows. bugs_issues.title: An adopting verify that races a redaction can append the redacted tenant's IDs after the redaction finished
bugs_issues.body: ### An adopting verify that races a redaction can append the redacted tenant's IDs after the redaction finished Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Source reading only; the interleaving was not run. Severity is lowered one level from High. Found by: A-history F5 (third bullet) ([intent](../uplift/ivg-verus-initial/intent/ledger-history.md)); A-ops hazard (c)2; review R1-core CV-3 and R1-6. Reproduced by: none Expected: after a complete redaction no record reachable through IVG holds the target's IDs (ADR-0013; spec 256 FR-001); an adoption records the current differences. Observed: `verify(adopt=True)` checks the marker once, reads the divergence with no lock and commits the adoption without `expected_head` (`replay.py:806-858`). If it reads after the erase and before the redaction starts, and the redaction then runs to completion, the adoption is admitted (the marker is gone) and writes `delete_*` records naming the tenant's IDs after the redaction revision; `enable()` runs this adoption. Consequence: tenant IDs re-enter the history after a redaction reported complete; a re-run of the redaction removes them, but nothing tells the operator to re-run. Repair proposal (not implemented): commit the adoption with the head it read (`expected_head`) so a moved head refuses it, or refuse adoption of records that match a completed redaction's target. Governing statements: [ledger.verify](../ontology/features/ledger.g5.md#ledger.verify), [redaction.purpose](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.purpose).

bugs_issues.title: A replayed commit applies its post-commit properties again over newer values and returns no statement IDs
bugs_issues.body: ### A replayed commit applies its post-commit properties again over newer values and returns no statement IDs Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Source reading only; no retry after a later write was run. Severity is lowered one level from High. Found by: A-history F13 ([intent](../uplift/ivg-verus-initial/intent/ledger-history.md)); reconstruction check 2(a)11; review R1-core CV-6 and R1-6. Reproduced by: none Expected: a retry with a bound idempotency key returns the original outcome with `replayed=True` and changes nothing (spec 213 `contracts/ledger-api.md:26`), including the `stmt_ids` the result carries (`:64`). Observed: a replay returns `stmt_ids` as `{}` (`Ledger.cls:461`); `post_commit_properties` are excluded from the fingerprint and applied again on a replay (`changeset.py:365-386`; `client.py:431-436`). Consequence: a client that retries after a timeout overwrites property values written since the original commit with its stale ones, an unrecorded write that verify then reports ([q-010](open_questions.md#q-010)); a retrying caller cannot learn the statement IDs of its own revision. Repair proposal (not implemented): on a replay, skip the post-commit properties (or apply them only if unchanged since the original revision) and return the original `stmt_ids`. Governing statement: [ledger.idempotency](../ontology/features/ledger.g5.md#ledger.idempotency).

bugs_issues.title: A BM25 delete issued while a Build runs is lost, and bug-srch-003's proposed repair does not prevent it
bugs_issues.body: ### A BM25 delete issued while a Build runs is lost, and bug-srch-003's proposed repair does not prevent it Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: review round2-domains R2-1; the search model's as-built lost-delete witness and the witness that the round-1 repair (lock Build and Drop) still loses it, with the extended repair proved by `theorem_repair_delete_takes_effect` ([prove receipt](results/search/20261114T035601Z-prove/receipt.json); controls `repair-delete-checks-n-first`, `as-built-delete-without-early-return`). Reproduced by: [search_bm25_delete_during_build](receipts/native/search_bm25_delete_during_build.json) — while a rebuild of a 4,000-document index ran (0.71 s), two node deletes with their `bm25_delete` landed inside the window; both deletes answered False and both documents are still returned by a search after the rebuild. Expected: a committed delete takes effect; every index write runs under the index's lock in a transaction (ADR-0007). Observed: `Delete` returns 0 before it takes the lock when `cfg N` is absent (`BM25Index.cls:496-499`), and `Build` sets N only after its scan (`:160`); a `bm25_delete` during a Build therefore answers False ("not in the index"), and if the Build's scan already flushed that document, the Build publishes it. Consequence: a document the caller deleted stays searchable after the Build. Repair proposal (not implemented): both changes are required together: run Build and Drop under the index lock ([bug-srch-003](#bug-srch-003)'s repair) **and** test N under that lock in Delete (and Insert). Either alone still loses the delete: `witness_round1_repair_loses_delete` (locked Build, as-built Delete) and the round-3 scratch witness `r3_witness_delete_lock_only_still_loses_delete` (locked Delete, unlocked Build; review round 3 R3-7). The combination is proved by `theorem_repair_delete_takes_effect` under variant `locked_build()` ([search.rs](models/search/search.rs)). Alternatively, a build-and-swap that replays the deletes it overlapped. Governing statements: [search.bm25.write_lock](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.bm25.write_lock), [search.bm25.incremental](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.bm25.incremental).

bugs_issues.body: ### The bulk loader writes duplicate node, label, property and edge keys: an id twice in one batch, a load with skip_existing=False, or two loaders at once Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Playbook uplift and completion audit, 2026-11-13/14 (imported 2026-11-14) Found by: playbook arm, [zz-structural.json](../../experiment/playbook-completion/findings/audit/zz-structural.json) (live `st-live-keys`; inspected `iris_vector_graph/bulk_loader.py:290-334`; inspected `iris_vector_graph/bulk_loader.py:420-440`) Reproduced by: playbook arm, live on its IRIS (x86_64 VM): `st-live-keys` - Expected: Graph_KG.nodes is keyed by (node_id, graph_id), rdf_labels by (graph_id, s, label), rdf_props by (graph_id, s, key) and rdf_edges by (s, p, o_id, graph_id, ekey) (iris_vector_graph/schema.py:35-44, 396-419). bugs_issues.title: A PPR limit above the native cap can turn truncated positive scores into zero
bugs_issues.body: ### A PPR limit above the native cap can turn truncated positive scores into zero Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Consolidated iteration10, 2026-11-15 Found by: iteration9 frozen producer/final-reader panel, PPR builder's source cap/limit trace, [four actual native/DB cases](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-10/root-ppr-cap-native.json), [provenance](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-10/root-ppr-cap-provenance.json) and [independent intent/dedup review](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-10/root-ppr-review-cap.md). Reproduced by: `root-ppr-cap-native.py` on the identity-guarded task-owned IRIS: ordinary successful1002-node bulk write without index disable/rebuild; actual public native/store PPR entry and actual private Python fallback using the same real DB. No external service/security scenario or physical unavailable-provider dispatch reproduction. Expected: [algorithms.op.ppr.completion](../ontology/features/algorithms.g5.md#algorithms.op.ppr.completion), the documented PPR recurrence and return_top_k contract. Every valid isolated seed in a uniform seed set has positive1/N after one iteration: its dangling mass restarts uniformly. A row limit may omit nodes, but a completed answer must not label an omitted positive score as unreachable0. Observed: with1002 isolated persisted valid seeds, damping1/2, one iteration/tolerance0, exclude_predicates=None and return_top_k1002, the actual public method returns1002 rows:1000positive scores near1/1002 and two fabricatedzeros. With an explicit empty exclusion list and the same limit, all1002 scores are positive; public limit1000 retains1000positive rows; the actual fallback at1002 gives all1002positive. All four source-derived predictions agree. Samples and zero IDs are retained in the native receipt; arithmetic comparisons allow1e-12 rounding. Cause: kg_PERSONALIZED_PAGERANK sends the requested row limit to the store/native Owner only when exclude_predicates is notNone. The native producer otherwise retains its1000 cap (also when a custom tolerance is sent). _ppr_every_node then prefers the larger positive caller top_k over the producer cap and treats absent scored nodes as0. The inference is invalid when that absence was caused by truncation. The class fast-path is analogous by source inspection, not an additional native route reproduction. Consequence: a completed PPR result reports genuinely scored/reachable seeds as0, and the numerical answer changes when an empty exclusion list is supplied. This is distinct from F-1003's global PageRank10000 row omission, F-1004/bug-plt-017's node-token cache issue, and bug-plt-103's tiny-positive ordering policy. Intentional cap1000 mass below1 is not itself the finding; fabrication inside a1002-row answer is. Repair proposal (not implemented): propagate the actual requested producer limit independently of exclusions, or carry enough completeness information to prevent zero-filling a truncated score set. Preserve intentionally capped answers and the None/[] compatibility behavior explicitly. No repair or simplification is approved here. Formal corroboration: [ppr_walk](models/ppr_walk/NOTES.md) `theorem_public_default_cap_gap_from_raw_seeds` starts from arbitrary distinct isolated valid raw seeds N>1000, derives their positive one-step scores, the actual public default1000 cap and a missing ID emitted as0. The three-node/cap2 structural witness is not the only closure of actual1000. Native floating/database/cache correspondence remains separately qualified.

bugs_issues.title: A leading grouped OPTIONAL MATCH with no matches returns NULL for SUM instead of zero
bugs_issues.body: ### A leading grouped OPTIONAL MATCH with no matches returns NULL for SUM instead of zero Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Ordinary consolidated iteration13, 2026-11-15 Found by: the fresh aggregate source survey, actual local SQL caller contrasts, [prospective native neighbors](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-13/root-optional-aggregate-PAIRS.md), [four actual native caller observations](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-13/root-optional-aggregate-native.json), and [independent29-check fact audit](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-13/review-optional-aggregate-audit.json) with [authority/dedup triage](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-13/review-optional-aggregate-triage.md). This is a source-informed ordinary discovery, not private evaluation or an assessment of interrupted work. Reproduced by: actual pinned SQL-path execute_cypher on the task-owned IRIS, using only a fresh graph, one new anchor and a never-created unique label. No namespace census, unrelated data, supplied result rows, injected provider error or product patch. Expected: [query.aggregation](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.aggregation). The newer [R308 regression](../../tests/unit/test_460_r308_guards.py#L53) explicitly says openCypher SUM over no values is0 and requires zero for an all-null group. A synthetic optional row contributes to COUNT(*) but supplies no value to SUM. Observed: leading `OPTIONAL MATCH (n:Missing) RETURN n.kind, count(*), count(n), sum(n.x), avg(n.x), collect(n.x)` in the fresh graph returns `[null,1,0,null,null,[]]`. The sum should be0. Ordinary empty global MATCH returns `[0,0,0,null,[]]`, leading global OPTIONAL returns `[1,0,0,null,[]]`, and an anchored missing OPTIONAL returns `[1,0,0,null,[]]`. All four source forecasts agree with the actual calls; only the grouped fallback differs from the prospectively recorded zero-sum reference. The fixture and anchor readback are retained in the raw receipt. Cause and authority: `_null_row_aggregate` supplies SQL NULL for SUM, and a leading grouped OPTIONAL materializes that value in its synthetic UNION fallback rather than passing through the ordinary SUM zero-if-null expression. The older [R298 helper unit](../../tests/unit/test_460_r298_fixes46_leftovers.py#L28) explicitly tests that NULL as built. Root preserves this source tension and follows the newer, explicit all-null-group SUM requirement; the helper test does not justify different public SUM results by query shape. F-0823 concerns a different empty CALL result with max/avg/collect, not this grouped OPTIONAL SUM root. Consequence: an ordinary report can receive a missing metric instead of a numeric zero when it adds a grouping key to an unmatched OPTIONAL query. Low reflects this narrow read-result consequence; no data loss or wider aggregation failure is claimed. Repair proposal (not implemented): return a numeric zero for SUM in the synthetic no-value fallback and preserve its final type, while retaining COUNT(*)1, COUNT(value)0, AVG null and COLLECT[]. Keep ordinary/global/grouped/anchored neighbors separate. The ordinary aggregate model's SQL-fold domain remains qualified; this OPTIONAL caller boundary is observed and still partial in Verus, not a new active source binding or executable-body proof. No product repair or owner decision is recorded.

bugs_issues.title: Concurrent writers of one multigraph triple can lose its multiplicity or leave a ghost edge entry
bugs_issues.body: ### Concurrent writers of one multigraph triple can lose its multiplicity or leave a ghost edge entry Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Source reading only; concurrent keyed writers are not represented in the model and were not run. Severity is lowered one level from Medium. Found by: A-structure F4 and S6 ([intent](../uplift/ivg-verus-initial/intent/graph-structure.md)). Reproduced by: none Expected: a triple's adjacency is a leaf, plus one child per edge and `#` while two or more edges share it, and holds no entry without a row (spec 234 FR-004/FR-006; spec 252 FR-003). Observed: `PutKeyed` tests `'$Data(leaf)` and calls `Put` with no mutual exclusion (`Adjacency.cls:220-223`); writers hold shared locks only. Two first puts of one triple (two `%BuildIndices` jobs, `TraversalBuild.cls:131-133`, or two transactions) both take the `Put` branch; a writer that builds children from another's uncommitted leaf keeps them after that one rolls back; two `RemoveKeyed` of a two-edge triple can both pass their guards and leave a leaf with no rows. The comment at `Adjacency.cls:227-230` covers only an existing leaf. Consequence: wrong degree and traversal multiplicity, or an edge entry with no row, until a rebuild. Repair proposal (not implemented): serialize keyed transitions per triple with an exclusive lock on `^IVG.AdjT(g,s,p,o)` held to commit (mode-off writers never take it), or derive children and `#` from committed rows at rebuild. Governing statement: [structure.multigraph.layout](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.multigraph.layout).
bugs_issues.reproduced: none

bugs_issues.title: Restoring a multigraph archive into an indexed namespace loses its parallel edges' multiplicity
bugs_issues.body: ### Restoring a multigraph archive into an indexed namespace loses its parallel edges' multiplicity Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Source reading only; severity is lowered one level from Medium. Found by: A-structure F5; A-platform F-B2. Reproduced by: none Expected: the multigraph mode is part of the snapshot so a restored multigraph keeps its parallel edges (spec 234 FR-001; `snapshot.py:157-160` comment). Spec 234 lists restore (US4) as not done but specifies no refusal. Observed: the replacing restore runs `erase_all`, which clears the modes, then inserts rows (`snapshot.py:1234-1300`); `RowPut` sees mode off and writes single-edge leaves; `^IVG.GraphMode` arrives later with the globals (`:1554-1590`) and the keyed `out`/`in` lines are skipped as index-derived (`:1659-1665`); no rebuild follows. Consequence: after a restore, parallel triples have degree 1 and one-hop Cypher answers once, until `sync()`. Repair proposal (not implemented): restore `^IVG.GraphMode` before the rows, or rebuild the adjacency of multigraph graphs after the restore. Governing statement: [structure.multigraph.restore](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.multigraph.restore).

Found by: A-structure F6 and Q6. Reproduced by: none Expected: with multigraph mode off there is one row per triple (spec 234 FR-003); switching off is refused while a triple has two rows. Observed: `u_spo_graph_ekey` admits `ekey<>0` rows in a mode-off graph (`schema.py:44`). `GraphMode.Set(off)` counts and then kills with no lock (`GraphMode.cls:35-40`); another engine's cached "on" (`admin.py:922-926`; `translator.py:441-457`) keeps emitting the `MAX(ekey)+1` insert (`translator.py:10368-10386`); a restore can do the same ([bug-str-007](#bug-str-007)). Consequence: deleting either of the two rows kills the shared leaf (`RowRemove` → `Remove`), leaving the other row without adjacency. Repair proposal (not implemented): re-read the mode per statement, or have the functional index refuse an `ekey<>0` row in a mode-off graph, and lock the mode switch against writers. Governing statements: [structure.multigraph.off](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.multigraph.off), [structure.multigraph.switch](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.multigraph.switch).

bugs_issues.title: A failed indexed rebuild, or a failed rebuild after a bulk load, leaves a partial adjacency index
bugs_issues.body: ### A failed indexed rebuild, or a failed rebuild after a bulk load, leaves a partial adjacency index Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Source reading only; severity is lowered one level from Medium. Found by: A-structure F8; reconstruction check 2(a)6, 2(a)11 and gap G39 ([reconstruction check](../uplift/ivg-verus-initial/reconstruction-check.md)). Reproduced by: none Expected: a failed rebuild "leaves the previous adjacency intact" (spec 248 spec.md:74-75; `BuildKG` comment `TraversalBuild.cls:46-58`); a bulk load de-duplicates and rebuilds whether it succeeds or fails (spec 252 FR-008). Observed: the indexed path runs `%BuildIndices` after `TCommit`, and `PurgeIndex` is `RemoveAll` (`TraversalBuild.cls:124-136`; `AdjIndex.cls:29-32`), so the promise holds only for the non-indexed path (the catch does bump the token, `:164-170`); `BuildKG` commits every 50k rows; the `rebuild_edge_indices` procedure empties the whole index outside a transaction; a failed `_rebuild_after_load` is only logged. Consequence: readers see a partial or empty adjacency after a failed rebuild, and a failed post-load rebuild goes unnoticed. Repair proposal (not implemented): build into a staging tree and swap, or report the failure and keep `^IVG.AdjNoLock`-style degradation visible; raise from `_rebuild_after_load`. Open part: [structure.rebuild.failure](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.rebuild.failure). Governing statements: [structure.rebuild](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.rebuild), [structure.adjacency.bulk](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.adjacency.bulk).

bugs_issues.title: Node interning runs inside the functional-index callback, which ADR-0008 rules out
bugs_issues.body: ### Node interning runs inside the functional-index callback, which ADR-0008 rules out Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Source reading only; the impact depends on `^NKG` readers that were not traced. Severity is lowered one level from Medium. Found by: A-structure F9. Reproduced by: none Expected: interning "cannot" live in the index, because a rollback leaves nameless IDs and the locks deadlock under overlapping writers (ADR-0008:66-67). Observed: `RowPut` → `Put` interns when `^NKG` is built (`Adjacency.cls:95-107`); inside a transaction `InternNode`'s lock is held to commit, and after a 5 s wait it returns another transaction's possibly uncommitted index or `""` (`GraphIndex.cls:49-54`); `$Increment(^NKG(-3,s))` and `edgeCount` survive a rollback. Consequence: 5 s stalls under overlapping writers and interned IDs or counters that disagree with committed rows until the next build sweep (`TraversalBuild.cls:478-479`). Repair proposal (not implemented): move interning out of the callback (intern on read or at rebuild), as ADR-0008 decided, or amend the ADR with the accepted residue. Governing statement: [structure.adjacency.declared](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.adjacency.declared).

bugs_issues.title: A ledger qualifier update reweights a multigraph triple's leaf to an edge that is not the lowest
bugs_issues.body: ### A ledger qualifier update reweights a multigraph triple's leaf to an edge that is not the lowest Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Source reading only; severity is lowered one level from Medium. Found by: A-structure F11. Reproduced by: none Expected: the leaf carries the weight of the lowest live `ekey` (spec 234 FR-004). Observed: `LedgerApply.PersistQuals` calls `Reweight`, which sets the leaf unconditionally (`LedgerApply.cls:561-563`; `Adjacency.cls:334-339`); in an indexed namespace the call also duplicates the index's `RowUpdate`. Consequence: weighted algorithms and traversals read the updated edge's weight for the whole triple. bugs_issues.title: A write inside CALL { } is refused with a raw SQL syntax error instead of a clear refusal
bugs_issues.body: ### A write inside CALL { } is refused with a raw SQL syntax error instead of a clear refusal Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: reconstruction check 2(a)15 and correction 22 (the subquery translation handles only `MATCH`/`WHERE`/`UNWIND`, `translator.py:14635-14663`); review R3-platform R1-10. Reproduced by: [cypher_subquery_write](receipts/native/cypher_subquery_write.json) — `CALL { CREATE (n:SubqProbe {id: 'subq|1'}) } RETURN 1 AS one` returned a result whose `error` field holds SQLCODE -12 ("A term expected…"), raised nothing and wrote nothing; a plain `CREATE` wrote its node. This meets "carried out or refused" (verdict OBSERVED_AS_EXPECTED for that intent); the defect is the form of the refusal. Expected: a write clause inside a `CALL { }` body is carried out, or the whole query is refused; it is never skipped silently. Observed: the subquery translator does not classify `CALL { CREATE … }` as a write and emits SQL that IRIS cannot parse; the error surfaces only as an internal SQL message in the result object, with no raise, no `GraphWriteError` and no strict-mode refusal. A silent drop when `RETURN` reads only matched variables remains unobserved. Consequence: callers cannot tell an unsupported construct from a server fault; the limitation is not listed among the documented deviations. Repair proposal (not implemented): refuse a write inside `CALL { }` at translation with a named error, and list it in the conformance deviations. Governing statements: [query.writes.subquery](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.writes.subquery), [query.conformance](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.conformance).
bugs_issues.reproduced: [cypher_subquery_write](receipts/native/cypher_subquery_write.json) — `CALL { CREATE (n:SubqProbe {id: 'subq|1'}) } RETURN 1 AS one` returned a result whose `error` field holds SQLCODE -12 ("A term expected…"), raised nothing and wrote nothing; a plain `CREATE` wrote its node. This meets "carried out or refused" (verdict OBSERVED_AS_EXPECTED for that intent); the defect is the form of the refusal.

bugs_issues.title: An all-graphs read skips graph correlation when only the nodes table looks single-graph
bugs_issues.body: ### An all-graphs read skips graph correlation when only the nodes table looks single-graph Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Data-dependent; source reading only. Severity is lowered one level from Medium. Found by: A-cypher F6. Reproduced by: none Expected: an all-graphs read pairs each node only with its own graph's rows. Observed: `_all_graphs_correlated` asks `_more_than_one_graph`, which reads only `nodes` (`engine.py:612-639`; `translator.py:782-794`); `rdf_props` has no foreign key to `nodes` (`schema.py:411-418`), and 4.7.0 states that property rows left by SQL-removed nodes exist (CHANGELOG l. 54-58). Consequence: with nodes in one graph and leftover property rows of the same ID in another, the SQL path reads the other graph's value; the native path does not, so shadow mode raises or the answers differ. Repair proposal (not implemented): probe `rdf_props` too, or correlate whenever any graph-owned table holds two graphs. Governing statement: [query.graph-scope.read](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.graph-scope.read).

bugs_issues.title: USE GRAPH accepts graph names the graph keys refuse
bugs_issues.body: ### USE GRAPH accepts graph names the graph keys refuse Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Source reading only; severity is lowered one level from Medium. Found by: A-cypher F8. Reproduced by: none Expected: the reserved name `"0"` and control characters are refused before anything is written (ADR-0003). Observed: `parser.py:174-192` accepts any string; refusal happens only where `ForIndex` runs, so a label-less `USE GRAPH '0' CREATE ({id:'a'})` writes a `nodes` row in graph `'0'` that `^KG` cannot represent, and native reads throw and fall back to SQL. Consequence: rows in an unrepresentable graph, which every later functional-index callback for that graph rejects. Repair proposal (not implemented): call `validate_graph_name` on the graph context at parse or translate. Governing statement: [query.graph-scope.names](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.graph-scope.names).

bugs_issues.title: A run that started before a property-layout change can recompile a shape's class for the old layout under newer runs
bugs_issues.body: ### A run that started before a property-layout change can recompile a shape's class for the old layout under newer runs Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Proved on the model; needs a layout recompile inside one run's window, not probed. Found by: [witness_straggler_recompiles_for_an_old_layout](results/platform/20261114T002651Z-prove/receipt.json) in [platform.rs](models/platform/platform.rs) (B-platform P2, W-O2c). Reproduced by: none Expected: a stale entry is never run (ADR-0014:16-23). Observed: the check is made once per run (`Exec.cls:158`); a run whose `Props.Begin` preceded an `rdf_props` recompile reaches `For` after a newer run compiled the shape, rewrites the entry and recompiles the same class for the old layout (`Gen.cls:63-101`). Consequence: the newer run's next walk reads old global names; only in-flight runs are affected and the entry heals on the next check. Repair proposal (not implemented): [simp-cyp-001](design_simplification.md#simp-cyp-001). bugs_issues.title: A ledger commit into a graph during its erase can lose the new relationship's statement entry
bugs_issues.body: ### A ledger commit into a graph during its erase can lose the new relationship's statement entry Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Source reading only; not run. Severity is lowered one level from Medium. Found by: A-history F4 scenario 2 ([intent](../uplift/ivg-verus-initial/intent/ledger-history.md)). Reproduced by: none Expected: every live relationship committed through the ledger has its statement entry (the statement index addresses it). Observed: the Eraser takes no ledger head lock; a ledger commit can insert a relationship (and its endpoints) after the erase's `DELETE rdf_edges` and before `EraseLedgerFor`, which then kills every statement entry of the graph (`Eraser.cls:1107-1143`). Consequence: the new relationship stays live with no statement, so later ledger operations by statement and redaction attribution cannot reach it. Repair proposal (not implemented): see [q-004](open_questions.md#q-004) (serialise erase with commits, for example by taking the head lock in the Eraser while the ledger is enabled). Open part: [erasure.concurrency](../ontology/features/erasure.g5.md#erasure.concurrency).

bugs_issues.title: Re-enabling the ledger during an unfinished redaction skips the adoption without telling the caller
bugs_issues.body: ### Re-enabling the ledger during an unfinished redaction skips the adoption without telling the caller Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Source reading only; severity is lowered one level from Medium. Found by: A-history F14; review R1-core CV-6 and R1-6. Reproduced by: none Expected: enabling adopts the current state, so that writes made while the ledger was disabled are recorded and verify is equal. Observed: `enable()` runs `verify(adopt=True)` (`client.py:288-296`), which answers `redaction_in_progress` while the marker exists and adopts nothing (`replay.py:812-823`); `enable()` neither raises nor reports it. Consequence: the ledger is enabled with unrecorded writes; a later verify diverges with no hint that the adoption was skipped. Repair proposal (not implemented): refuse `enable` while a redaction is unfinished, or report the skipped adoption. Related question: [q-led-003](open_questions.md#q-led-003). Governing statement: [ledger.lifecycle](../ontology/features/ledger.g5.md#ledger.lifecycle).

bugs_issues.title: A reifier's delete record written inside a tenant's revision is reached by neither redaction target
bugs_issues.body: ### A reifier's delete record written inside a tenant's revision is reached by neither redaction target Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Source reading only; nothing tests it. Severity is lowered one level from Medium. Found by: review R1-core CV-4 and R1-11. Reproduced by: none Expected: every record of the target becomes a tombstone (ADR-0013; spec 256 FR-001). Observed: `DeleteRelInternal` writes a `delete_node` record (graph `""`, the reifier's own ID, prior = its label and property snapshot) for each reifier of a deleted edge; `Matches` reaches it only through a prefix the reifier ID carries, so neither `redact(tenantGraph)` nor `redact(None, prefix=tenant)` tombstones it unless the reifier ID has the tenant prefix. Consequence: the reifier's labels and properties from the tenant's own revision stay in clear after a complete redaction. Repair proposal (not implemented): attribute a cascade record to the relationship that caused it (for example by recording the edge's endpoints in it, as [simp-002](design_simplification.md#simp-002) proposes for qualifier records), or name reifier IDs with the tenant prefix. Governing statement: [redaction.target.nodes](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.target.nodes).

bugs_issues.title: A redaction that finds nothing to tombstone sets no marker, so a target record committed meanwhile survives a complete run
bugs_issues.body: ### A redaction that finds nothing to tombstone sets no marker, so a target record committed meanwhile survives a complete run Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Shown by a reviewer's scratch model witness; not probed. One `create_temporal_edge` of a temporal-only predicate into the target suffices, because it writes no row that the final step's liveness check reads (review round2-core); otherwise the trace needs a create and a delete of target content inside the run's window. Found by: review R1-core CV-2 and R1-9 (scratch witness `rv_witness_unstarted_run_completes_with_target_record`, `$RUN_DIR/agents/R1-core/adv_valid/verus.log`); `theorem_completion` holds only for started runs ([receipt](results/ledger_redaction/20261114T044401Z-prove/receipt.json)). Reproduced by: none Expected: while a redaction runs, nothing may be written into its target, and a complete run leaves no target record (spec 256 Decision 3; ADR-0013). Observed: `BatchInLock` writes the marker only at the first match (`LedgerRedact.cls:322-324`), and `FinalInLock` returns without a revision when there is no marker and no statement; `BlocksCommit` refuses only while a marker exists. Consequence: a target commit that lands after the scan has passed its position is admitted and survives a run that reports `complete`. Repair proposal (not implemented): claim the marker at the start of the first batch ([simp-001](design_simplification.md#simp-001)). Governing statement: [redaction.batches.commits](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.batches.commits).
bugs_issues.reproduced: none

bugs_issues.title: Under strict mode the only API delete is a ledger changeset, which leaves documents, temporal, FHIR and search-index content that redaction and verify cannot see
bugs_issues.body: ### Under strict mode the only API delete is a ledger changeset, which leaves documents, temporal, FHIR and search-index content that redaction and verify cannot see Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Source reading only; not probed. Severity is lowered one level from Medium. Found by: review round2-core R2-3 (expectation E10). Reproduced by: none Expected: an erase removes content from every store that holds it, and a path that removes content from one store but not the others is a defect (ADR-0004:71-82); a redaction is refused while the target's content is live. Observed: under strict mode `erase_graph`, `erase_all` and `delete_nodes_by_prefix` raise `LedgerStrictModeError` ([platform_strict_paths](receipts/native/platform_strict_paths.json)), so the only API deletion is a ledger `delete_node`/`delete_relationship`. `LedgerApply.DeleteNodeRows` (`LedgerApply.cls:353-372`) deletes `kg_NodeEmbeddings(_optimized)`, `rdf_labels`, `rdf_props` and `nodes` only; it leaves `Graph_KG.docs` (no foreign key, `schema.py:471-479`), the temporal index, the FHIR side tables, routed node vectors and the named search indexes (a routed table's foreign key may instead refuse the whole changeset). `LiveRows` and verify read none of these stores. Consequence: "delete through the ledger, then redact" completes with `verify()` equal while the tenant's text, vectors and events remain. Repair proposal (not implemented): route the ledger's node delete through the Eraser's node erase ([simp-str-001](design_simplification.md#simp-str-001)'s single path), or let erasure run under strict mode as a recorded operation; see [q-003](open_questions.md#q-003). Open part: [redaction.strict-mode](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.strict-mode). Governing statements: [erasure.entry-points.single-path](../ontology/features/erasure.g5.md#erasure.entry-points.single-path), [redaction.after-erasure](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.after-erasure).

bugs_issues.title: Post-commit properties bypass strict mode and the block on commits into a target being redacted
bugs_issues.body: ### Post-commit properties bypass strict mode and the block on commits into a target being redacted Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Source reading only; the strict-mode and mid-redaction cases were not run. Found by: review round2-core R2-4 (expectation E11). Reproduced by: none — [ledger_post_commit_verify](receipts/native/ledger_post_commit_verify.json) shows only that post-commit properties are written outside the revision (verify diverges). Expected: strict mode refuses writes made outside the ledger; while a redaction runs, a commit with a record in its target is refused (spec 256 Decision 3). Observed: `ledger.commit` writes `post_commit_properties` by direct SQL after the revision (`client.py:430-487`); the strict guard is not consulted for them and `BlocksCommit` checks only the changeset's records. Consequence: a commit whose post-commit properties name `tenant|…` makes a default-graph prefix target live in the middle of a run (the final step then refuses and the marker stays; for a prefix target an erase by prefix cannot clear such a property row, because the prefix erase selects IDs from node rows ([bug-led-010](#bug-led-010)), so only an explicit-id erase or raw SQL clears it, and until then the namespace-wide marker blocks readers, verify and every other target), and after a completed redaction it re-creates erased IDs as property rows. Repair proposal (not implemented): check post-commit properties against strict mode and the redaction marker before writing them, or record them in the revision. Related: [q-010](open_questions.md#q-010), [bug-led-003](#bug-led-003). Governing statements: [ledger.unrecorded](../ontology/features/ledger.g5.md#ledger.unrecorded), [redaction.batches.commits](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.batches.commits).
bugs_issues.reproduced: none — [ledger_post_commit_verify](receipts/native/ledger_post_commit_verify.json) shows only that post-commit properties are written outside the revision (verify diverges).

bugs_issues.title: A property row with no node row survives the prefix erase, and every later prefix redaction of its tenant is refused
bugs_issues.body: ### A property row with no node row survives the prefix erase, and every later prefix redaction of its tenant is refused Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: review round 3 R3-4 (scratch model L-d); integrated as witness W6 [witness_orphan_prop_row_blocks_prefix_redaction](results/ledger_redaction/20261114T044401Z-prove/receipt.json) in [redaction.rs](models/ledger_redaction/redaction.rs) (a `PropRow` goes with a prefix erase only when its node row exists in the same graph), with control [prefix-erase-takes-orphan-props](results/ledger_redaction/20261114T044600Z-control-prefix-erase-takes-orphan-props/receipt.json) (EXPECTED_FAIL). Reproduced by: [redaction_orphan_prop_blocks](receipts/native/redaction_orphan_prop_blocks.json) — a commit with `post_commit_properties = {"tP|x": {...}}` (the node `tP|x` is never created) leaves 1 property row and 0 node rows; after `delete_nodes_by_prefix("tP|")` the row is still there and `redact(None, prefix="tP")` is refused `RedactionTargetLiveError`; a second prefix erase changes nothing and the redaction is refused again; `delete_node("tP|x", graph="")` removes the row and the redaction then completes. Expected: an erase removes the tenant's content from every store that holds it (ADR-0004; CONTEXT.md "Erasure"), and the documented tenant recipe — erase by prefix, then redact by prefix (ADR-0013; USER_GUIDE) — completes. Observed: `Graph_KG.rdf_props` has no foreign key to `Graph_KG.nodes` (`schema.py:411-418`), and `ledger.commit` inserts post-commit property rows for any ID (`client.py:466-473`); `Eraser.EraseNodes` collects the IDs to erase from `Graph_KG.nodes` rows only (`Eraser.cls:331-349`), while `LedgerRedact.LiveRows` counts `rdf_props` rows by prefix. Consequence: a loud refusal, not silent retention: the tenant cannot be redacted through the documented recipe until an administrator finds the orphan IDs and erases them by ID. If the orphan row is written while a redaction runs ([bug-led-009](#bug-led-009)), the run's final step refuses and its marker blocks the namespace's readers, verify and other targets until then. Severity Low because the refusal is visible and an explicit-id erase repairs it. Repair proposal (not implemented): let the prefix erase also select property (and label) rows by ID prefix, or refuse `post_commit_properties` for IDs with no node row; the first keeps the recipe working for data written before the change. Related: [bug-led-007](#bug-led-007) (the same node-row selection misses temporal-only events), [simp-003](design_simplification.md#simp-003). Governing statements: [erasure.prefix-match](../ontology/features/erasure.g5.md#erasure.prefix-match), [redaction.after-erasure](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.after-erasure).
bugs_issues.reproduced: [redaction_orphan_prop_blocks](receipts/native/redaction_orphan_prop_blocks.json) — a commit with `post_commit_properties = {"tP|x": {...}}` (the node `tP|x` is never created) leaves 1 property row and 0 node rows; after `delete_nodes_by_prefix("tP|")` the row is still there and `redact(None, prefix="tP")` is refused `RedactionTargetLiveError`; a second prefix erase changes nothing and the redaction is refused again; `delete_node("tP|x", graph="")` removes the row and the redaction then completes.

bugs_issues.title: Without the adjacency index, a temporal write to an existing triple changes its stored weight without moving the version token
bugs_issues.body: ### Without the adjacency index, a temporal write to an existing triple changes its stored weight without moving the version token Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Code reading only; non-indexed installs only; not run natively. Found by: review round2-domains R2-5 (code reading); reclassified from an observation to a suspected bug by review round 3 R3-8. Reproduced by: none Expected: every change to the adjacency index, its edges or its labels increases the graph-version token (CONTEXT.md "Graph-Version Token"; [structure.rebuilt.token](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.rebuilt.token)). Observed: `Adjacency.PutShadow` on a triple that already has an adjacency entry rewrites the `out`/`in` weight and moves `^KG("__version")` only when the entry is new (`Adjacency.cls:128-136`), unlike `Reweight` (`:340`). Consequence: a token-validated cache can serve the old weight. The algorithm cache `^IVG.AlgoCache` admits only PageRank, PPR, WCC and CDLP, which count multiplicity and ignore weights, so it is unaffected. `^ArnoKG` snapshots are validated only by the token (`GraphStores.cls:131`); whether any `^ArnoKG` reader uses weights is not traced, because the Arno library is not in this repository. Repair proposal (not implemented): bump the token in `PutShadow` when the stored weight changes, as `Reweight` does.
bugs_issues.reproduced: none

bugs_issues.title: Setup records an explicitly named schema while IVG's tables sit in one other schema
bugs_issues.body: ### Setup records an explicitly named schema while IVG's tables sit in one other schema Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Code reading only (review round 3 R3-reader H3); not run natively. The only upstream test of FR-009 uses a default engine (`tests/e2e/test_262_record.py`). Found by: review round 3 R3-reader H3. Reproduced by: none Expected: spec 262 FR-009: when IVG's tables are in exactly one schema and it is not the engine's, the engine "MUST be refused with an error naming that schema … and MUST record nothing"; the explicit-name exception is stated only for tables in *more than one* schema. FR-005/FR-006 exist so that two schemas never silently share the namespace-wide globals. Observed: `initialize_schema` sets `how = "explicit"` and records the engine's schema whenever the name was given by argument or `IVG_SCHEMA_PREFIX`, including when every IVG table is in one other schema (`_engine/schema.py:2229-2242`); the engine's own comment says the explicit branch is for "several schemas" (`engine.py:295-297`). Consequence: the namespace records schema T while the adjacency index and the other namespace-wide globals still hold schema S's data, the sharing FR-005/FR-006 were written to prevent. Interpretation needing confirmation: FR-009's rationale ("an engine never writes to a schema it was not given") is met by an explicit name, so the as-built branch may be intended; the wording of FR-009 is not. See [install.schema.existing](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.schema.existing). Repair proposal (not implemented): apply the explicit branch only when IVG's tables are in more than one schema, or amend FR-009 to allow an explicit name in the one-other-schema case and say what happens to the other schema's globals.
bugs_issues.reproduced: none

bugs_issues.title: Erasing a long list of node IDs or relationships without a caller's transaction commits once per 500 entries
bugs_issues.body: ### Erasing a long list of node IDs or relationships without a caller's transaction commits once per 500 entries Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Code reading only (review round 3 R3-reader M4); no failure was injected natively (the erasure failure-injection suites could not run on Community Edition). Found by: review round 3 R3-reader M4. Reproduced by: none Expected: an erase runs as one transaction and either completes or leaves the content untouched (ADR-0004:21-23; [erasure.atomic](../ontology/features/erasure.g5.md#erasure.atomic)). Observed: the store's `delete_nodes` and `delete_edges` split the IDs into chunks of 500 (`_DELETE_CHUNK`, `stores/iris_sql_store.py:1302-1305`) and call the Eraser once per chunk (`:1347-1358`); without a caller's transaction `_eraser_txn` commits immediately and "each Eraser call owns its transaction" (`:1451-1472`). `bulk_delete_nodes` batches by design and reports a failed batch as wholly "rolled back" even when its earlier chunks committed (`_engine/nodes_edges.py:2283-2298`). `erase_bare_nodes` commits per 10,000 IDs (`Eraser.cls:1297-1304`). Consequence: a failure part-way through a large ID-list erase leaves the earlier chunks erased and the rest live; running the same erase again finishes it. Inside a caller's transaction the chunks nest and roll back together. Repair proposal (not implemented): run the chunks inside one IVG transaction level when there is no caller transaction, or document the per-chunk commit and report the committed count on failure. Iteration 2 scope: [bulk_delete](models/bulk_delete/NOTES.md) corroborates the caller's counts and partial-effect risk at Python unit level. Actual `_delete_in_scope` deletes the primary nodes before later reifier cleanup; an injected cleanup-provider failure makes `bulk_delete_nodes` report the whole request as failed while those nodes are gone. This is a related producer path, not a new per-chunk IRIS reproduction or a new finding. The Verus model represents the partial effect and continued later batches. Owner: [structure.node.delete.bulk](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.node.delete.bulk); the store's real per-chunk transaction behavior remains inherited/inspected.
bugs_issues.reproduced: none

bugs_issues.title: A BM25 index built before 4.0.0 reports the default graph, so the default graph's fusion reads another graph's documents as its own
bugs_issues.body: ### A BM25 index built before 4.0.0 reports the default graph, so the default graph's fusion reads another graph's documents as its own Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Code reading only (review round 3 R3-reader M25); not run natively (no pre-4.0.0 index on this arm). Found by: review round 3 R3-reader M25. Reproduced by: none Expected: a BM25 index records which graph it covers, and fusion reads the graph's own index ([search.scope.indexes](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.scope.indexes); spec 230 graph scope). Observed: an index left over from a pre-230 build has no graph subscript and covered every graph; `BM25Index.Info` reports graph `""` for it, the same value the default graph reports (`BM25Index.cls:603-611`, whose comment says to rebuild such an index). `_pick_fusion_index` prefers an index recorded for `graph_id` (`_engine/vector.py:164-206`), so the default graph's fusion picks it without a warning. Consequence: default-graph fusion can return node IDs from other graphs until the index is rebuilt. Repair proposal (not implemented): mark pre-230 indexes as unscoped during upgrade (or refuse them in fusion with a message to rebuild).

bugs_issues.title: BulkLoader's node and edge loads write without indexes and return before rebuilding them
bugs_issues.body: ### BulkLoader's node and edge loads write without indexes and return before rebuilding them Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 **Suspected.** Code reading only (review round 3 R3-reader M6); the bulk-loader suites passed (`test_bulk_loader_live` 18, `test_bulk_loader_endpoints` 5), which exercise the documented call sequence. Found by: review round 3 R3-reader M6. Reproduced by: none Expected: spec 252 FR-008: "Bulk paths that write `%NOINDEX` MUST dedupe and MUST end in `%BuildIndices` before returning, success or failure"; ADR-0008: "No `%NOINDEX` writer returns before its `%BuildIndices`." Observed: `BulkLoader.load_nodes` and `load_edges` write with `%NOINDEX %NOCHECK` by default and leave the rebuild to the caller ("Call rebuild_all_indices() after loading", `bulk_loader.py:380-395`); `bulk_load_session` rebuilds, and inside a caller's transaction leaves it to `sync()` (`:540-603`). Interpretation needing confirmation: the class may be meant as a low-level tool outside FR-008, with `bulk_load_session` as the governed path; no source says so. Repair proposal (not implemented): rebuild at the end of `load_nodes`/`load_edges` (or make `use_noindex` imply it), or document the class as outside FR-008. bugs_issues.body: ### A batch fallback in the embedded cursor reruns the rows that already ran Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Consolidated uplift 2026-11-14 **Suspected:** the control flow is observed on the real cursor with a scripted `iris.sql`; whether IRIS raises an unsupported-path error at a row after a successful prepare is not shown. Severity is lowered one level from Medium. Found by: [witness_ddtab_mid_batch_reruns_rows](results/embedded_no_data/20261115T042913Z-prove/receipt.json) in [embedded_no_data.rs](models/embedded_no_data/embedded_no_data.rs), with control `repair-fallback-resumes` (EXPECTED_FAIL); reading `embedded.py:387-413` while lifting public case M17. Expected: a batch runs each row once (`executemany` reports "the rows run"; `OPS-B4.6.90`). Observed: the first pass runs rows in order; an unsupported-path error at row k sends the whole batch to the fallback, which starts again at row 0 (`embedded.py:399-410`), so rows 0..k-1 run twice and the row count reports only the second pass. Consequence: an INSERT batch can write rows twice or fail on a key it wrote itself; an UPDATE batch reapplies changes. Repair proposal (not implemented): resume the fallback at the row that failed (the model's `fallback_start(failed_at)`), or run the whole batch through one path chosen at prepare time. bugs_issues.title: A property changed before node deletion loses its range-start prior in a lifecycle diff
bugs_issues.body: ### A property changed before node deletion loses its range-start prior in a lifecycle diff Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Consolidated uplift 2026-11-14; producer correction and stronger witness 2026-11-15 **Suspected end to end and policy-dependent.** Real named Python readers agree with a source-faithful snapshot fixture; no live IRIS writer ran. The promised net endpoint interpretation still needs its lifecycle application policy made precise by the maintainer. Found by: original [l2-inverse-order probe](results/unit-probes/20261115T043637Z-l2-inverse-order/receipt.json); corrected and strengthened by [history_diff](models/history_diff/NOTES.md), `theorem_change_then_delete_loses_range_prior` and the actual named-reader binding. Reproduced by: none on IRIS in this iteration. Python `GraphLedger.diff` and `GraphLedger.reconstruct` execute with SQL, revision IDs and ObjectScript records substituted; [binding receipt](results/history_diff/20261115T065234Z-binding/receipt.json). Expected: under the net endpoint interpretation of the ledger API, a diff from a later revision back to one where n.k was 1 must retain that original value, or expose that it cannot describe it. Governing owners: [ledger.readers.diff](../ontology/features/ledger.g5.md#ledger.readers.diff), [lifecycle policy](../ontology/features/ledger.g5.md#ledger.readers.diff.order). Observed: start at revision 1 with k=1; set k=2 at 2; delete n at 3; recreate n at 4 and set k=3 at 5. DeleteNodeRows stores NodeSnapshotJson containing k=2. compute_diff closes that life and drops its earlier attribute prior 1. The reverse range has an existence creation snapshot with k=2 and prop:k from 3 to absent; neither gives the original 1. The new Verus witness derives that snapshot from the raw writes; continuous lives instead preserve the first prior and last value for arbitrary operation sequences. Consequence: the range cannot be treated as a complete endpoint delta across this lifecycle. Rev==fwd.inverse() still passes and does not establish that stronger behavior. Repair options (not implemented): retain the first observed prior in the closed life's snapshot; or specify that lifecycle entries describe the deletion moment and do not reconstruct range endpoints. The maintainer owns that choice. q-con-002 also retains the independent ordered-script question. #### Historical witness correction The original headline claimed any delete/recreate lost the old property. Its fixture supplied delete_node prior="" and its script applier ignored JSON snapshots. The actual producer stores labels and properties in NodeSnapshotJson (LedgerApply.cls:339-371). For the simple no-intervening-change neighbor, reverse existence.after contains k=1; the former missing-property inference is withdrawn. The original probe/receipt remain unchanged. The stronger change-before-delete witness is corroboration of the same range-prior boundary, not a newly counted bug; stable tie ordering remains as built and its desired application policy remains open.

By extrapolation a namespace of a million edges needs about 11 GB on the client; nothing refuses or streams. - Source severity S3, confidence high; module 18; governing page here: `install.snapshot`. - Remedy proposed by the playbook arm (not implemented): Stream each table into its ZIP member with a server-side cursor in pages (zipfile open(..., 'w') per member) and restore member by member in batches; until then document the memory needed per edge and a size above which snapshots are refused. - Not yet compared with the guidance arm's entries beyond the confirmed merges. _Imported from the playbook arm by `tools/make_crosswalk.py`; regenerate rather than edit._ ## Observations and documentation drift
bugs_issues.reproduced: playbook arm, live on its IRIS (x86_64 VM): `st-live-cap-snapshot-mem`

bugs_issues.title: WebSocket Bolt counts re-encoded bytes instead of received chunks and can lose later messages
bugs_issues.body: ### WebSocket Bolt counts re-encoded bytes instead of received chunks and can lose later messages Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Consolidated iteration9, 2026-11-15 · Suspected end to end (actual Python local transports) Found by: the [iteration8 remaining-work framing challenge](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-8/next-survey-remaining.md), followed by [36 actual full-session traces and two localized method-copy controls](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-9/bolt-session-probe.json). Source: `BoltSession._recv_message`, `bolt_server.py:439-459`. Formal source-transcription witnesses: [bolt_stream.rs](models/bolt_stream/bolt_stream.rs) `theorem_small_chunk_reencoding_leaves_terminator`, `theorem_small_chunk_empty_closes_before_queued_run`, and the coalesced passing witness; [limits](models/bolt_stream/NOTES.md). Reproduced by: None natively; `bolt-session-probe.py` executes the real ordinary handshake, WebSocket session run/receive/dispatch, RUN/PULL and record encoder using local async transport objects and a one-row engine adapter, with zero socket connections. Listener and real driver reachability are not claimed. Expected: [access.bolt.framing](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.bolt.framing), from the product's Bolt4.4 compatibility commitment and the [primary chunking specification](https://neo4j.com/docs/bolt/current/bolt/message/): a message may be split into arbitrary positive chunks through 65,535 bytes, without changing subsequent messages. Observed: the stateless decoder accepts the valid fragmented HELLO, then `_recv_message` advances the raw buffer by the length of a default-chunk re-encoding. This omits extra received chunk headers and leaves old bytes. With later RUN/PULL delivered separately, the retained HELLO trace executes RETURN1 once but never emits a record, remains STREAMING, and fails to consume PULL/GOODBYE before the local transport is exhausted. The earlier small RESET witness instead returns empty before the later RUN. These are distinct concrete consequences of the same wrong offset; it does not always suppress RUN. Canonical default framing succeeds. Coalescing the whole exchange also succeeds because all complete bodies enter the queue before the wrong cut, but leaves residue; this passing neighbor is retained. The initial harness incorrectly expected coalesced failure and is preserved under `bolt-attempts/overbroad-packet-oracle.*` as a withdrawn expectation. Consequence: a valid ordinary client exchange can lose its query or response depending on chunk/transport boundaries. This is separate from the known PULL suffix loss (F-1602), transaction atomicity (F-1601), and empty-NOOP run-loop root (bug-plt-102). Repair proposal (not implemented): retain actual consumed-byte offsets from the raw decoder. A copy of the actual receive method using counted raw headers/payload boundaries fixes the fragmented/separate-frame case while the unchanged run loop still fails on NOOP. Changing only the run loop leaves the fragmented HELLO failure; both changes pass the ordinary matrix. No product file was edited.
bugs_issues.reproduced: None natively; `bolt-session-probe.py` executes the real ordinary handshake, WebSocket session run/receive/dispatch, RUN/PULL and record encoder using local async transport objects and a one-row engine adapter, with zero socket connections. Listener and real driver reachability are not claimed.

bugs_issues.title: WebSocket Bolt closes an ordinary session when it receives a valid keep-alive chunk
bugs_issues.body: ### WebSocket Bolt closes an ordinary session when it receives a valid keep-alive chunk Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Consolidated iteration9, 2026-11-15 · Suspected end to end (actual Python local transports) Found by: [36 full-session local-transport traces](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-9/bolt-session-probe.json), source inspection of `BoltSession.run` (`bolt_server.py:410-412`) versus `TcpBoltSession.run` (`:946-948`), and primary protocol adjudication. [bolt_stream.rs](models/bolt_stream/bolt_stream.rs) separately proves `theorem_noop_closes_wire_without_engine` and `theorem_noop_coalesced_closes_with_queued_run` in the admitted state/wire fragment; [limits](models/bolt_stream/NOTES.md). Reproduced by: None natively; actual session/codec methods run through local transport objects, with no listener, actual socket, authentication scenario or database provider. Scalar query output is a declared one-row adapter premise. Expected: [access.bolt.framing](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.bolt.framing). The [primary Bolt message specification](https://neo4j.com/docs/bolt/current/bolt/message/) introduces empty NOOP chunks in4.1 with both clients and servers supporting them;4.3 permits them in all connection states. The actual trace negotiates the product's supported4.4. Observed: a canonical HELLO then empty chunk followed by ordinary RUN/PULL closes before the query, because `_recv_message` returns b'' and the WebSocket run loop treats every false value as connection end. Both separate and coalesced transport frames fail. The same actual TCP session run/receive using StreamReader and a local writer continues and emits the expected scalar record; no TCP socket was opened. Consequence: a legal keep-alive prematurely ends an otherwise usable WebSocket Bolt connection. This root remains after correcting actual chunk consumption (bug-plt-101). Repair proposal (not implemented): distinguish end-of-connection from empty keep-alive bytes, or consume NOOP in the receive layer. A copy of the WebSocket run method using a None-only end check fixes canonical-NOOP cases, while retaining the fragmented/separate HELLO failure from the other root. Both local changes together pass all packetization neighbors. No product file was edited.
bugs_issues.reproduced: None natively; actual session/codec methods run through local transport objects, with no listener, actual socket, authentication scenario or database provider. Scalar query output is a declared one-row adapter premise.

bugs_issues.title: PPR native/store and Python fallback can retain different top-k nodes at a rounded zero tie
bugs_issues.body: ### PPR native/store and Python fallback can retain different top-k nodes at a rounded zero tie Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Consolidated iteration10, 2026-11-15 Found by: iteration9 frozen PPR final-reader/tie panel; iteration10 source trace, [six actual native/Python neighbors](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-10/root-ppr-tie-native.json), [source provenance](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-10/root-ppr-tie-provenance.json) and [independent intent/dedup review](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-10/root-ppr-review-intent.md). Reproduced by: `root-ppr-tie-native.py`, actual ordinary graph writes and native RunJson/WithUnscored/public store route plus actual private Python fallback with real database reads on the hostname-guarded task-owned IRIS. Physical provider unavailability and the outer public-to-fallback dispatch were not reproduced; the two actual implementations and final selected rows were. No external service or security scenario. Expected: the documented common PPR answer and ordering for shared options/explicit supported limit (USER_GUIDE547-552/590-600; API_REFERENCE1661-1678; `_collation.rank_key`). The12-decimal tie rule and the more specific zeros-after-scored statement conflict at tiny positives; [q-iter-008](open_questions.md#q-iter-008) keeps that policy undecided. Under either eventual choice, matching native/store and fallback calls should retain the same ordered node set. Observed: for s:seed->t:tiny plus disconnected0:zero, damping1e-13, one iteration/tolerance0 and limit2, native RunJson returns sparse seed/tiny and WithUnscored/public store retains both. Scores are seed0.9999999999999/tiny1e-13. The actual fallback sorts the full map by unchanged rank_key, where tiny and true zero both round to0 and0:zero sorts before t:tiny, retaining seed/zero. Full uncapped orders differ too. Limit1, damping1e-11, and zero ID z:zero give matching answers. All six source-derived predictions agree; this is not merely comparing a changed observation with its baseline. Cause: `_ppr_every_node` sorts scored rows then appends zeros (or returns early once scored rows fill the limit); native WithUnscored likewise appends/early-returns. The fallback sorts all nodes together before cutting. Tiny positive scores in the zero rounding bucket make those different selection algorithms. This differs from the inherited node-token/cache root F-1004/bug-plt-017 and global row cap F-1003; no matching existing finding was located. Consequence: a caller's explicit top-k result can change with the available execution route even when graph, seeds and walk values are unchanged. Finite native evidence and the actual source readers establish this sampled consequence; arbitrary floating equivalence and all fallback configurations remain unproved. Repair proposal (not implemented): choose the zero-tie policy, then apply the same ordering and cut to both final readers. If the global rounded-tie rule governs, merge eligible zeros with scored rows before the final sort/cut; if positive-first governs, align the fallback and clarify the ranking statement. Neither policy nor repair is approved here. Formal corroboration: [ppr_walk](models/ppr_walk/NOTES.md) `theorem_request_tiny_readers_differ` derives the raw one-step recurrence, ideal zero bucket and selected-set inequality; the larger-score neighbor agrees. This does not resolve q-iter-008 or certify arbitrary native rounding.
bugs_issues.reproduced: `root-ppr-tie-native.py`, actual ordinary graph writes and native RunJson/WithUnscored/public store route plus actual private Python fallback with real database reads on the hostname-guarded task-owned IRIS. Physical provider unavailability and the outer public-to-fallback dispatch were not reproduced; the two actual implementations and final selected rows were. No external service or security scenario.

bugs_issues.title: After a primary scoring failure, a seed vector search can return the seed it should exclude
bugs_issues.body: ### After a primary scoring failure, a seed vector search can return the seed it should exclude Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Consolidated iteration11, 2026-11-15 Found by: vector workflow source transcription; [five controlled native/provider cases](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-11/root-seed-native.json), [frozen predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-11/root-seed-predictions.md), [source provenance](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-11/root-seed-provenance.json), and [independent intent/dedup/source review](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-11/review-seed-intent.md). Reproduced by: the actual public kg_KNN_VEC and optimized fallback over the hostname-guarded task-owned IRIS, using the previously created width4 route, seed vector and peer. An in-process DBAPI adapter injects exactly one generic first-score exception; it supplies no score rows or expected result. Subsequent scoring is real native VECTOR_COSINE. Independent actual-source cases additionally exercise the embedded and DBAPI readers over a cosine/predicate provider. No organic outage, native class failure, data/metadata modification or product patch was observed or performed. Expected: [search.knn](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.knn), API_REFERENCE971 and USER_GUIDE926 explicitly leave the seed node out of this search's answer. The separate vec_expand surface may include its seed and is not the operation tested here. Observed: normal seed requests at k1/k2 return only the distinct peer, with cosine1/sqrt2. After the controlled generic primary scoring failure, actual fallback returns the seed at score1 for k1 and seed plus peer for k2. A literal-vector request under the same failure lawfully returns the seed because there was no seed-ID exclusion. All five native/source predictions and six independent source cases agree; the original vector13 observations remain byte-identical. Cause: primary kg_KNN_VEC reads the seed vector, rewrites query_vector as a literal and keeps exclude_id only in its local primary SQL predicate. Its generic-error branch passes the expanded literal to _kg_KNN_VEC_python_optimized without the seed identity. That method treats it as a literal query and does not exclude the seed. A width error is a different branch and is not needed for this witness. Consequence: an admitted fallback can replace the requested neighbor with a perfect self-hit, or consume one of the k places with the seed. This provider-conditioned composition is confirmed; the frequency or occurrence of an organic primary failure in deployment is unmeasured. This is distinct from F-C0602's duplicate label rows, F-C0603's route preference and the existing TO_VECTOR syntax finding; no matching seed-identity-loss root was found. Repair proposal (not implemented): retain the original seed identity through every fallback and apply exclusion before ranking/cutting to k. Merely removing the seed after an already limited result may leave the answer short or lose the proper peer. No product repair or owner decision is recorded here. Formal corroboration: [vector_admission](models/vector_admission/NOTES.md) `theorem_seed_failure_passes_expansion_without_identity` proves the actual primary-to-optimized handoff of the expanded literal without the seed identity. Typed provider/readers and the controlled five-case native panel establish the sampled self-hit consequence; no organic outage, universal native numerical proof or repair is inferred.
bugs_issues.reproduced: the actual public kg_KNN_VEC and optimized fallback over the hostname-guarded task-owned IRIS, using the previously created width4 route, seed vector and peer. An in-process DBAPI adapter injects exactly one generic first-score exception; it supplies no score rows or expected result. Subsequent scoring is real native VECTOR_COSINE. Independent actual-source cases additionally exercise the embedded and DBAPI readers over a cosine/predicate provider. No organic outage, native class failure, data/metadata modification or product patch was observed or performed.

bugs_issues.title: Without the adjacency index, deleting a temporal edge removes the adjacency of an explicit edge on the same triple
bugs_issues.body: ### Without the adjacency index, deleting a temporal edge removes the adjacency of an explicit edge on the same triple Severity: Low Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: review R2-data R1-13 and expectation E8. In a namespace without the adjacency index, `TemporalIndex.DeleteTemporalEdge` calls `Adjacency.Remove` with no row check, unlike the purge's `RetractTemporalShadows`, which keeps a triple that has any row; the Python docstring documents this as a "KNOWN AMBIGUITY" (`temporal.py:364-369`). `temporal.structural.end` ("An unmarked structural edge stays") holds only with the index declared. Legacy installs only; recorded as an observation. Governing statement: [temporal.structural.end](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.structural.end).
