bugs_issues.title: The OpsReview brief's one-call redaction recipe never reaches the tenant's node records
bugs_issues.body: ### The OpsReview brief's one-call redaction recipe never reaches the tenant's node records Severity: Low Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: A-history F3 (confirmed by source) ([intent](../uplift/ivg-verus-initial/intent/ledger-history.md)); review R1-core CV-6 and R1-6. Reproduced by: none — follows from the behavior shown by [redaction_binding](receipts/native/redaction_binding.json), where node records carry the default graph. `IVG-OPSREVIEW-BRIEF.md:125` recommends `engine.ledger.redact(graph, prefix="tenant|")`. Node records always carry graph `""` (`LedgerApply.cls:232-369`; spec 256 plan.md:9) and `Matches` requires the record's graph to equal the target (`LedgerRedact.cls:93`), so this call leaves every node record of the tenant. The correct recipe is the pair in ADR-0013:37 (the tenant's graph, then the default graph with the prefix). Governing statement: [redaction.tenant](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.tenant).
bugs_issues.reproduced: none — follows from the behavior shown by [redaction_binding](receipts/native/redaction_binding.json), where node records carry the default graph.

bugs_issues.body: ### The user guide says a repeated commit replays, which holds only with an idempotency key Severity: Low Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: A-history F7 (confirmed by source); review R1-core E1.2 and R1-6. `USER_GUIDE.md:1102` ("Retries") says committing the same actor and operations again replays. bugs_issues.title: Spec 256's text contradicts its own decisions and the shipped tombstone format
bugs_issues.body: ### Spec 256's text contradicts its own decisions and the shipped tombstone format Severity: Low Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: A-history F6 (confirmed by source). - FR-004 says metadata is cleared when "every" record is redacted, Decision 2 says "any" (`spec.md:121` vs `:155`); SC-004 promises byte-identical revision rows, which Decision 2 contradicts for spanning revisions (`:148`). - "The revision count does not change" (`:106`) contradicts Decision 1's redaction revision; acceptance scenario 2 is garbled (`:57-58`). - The Key Entities tombstone `$LB("redacted", digest, flags)` (`:134`) differs from the code's five fields (`LedgerRedact.cls:337`). - FR-003 requires history and export to mark ordinals, which they cannot; spec 213's contracts lack the spec 256 codes and kinds, and spec 213 `spec.md` and `research.md` are cited but absent at the pin. Governing statement: [redaction.tombstone](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.tombstone).

bugs_issues.title: Temporal documentation contradicts the code in several places
bugs_issues.body: ### Temporal documentation contradicts the code in several places Severity: Low Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: A-temporal S4, F5 and F12; B-temporal O1 (contradictory docs); reconstruction check 2(b)3. - The `create_edge_temporal` docstring says a refused write "writes nothing" (`temporal.py:260-261`); `_temporal_left` says the stores written before the error stay (`temporal.py:12-17`). - `Changeset.create_temporal_edge` says "insert (fail if key exists)" (`changeset.py:334-335`); since spec 254 an insert collision succeeds and is recorded. - `delete_edge_temporal`'s "KNOWN AMBIGUITY" (`temporal.py:364-369`) is false for indexed installs. - Spec 213 `contracts/ledger-api.md:92` says a strict-mode temporal write skips its plain row; with the index declared the marked row is written server-side. - ADR-0009:40 on Cypher adoption is stale, and ADR-0002 forbids other classes to read the temporal globals while `TemporalWindow` reads `tout`/`tin`/`edgeprop`/`tlast` (the guard test checks writers only, `test_temporal_single_owner.py:1-40`). - USER_GUIDE "Writes inside your transaction" lists two counters a rollback leaves; the statistics are also left ([bug-tmp-003](#bug-tmp-003)). bugs_issues.title: A build job queued before a layout change can leave a shape interpreted until the next change
bugs_issues.body: ### A build job queued before a layout change can leave a shape interpreted until the next change Severity: Unranked Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Found by: B-platform Part 3 "Not represented" (source reading, not modelled) ([NOTES](models/platform/NOTES.md)). A build job queued before an `rdf_props` recompile can mark a fresh pending entry "refused" (its digest is for old-layout lines); the fresh job then quits on the non-pending status and the shape stays interpreted until the next stamp change or deploy. design_simplification.title: Claim the redaction marker for one run, under the head lock, before the first batch
design_simplification.body: ### Claim the redaction marker for one run, under the head lock, before the first batch Severity: High · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Also recorded as: HD-1301 (playbook decision: should the redaction's opening check and its marker be one locked step; [DECISIONS.md](../../experiment/playbook-uplift/DECISIONS.md), intent [HD-1301](../../experiment/playbook-completion/intent/HD-1301.md)). (crosswalk) Comparison: [As-built](results/ledger_redaction/20261114T044401Z-prove/receipt.json) → [Proposed simplification](results/ledger_redaction/20261114T044401Z-prove/receipt.json) Scope qualification: both sides are the same Verus model ([redaction.rs](models/ledger_redaction/redaction.rs)); the as-built side is `witness_concurrent_targets_break_the_marker` under `Variant { serial: false, repaired: false }`, the proposal is `witness_repair_refuses_the_interleaving` under `repaired: true`. These are finite witnesses, not state counts; the serialised invariant (`lemma_step_preserves_inv`) is proved for the as-built design only. What is complicated now: `LedgerRedact.Redact` checks the marker and liveness outside the head lock; the marker is written lazily by the first batch that finds a match; `BatchInLock` and `FinalInLock` never compare the marker with their own target; counters and the redacted-revision list live under the marker and are shared by any run. Correctness therefore depends on callers never running two redactions at once, and readers, commits and receipts all derive their view from a marker no run owns. Proposal: in the first batch's transaction, under the head lock, re-run the liveness check and write the marker with the run's target digest and a run token; refuse a batch or final step whose token is not the marker's; let a later call of the same target take over a stale token. The "started" state and the separate entry check disappear. Behavior to preserve: resuming the same target after a pause, error or process death; refusing a different target while one is unfinished; a re-run of a finished target writes nothing and leaves no marker; readers and target commits refused only while a run is unfinished; batches still release the head lock between transactions. Distinguishing case: the schedule of `redaction_concurrent_targets` (two targets started while a long commit holds the head lock) — the second run must be refused with `redaction_in_progress`, and each completed target must have its own redaction revision.

design_simplification.title: Name each compiled Cypher class by its code's digest instead of the shape's CRC-32
design_simplification.body: ### Name each compiled Cypher class by its code's digest instead of the shape's CRC-32 Severity: High · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Comparison: [As-built](results/platform/20261114T002651Z-prove/receipt.json) → none Scope qualification: the as-built side is the witnesses `witness_collision_swaps_the_class_mid_run`, `witness_collision_leaves_another_shapes_code_under_an_ok_entry`, `witness_straggler_recompiles_for_an_old_layout` and `witness_readback_trusts_the_entrys_class` in [platform.rs](models/platform/platform.rs), finite traces rather than state counts; no proposal variant was run. Review R3-platform's scratch check Adv-2 showed that a shape check in `Build` alone closes W-O2b but not W-O2a. What is complicated now: the class name `IVGC.P<$ZCRC(shape,7)>` (`Gen.cls:69, 183`) is shared by colliding shapes, so `For` must compare the stored shape (`:71`), rebuild the same class for each colliding shape in turn (thrash), check the class name (`:73`) and the lines' SHA-256 digest (R311), and still cannot stop a class changing under a run ([bug-cyp-001](bugs_issues.md#bug-cyp-001), [bug-cyp-007](bugs_issues.md#bug-cyp-007), [bug-cyp-008](bugs_issues.md#bug-cyp-008)). Proposal: name the class by the SHA-256 already computed for its lines (or by a per-entry sequence) and record it in the entry; have `Build` require the entry's shape and stamp to match the lines it compiles; optionally store shape and stamp as class parameters and compare them in `RunA`. Behavior to preserve: one class per shape and layout; interpreted until built; R311's digest check; a deploy and `Gen.DropAll()` still discard every class. Distinguishing case: two shapes forced to one CRC-32 by a test hook, run alternately in job and sync mode; each run executes only its own shape's code and no rebuild thrash occurs. Governing statement: [query.compiled.integrity](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.compiled.integrity).

design_simplification.body: ### Multi-call readers have no consistency protocol Severity: High · Decision: Open Run: Playbook completion audit, reflection lane r3 (imported 2026-11-14) Comparison: [playbook-proofs-d9c `control_f1402_reader_no_recheck` (as built)](results/playbook-proofs-d9c/20261115T040858Z-control_f1402_reader_no_recheck/receipt.json) → [reviewed design](results/playbook-proofs-d9c/20261115T041012Z-baseline/receipt.json) — a reviewed model that removes this burden for one member finding (2 such controls rerun here); the rest is prose only - Burden today: Readers that span several calls check the redaction marker once before reading, and save_snapshot reads every store READ UNCOMMITTED with no epoch, so a reader can return a partially redacted view and an archive can hold writes that never commit. - Findings that share it: 2 (highest S1): F-1402, F-C1801. - Rule it breaks: SYS-I8; HD-1401 (a reader returns a consistent view or the documented in-progress result); HD-1802 (a consistent snapshot needs quiet writers or an epoch); IRIS contract E-VIS. - Redundant decision a shared mechanism would remove, and the proposal (not implemented): Validate every multi-call read against an epoch (bumped by each redaction batch and Final and by writers) after the read and retry or refuse on change; for exports, an export gate that writers respect or a refusal while transactions are open. - Caller behavior to preserve and a distinguishing case: not stated by the playbook arm beyond the remedy; see each member finding's `Expected` line. - Source: [reflection/ROOT-CAUSES.md](../../experiment/playbook-completion/reflection/ROOT-CAUSES.md). design_simplification.title: Put a relationship's endpoints in every relationship record so redaction never has to look them up
design_simplification.body: ### Put a relationship's endpoints in every relationship record so redaction never has to look them up Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Comparison: [As-built](results/ledger_redaction/20261114T044401Z-prove/receipt.json) → none Scope qualification: the as-built side is `witness_unattributed_qualifier_survives` and `lemma_complete_run_removes_every_target_record` (which needs premise P_ends); no proposal model was run. What is complicated now: qualifier records (`set_qual`, `remove_qual`) carry only a statement id. `LedgerRedact.Matches` reconstructs the endpoints from a pre-pass over create/delete records (process-private `^||IVG.RedactStmt`), the live statement map, and the statements tombstoned by the run (`("redacting","stmt")`). When none of these knows the statement — a statement assigned to an edge written outside the ledger and erased since — the record is left in place and counted as `unattributed_records`. Proposal: when the ledger assigns a statement (`assigned_stmt`) or writes any qualifier record, include the tuple (source, target, graph) in the record (or always write a `create_rel` record when a statement is first assigned). Matching then reads only the record itself; the pre-pass, the private global and the redacting-statement set can go. Behavior to preserve: the canonical form and digest of every existing record (old records keep their layout; the reader must accept both); replay and diff results; the record count of a commit if the create-on-assign variant is chosen must be documented. Distinguishing case: `redaction_unattributed_qualifier` — the qualifier record must become a tombstone and `unattributed_records` must be 0.

design_simplification.title: Derive redaction's liveness check from the eraser's store inventory
design_simplification.body: ### Derive redaction's liveness check from the eraser's store inventory Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Comparison: [As-built](results/ledger_redaction/20261114T044401Z-prove/receipt.json) → [Proposed simplification](results/ledger_redaction/20261114T044401Z-prove/receipt.json) Scope qualification: the as-built side is `lemma_checked_implies_content` with witnesses W2 (temporal-only) and W3 (whole default graph); the proposal side is `witness_full_check_refuses_the_gaps` under `full_check: true`, in the same model. What is complicated now: `LedgerRedact.LiveRows` keeps its own list of four tables and its own graph-blindness rule (only with a prefix), separate from `Graph.KG.GraphStores`, the inventory the eraser derives its work from. The two lists already disagree: the temporal index and a whole-default-graph target's named-graph node rows are content to the eraser but not to the liveness check. Proposal: answer "is the target live?" from the same inventory the eraser uses, with one graph-blindness rule for every default-graph target (prefix or not), as spec 256 plan.md states. Behavior to preserve: the separator boundary (`acme` is not blocked by live `acme-health|` rows); the refusal message naming the stores that are live; a target whose content was erased is not refused. Precondition (review round 3 R3-3): the last property holds only once the prefix erase itself reaches every store the full check reads. Under the as-built `EraseNodes`, which selects IDs from node rows, a full check would refuse every prefix redaction of a tenant with temporal-only events whose endpoints have no node row ([bug-led-007](bugs_issues.md#bug-led-007)) or with property rows that have no node row ([bug-led-010](bugs_issues.md#bug-led-010)), until those are erased by ID. So this simplification depends on bug-led-007's erase repair (and bug-led-010's). Distinguishing cases a repair must pass: [erasure_prefix_temporal_only](receipts/native/erasure_prefix_temporal_only.json) (after the prefix erase, no event of the tenant is readable and the redaction completes) and [redaction_orphan_prop_blocks](receipts/native/redaction_orphan_prop_blocks.json) (after the prefix erase, the redaction completes without an explicit-id erase); in the model, W5 `witness_prefix_erase_leaves_temporal_only_content` and W6 `witness_orphan_prop_row_blocks_prefix_redaction` must stop holding. Distinguishing cases: `redaction_temporal_only_live` and `redaction_default_graph_whole` must both be refused with `target_live`, and `test_live_acme_health_nodes_do_not_block_redacting_acme` must still pass.

design_simplification.title: Delete a relationship through one Eraser path, whatever the caller
design_simplification.body: ### Delete a relationship through one Eraser path, whatever the caller Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Comparison: none — no model run compares the as-built deletes with the proposal. What is complicated now: four paths delete a relationship row: `delete_edge` (`nodes_edges.py:1382-1456`), Cypher `DELETE r` (`translator.py:10699-10712`), ledger `DeleteRelInternal` (`LedgerApply.cls:652-693`) and `Eraser.EraseEdgeRow` (`Eraser.cls:641-677`). Each removes a different set of satellites (reifications, edge embeddings, ledger tuple and statement entries, adjacency), and the ledger path adds its own adjacency call that breaks multigraph triples ([bug-str-001](bugs_issues.md#bug-str-001), [bug-str-013](bugs_issues.md#bug-str-013)). Proposal: route `delete_edge`, Cypher relationship `DELETE` and the ledger's relationship delete through `Eraser.EraseEdgeRow` (by edge ID), so the satellites and the adjacency move in one transaction by one rule. Behavior to preserve: `delete_edge`'s return value and graph scoping; the ledger's record of the delete in the same transaction; Cypher's per-graph correlation of the deleted rows; nesting in a caller's transaction. Distinguishing case: delete one of two parallel edges that has a reification and an edge embedding through each path; afterwards the survivor keeps its adjacency, and the deleted edge's reification, vector and live statement are gone in every case. Governing statement: [erasure.entry-points.single-path](../ontology/features/erasure.g5.md#erasure.entry-points.single-path).

design_simplification.title: One fusion function with an explicit absent-rank rule and per-leg failure reporting
design_simplification.body: ### One fusion function with an explicit absent-rank rule and per-leg failure reporting Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Comparison: [As-built Python fusion](results/fusion_ranking/20261115T061822Z-prove/receipt.json) → none — the proposed common replacement is not modeled or implemented. Iteration 2 scope: the as-built side derives first occurrence, zero absent contribution and provider catch policy for `fusion.py`, with a real helper/wrapper unit comparison. It does not cover the engine, SQL procedure or Cypher translator. Preserve first occurrence, provider-score independence, empty-success modes, graph scoping, top-k details and unspecified tie order if sharing the mechanism. HD-0702 retains the P default of separately documented surfaces beside G's common-rule proposal; no owner selected either. What is complicated now: four RRF implementations rank the same inputs differently: the engine (`vector.py:1444-1446`, absent rank from the leg's length), the SQL procedure (`schema.py:2536-2537`, 1e9), `ivg.retrieve` (`translator.py:3342-3352`, 0) and `fusion.py:56-58` (0); one `try` turns a failed leg into an empty answer ([bug-srch-005](bugs_issues.md#bug-srch-005), [bug-srch-010](bugs_issues.md#bug-srch-010)). Proposal: one function, called by the engine, the operators and `fusion.py`, with an absent item contributing 0 (or one documented constant) and a failed leg raised or reported by name; the SQL procedure and `ivg.retrieve` document the same rule. Behavior to preserve: per-graph scoping of each leg; the empty-text skip; the default `c`. Distinguishing case: A at vector rank 1 only and B at rank 50 in both legs of 200 (c=60): B must rank first on every entry point. Open part: [search.fusion.absent](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.fusion.absent). Governing statement: [search.fusion](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.fusion).

design_simplification.title: Enforce strict ledger mode once, on the server, instead of in each Python engine
design_simplification.body: ### Enforce strict ledger mode once, on the server, instead of in each Python engine Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Comparison: [As-built](results/platform/20261114T002651Z-prove/receipt.json) → none Scope qualification: the as-built side is `witness_ttl_window_admits_a_write_after_set_strict`, `witness_failed_probe_admits_a_write`, `witness_undocumented_bypasses_break_the_contract` and `witness_class_absent_cached_for_the_engines_lifetime` in [platform.rs](models/platform/platform.rs); controls `g-ttl-zero` and `g-fail-closed` show the first two depend on the cache and the fail-open path. No server-side gate variant was run. What is complicated now: the strict check exists only in Python, as a per-engine probe cached for 5 s that fails open (`ledger/guard.py:20, 38-59`), called method by method; no ObjectScript writer reads `^IVG.Ledger("meta","strict")`. Paths without the call bypass it (`bulk_delete_adjacency` and the sample API's raw cursor, undocumented; FHIR sync and the MCP Cypher tool, undecided), an engine that first checked before the ledger classes existed never enforces it ([bug-plt-025](bugs_issues.md#bug-plt-025)), and another engine can write for up to 5 s after `set_strict(True)` ([bug-plt-005](bugs_issues.md#bug-plt-005), [bug-plt-006](bugs_issues.md#bug-plt-006), [q-plt-001](open_questions.md#q-plt-001)). Proposal: read the strict flag in the ObjectScript writers' shared entry (or in the Eraser and the adjacency writers), so every path that changes structure checks it at write time. Behavior to preserve: the documented exemptions (BulkLoader, raw SQL, the marked temporal row), the rejection counter, the ledger's own writes, and the error type `LedgerStrictModeError` at the Python surface. Distinguishing cases: the TTL window (a second engine's `create_node` 1 ms after `set_strict(True)`), `bulk_delete_adjacency` and FHIR sync under strict. Governing statement: [ledger.strict](../ontology/features/ledger.g5.md#ledger.strict).

design_simplification.title: Give the inverse of a graph key one owner in GraphKey
design_simplification.body: ### Give the inverse of a graph key one owner in GraphKey Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Comparison: none — the graph-key model proves the forward keys only. What is complicated now: several sites turn an index key back into a SQL `graph_id` on their own (`Adjacency.cls:583, 627, 654, 698, 889`, `AssertTemporalRow`, `Retract*`, `OtherEdgeKeys`, Python `delete_edge`), an undeclared third derivation outside `GraphKey` that is right only while `ForIndex(g) = ForName(g)` for named graphs (ADR-0003); the ledger's redaction code spells record graphs with an inline `$Translate` too ([simp-led-001](#simp-led-001)). Proposal: add `GraphKey.NameOf(indexKey)` (or pass names to those methods) and use it at every site. Behavior to preserve: every SQL `COALESCE(graph_id,'')` predicate; default and named graph rows. Distinguishing case: default- and named-graph rows deleted through each site. Governing statement: [graph.key.owner](../ontology/concepts/graph-scope.g5.md#graph.key.owner).

design_simplification.title: Bump the version token before ending a rebuild so the warm stamp survives it
design_simplification.body: ### Bump the version token before ending a rebuild so the warm stamp survives it Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Comparison: none — the warm stamp is not represented in the model. What is complicated now: `BuildKG` bumps the token after `EndRebuild(1)` (`TraversalBuild.cls:142-145`), so the whole-graph warm stamp written during the rebuild is stale at once and the O(1) bulk readers fall back after every `sync()`, against ADR-0012 and `Adj.cls:180-183`. Proposal: bump the token before `EndRebuild(1)`. Behavior to preserve: the token still moves on every rebuild; readers during the rebuild still see it as not current. Distinguishing case: `AllWarm(g) = 1` right after `BuildKG` with no writer. Governing statement: [structure.degree.cache.warm](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.degree.cache.warm).

design_simplification.title: Check embedding identity against the registry row the route lookup already read
design_simplification.body: ### Check embedding identity against the registry row the route lookup already read Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Comparison: [As-built](results/search/20261114T000543Z-prove/receipt.json) → [Proposed simplification](results/search/20261114T000543Z-prove/receipt.json) Scope qualification: both sides are `witness_identity_fail_open` in [search.rs](models/search/search.rs): its as-built branch (a cached route plus a failed identity read) admits the mismatched writer, and its fail-closed branch, the one raise-on-error policy proposed here, refuses it; control `repair-fail-closed-off` shows the refusal depends on the repair. Finite witnesses, not state counts. What is complicated now: a write reads the registry twice, once in `_read_route` (raises on error, R161) and again in `get_embedding_identity` (swallows every error, `schema.py:1054-1056`), and the second read decides the identity check ([bug-srch-012](bugs_issues.md#bug-srch-012)); the queue's enqueue check reads a third, wrong table ([bug-srch-006](bugs_issues.md#bug-srch-006)). Proposal: let `enforce_embedding_identity` use the row `_read_route` returned, with one raise-on-error policy, and give `enqueue_for_embedding` the same route-based check. Behavior to preserve: refusal before anything is queued or written; "no registry" (SQLCODE -30) still passes as documented. Distinguishing case: a cached route plus a failing identity read must refuse a mismatched mechanism. Governing statement: [search.embedding.check_on_write](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.embedding.check_on_write).
