design_simplification.title: Drawing degree generations from the version token is not a repair
design_simplification.body: ### Drawing degree generations from the version token is not a repair Severity: Unranked Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Comparison: [As-built](results/graph_structure/20261114T000451Z-prove/receipt.json) → [Proposed simplification](results/graph_structure/20261114T000451Z-prove/receipt.json) Scope qualification: the as-built side is `witness_aba_delete_and_recreate_serves_stale_degree`; the proposal side is `witness_s1_set_generation_is_undone_by_rollback`, which shows the proposal reviving an old entry after a rollback. Finite witnesses, not state counts. Rejected proposal (A-structure S1): `Set ^KG("gen",g,s) = $Increment(^KG("__version"))` in place of the two `$Increment`s. A `Set` is journaled, so a rollback restores the pre-image over a concurrent writer's committed generation and revives an old cache entry; the product's `$Increment` of `gen` is load-bearing (ADR-0012:23-24). The epoch stamp in [bug-str-003](bugs_issues.md#bug-str-003) is the proposed repair instead. Governing statement: [structure.degree.cache](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.degree.cache).

open_questions.title: Must erasure and redaction be serialised with each other and with ledger commits?
open_questions.body: ### Must erasure and redaction be serialised with each other and with ledger commits? Severity: High · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: `Graph.KG.Eraser` takes no ledger head lock; since 4.6.4 an erase made through an engine on a plain connection nests in the caller's transaction (aad50087), while an engine from `from_connect` runs it on a dedicated connection. `LedgerRedact.LiveRows` reads without locks. Probe [erasure_caller_transaction](receipts/native/erasure_caller_transaction_redaction.json): on a plain connection the erase nests at `$TLEVEL=1`, a concurrent redaction completes, and the caller's rollback restores the content ([bug-002](bugs_issues.md#bug-002)); through `from_connect` the erase [committed on its own](receipts/native/erasure_caller_transaction_from_connect.json) and the caller's rollback did not undo it. Interpretations: (a) callers must not redact while an erase is uncommitted (document it); (b) redaction must refuse while any erase of the target is uncommitted (take the head lock in the eraser, or a shared target lock); (c) erasure must never join a caller's transaction. Decision needed: the serialisation contract between erase, redact and commit, and whether erase joins a caller's transaction. Open statement: [erasure.concurrency](../ontology/features/erasure.g5.md#erasure.concurrency).

open_questions.title: Should another tenant's retry of a revision it shared with a redacted tenant be refused?
open_questions.body: ### Should another tenant's retry of a revision it shared with a redacted tenant be refused? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: spec 256 Decision 2 (Tom, 2026-10-22) clears the metadata of any revision with a redacted record, idempotency key included; the recorded trade-off named only the lost commit message (a140ed78 open question 2). `LedgerRedact.ClearRevision` moves the key to `idemRedacted`; `Ledger.CommitInTxn` then refuses every retry with that key (`idempotency_redacted`). Probe [redaction_mixed_retry](receipts/native/redaction_mixed_retry.json), re-run with byte-identical changesets: tenant B's retry of its own revision replays; its retry of the revision it shared with redacted tenant A is refused with `IdempotencyRedactedError` and changes nothing. The other tenant's `history(correlation_id=...)` lookup also stops finding the revision. Interpretations: (a) intended — a key names the whole revision, and a refused retry is safer than a replay of a partly tombstoned revision; (b) unintended — only the target's retries should be refused; the other tenant should get a replay (its content is intact) or a distinct error telling it the revision exists but was partly redacted. Decision needed: which response a non-target tenant's retry gets, and whether its correlation-id lookup should survive. Open statement: [redaction.idempotency.other-tenant](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.idempotency.other-tenant).

open_questions.title: How should strict mode and the erase-then-redact path fit together?
open_questions.body: ### How should strict mode and the erase-then-redact path fit together? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: `erase_graph`, `delete_nodes_by_prefix` and `erase_all` call the strict-mode check and raise `LedgerStrictModeError` (nodes_edges.py:1513, :1552; iris_sql_store.py:1433). Redaction refuses a live target, so it needs the erasure first. Erasing through changesets cannot reach named-graph node rows (ledger node operations are default-graph only, 4.6.0 R290). No document or test covers the combination. Model witness `witness_strict_erase_then_redact_needs_strict_off` ([platform model](models/platform/NOTES.md)); probe [platform_strict_redaction](receipts/native/platform_strict_redaction.json): under strict mode the tenant's graph cannot be erased, the ledger leaves its 2 named-graph node rows, and redaction is refused `target_live`; with strict off both run. Interpretations: (a) strict-mode users turn strict off for the erase, then on again; (b) erasure is exempt from strict mode because it removes content, not history (ADR-0004); (c) erasure should be recorded in the ledger in strict mode. Decision needed: which path a strict-mode tenant erasure takes, and its documentation. Open statement: [redaction.strict-mode](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.strict-mode).

open_questions.title: Should erase-by-prefix and redact-by-prefix use the same prefix rule?
open_questions.body: ### Should erase-by-prefix and redact-by-prefix use the same prefix rule? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: `Eraser.EraseNodes` (Eraser.cls:322-350) and `engine.delete_nodes_by_prefix` match a bare starts-with ("acme" erases `acme-health|1` too), while `LedgerRedact.MatchString` always appends the separator ("acme" redacts only `acme|…`). The documented tenant recipe pairs the two (ADR-0013:37; the e2e fixture erases with "tenantA|" and redacts with "tenantA"). An operator who erases with the same bare prefix they redact with also erases a neighbouring tenant's nodes, irreversibly. Found by the fresh-reader reconstruction check (reconstruction-check.md, correction 4). Interpretations: (a) intended — erase is a general id-prefix tool and the caller must add the separator; document it beside the recipe; (b) the tenant recipe should use one target notion for both steps (a separator-aware erase, or a combined erase-and-redact entry point). Decision needed: whether erase-by-prefix gains the separator rule (or a tenant entry point), and the documented recipe. Open statement: [erasure.prefix-match](../ontology/features/erasure.g5.md#erasure.prefix-match).

open_questions.title: Should redaction count a target's temporal-only edges as live content?
open_questions.body: ### Should redaction count a target's temporal-only edges as live content? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: ADR-0013 refuses redaction "while any **row** of the target is live", justified by replay; CONTEXT.md says redaction is "Refused while any of the target's **content** is live", and its Erasure definition lists the temporal index as content. A temporal-only predicate (ADR-0015) writes no row and no node. Model witness W2 (`witness_temporal_only_content_is_not_seen`, [prove receipt](results/ledger_redaction/20261114T044401Z-prove/receipt.json)) and probe [redaction_temporal_only_live](receipts/native/redaction_temporal_only_live.json): with only a temporal-only edge in `gT` (0 edge rows, 0 node rows), `redact("gT")` completed and tombstoned the `create_temporal_edge` record while the window reader still returns the edge. Erasure does not settle this for prefix targets: erasing a tenant by prefix leaves its temporal-only events whose endpoints have no node row ([bug-led-007](bugs_issues.md#bug-led-007)). Interpretations: (a) ADR-0013's "row" governs: temporal entries are not replayed, so tombstoning their records keeps verify equal and is acceptable; (b) the glossary's "content" governs: redaction must refuse until the temporal entries are erased, or the history of a still-readable event is lost. Decision needed: whether temporal-index entries count for the liveness check (and so whether this is a defect). Open statement: [redaction.after-erasure.temporal](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.after-erasure.temporal).

open_questions.title: Should post-commit properties be recorded, excluded from verify, or documented as unrecorded writes?
open_questions.body: ### Should post-commit properties be recorded, excluded from verify, or documented as unrecorded writes? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: spec 218 (CHANGELOG v2.18.x): `post_commit_properties` are applied "via direct SQL (Approach A — no new revision created)"; the docs do not mention verification. Probe [ledger_post_commit_verify](receipts/native/ledger_post_commit_verify.json): one commit with a post-commit property, then `verify()` → `diverges` (`node pcp|1 prop:audit_rev None → x`); `verify(adopt=True)` would record it as an adoption. Interpretations: (a) intended: the documented audit-trail pattern produces an unrecorded write and verify is right to report it (document it); (b) post-commit properties should be recorded (a second record in the same revision) or excluded by verify. Decision needed: which, and the documentation of the audit-trail pattern. Open statement: [ledger.commit.post-commit.recorded](../ontology/features/ledger.g5.md#ledger.commit.post-commit.recorded).

open_questions.title: How should an install that already holds a graph named "0", or one with a control character, find and migrate it?
open_questions.body: ### How should an install that already holds a graph named "0", or one with a control character, find and migrate it? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: ADR-0003:69-70 promises `verify_graph` reports such graphs; none does, and every `ForIndex` caller, the `%BuildIndices` callbacks included, throws on such rows (A-structure Q3). [graph_structure_keys](receipts/native/graph_structure_keys.json) shows new writes of these names are refused (K1, K2). Interpretations: (a) an upgrade step renames them; (b) `verify_graph` reports them and an operator renames them; (c) they are left and every write to them fails. Decision needed: the migration path, and whether `verify_graph` must report them as ADR-0003 says. Open statement: [graph.names.legacy](../ontology/concepts/graph-scope.g5.md#graph.names.legacy).

open_questions.title: Must temporal writes stay exact when several writers touch the same coordinates or triple at once?
open_questions.body: ### Must temporal writes stay exact when several writers touch the same coordinates or triple at once? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: spec 254 FR-003 states first-write-wins without condition and spec 255 says the latest index is "kept exact"; ADR-0010 explains why the temporal writers take no locks. The `$Data` collision guard and the writes are not locked (`TemporalIndex.cls:84`): `witness_concurrent_inserts_double_count` ([prove receipt](results/temporal/20261114T001508Z-prove/receipt.json)) shows two inserts at one coordinate counting twice. `NoteLatest` is an unlocked read-compare-set (`TemporalIndex.cls:493-496`), and two first writers into an empty graph each `Kill ^KG("tlast",g)` (`:90-92`), so the latest index can go stale-low while `Resolve` detects only vanished events (`:411-415`). The write/purge race on one triple is a defect against ADR-0009 and is registered separately ([bug-tmp-011](bugs_issues.md#bug-tmp-011)). No concurrent test exists; no probe was run (A-temporal F6, F7). Interpretations: (a) the rules hold for one writer per triple; concurrent writers are the caller's to serialise (document it); (b) the rules are unconditional, so the writers need per-triple locking despite ADR-0010's deadlock concern. Decision needed: whether first-write-wins, exact statistics and an exact latest index are promised under concurrency. Open statement: [temporal.write.concurrency](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.write.concurrency).

open_questions.title: Should quarantined vectors and documents survive erasure indefinitely?
open_questions.body: ### Should quarantined vectors and documents survive erasure indefinitely? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: `embedding_quarantine`, `docs_quarantine` and `edge_vector_quarantine` survive `EraseAll` and graph erasure by decision (FR-039/FR-040 as quoted; the spec is not in `specs/`), and no purge path exists; ADR-0004 says erasure is not a privacy tool, and ADR-0013's redaction does not mention quarantines (A-search Q5). Interpretations: (a) keep them: they are the only copy of vectors whose graph is unknown; (b) a deployment that must delete data needs a purge path or an erase-all that includes them. Decision needed: retention, and whether a purge operation exists. Open statement: [search.quarantine.retention](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.quarantine.retention).

open_questions.title: Is strict mode promised from the moment set_strict returns, or within a few seconds for other engines?
open_questions.body: ### Is strict mode promised from the moment set_strict returns, or within a few seconds for other engines? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: `witness_ttl_window_admits_a_write_after_set_strict` ([prove receipt](results/platform/20261114T002651Z-prove/receipt.json)); probe [platform_strict_ttl](receipts/native/platform_strict_ttl.json): a second engine that had probed before wrote `ttl-bypass` unrecorded 0.002 s after `set_strict(True)` returned, and was refused after the TTL; the calling engine was refused at once (the USER_GUIDE example). The guard caches `Meta()` per engine for 5 s (`ledger/guard.py:20, 38-59`), and `set_strict` refreshes only the calling engine's guard (`client.py:281-309`). Probe [platform_strict_paths](receipts/native/platform_strict_paths.json) confirms the guarded paths refuse once the cache is fresh. Interpretations: (a) strict is promised from the moment `set_strict` returns, so the window is a defect; (b) strict is enforced within 5 s per process, as the guard docstring implies, and needs documenting. Decision needed: the promise, and with (a) whether to fix it in the guard or by [simp-plt-001](design_simplification.md#simp-plt-001). Open statement: [ledger.strict](../ontology/features/ledger.g5.md#ledger.strict).

open_questions.title: Can an explicitly named schema be recorded over another schema's interrupted first setup?
open_questions.body: ### Can an explicitly named schema be recorded over another schema's interrupted first setup? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: `witness_interrupted_setup_then_explicit_schema` (W-S3, [prove receipt](results/platform/20261114T002651Z-prove/receipt.json)) holds even with serial setups. After an interrupted setup on S (marker present, no record; KNOWN_ISSUES:787-807), an engine with an explicit T sees `held={S}` and records T as "explicit" (`_engine/schema.py:2229-2239, 2312`); `^KG`, `^NKG` and `^IVG.Ledger` hold S's data, and `kg_built` is already marked, so setup does not rebuild `^KG` from T's rows (`:2356-2361, 2673-2678`). FR-009's explicit path was designed for 4.5.x namespaces (A-platform F-S3). The concurrent-setup case is [bug-plt-003](bugs_issues.md#bug-plt-003). Interpretations: (a) refuse the explicit path while another schema holds this release's marker (the premise the model's proof uses); (b) accept it and clear or rebuild the namespace's globals. Scope (review round 3 R3-reader H3): that an explicit name is recorded while IVG's tables sit in one other schema at all is the FR-009 divergence [bug-plt-026](bugs_issues.md#bug-plt-026); this question is narrowed to the globals an unfinished setup of the current release leaves behind. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [install.schema.concurrency.leftover](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.schema.concurrency.leftover).

open_questions.title: Should the server refuse to start on a reachable address with no key and a superuser login?
open_questions.body: ### Should the server refuse to start on a reachable address with no key and a superuser login? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: with no key, the HTTP server and Bolt bind `0.0.0.0` and connect as `_SYSTEM`/`SYS`, a `%All` superuser, exposing `/admin/load`, Cypher writes and `DELETE /admin/queries/{pid}` → `KillProcess` on any PID, with no warning in `cypher_api` or the CLI (A-platform F-H5); only the sample API warns about the default login. The environment-name mismatch that makes this silent is [bug-plt-009](bugs_issues.md#bug-plt-009). Interpretations: (a) refuse to start on a non-loopback host without a key (or with a superuser login); (b) warn loudly and document; (c) keep as is, the operator guide being the control. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [access.defaults.exposure](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.defaults.exposure).

open_questions.title: What should a restore do when the namespace already has a live ledger?
open_questions.body: ### What should a restore do when the namespace already has a live ledger? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Also recorded as: HD-1801 (playbook decision: what should a restore do to the live ledger; [decisions/18.md](../../experiment/playbook-uplift/decisions/18.md), intent [HD-1801](../../experiment/playbook-completion/intent/HD-1801.md)); the matching finding is F-1801 in the bugs register. (crosswalk) Evidence: `erase_all` keeps `^IVG.Ledger("rec")`, the head and the meta (`Eraser.cls:810-812`), and the replacing restore's global import only sets values (`_engine/snapshot.py:1654-1692`), so the archive's ledger entries are written over the live ones without removing the live revisions (A-platform F-B3; A-ops candidate finding). Restoring an earlier archive also brings back content a later redaction removed ([q-led-002](#q-led-002)). Interpretations: (a) refuse while a ledger is live; (b) replace the live ledger wholesale; (c) keep the live ledger and skip the archive's. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [install.snapshot.ledger](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.snapshot.ledger).

open_questions.title: Is BulkLoader meant to be the only writer, on single-edge graphs, outside the ledger?
open_questions.body: ### Is BulkLoader meant to be the only writer, on single-edge graphs, outside the ledger? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: BulkLoader bypasses the ledger and strict mode does not refuse it (documented exempt); its `PurgeIndex` → `RemoveAll` empties every graph's adjacency mid-load with no rebuild lock (`Adjacency.cls:452-473, 814-823`); its in-memory `(s,p,o)` dedupe gives a multigraph graph no parallel edges; two loaders can insert duplicates under `%NOCHECK` (A-platform F-B7; reconstruction check 2(a)6, G7, G34). Interpretations: (a) yes to all three, and the loader documents it; (b) the loader must preserve other graphs' adjacency and multigraph semantics. Decision needed: the loader's contract. Open statement: [install.bulk_load.limits](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.bulk_load.limits).

open_questions.title: Should whether a write joins the caller's transaction depend on how the engine was opened?
open_questions.body: ### Should whether a write joins the caller's transaction depend on how the engine was opened? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: `engine._iris_obj()` opens a separate connection whenever the engine knows its credentials (`from_connect`) and reuses the caller's process otherwise (`engine.py:1894-1943`); tests patch it back to the caller's connection. On that transport `erase_graph`/`erase_all` [committed on their own](receipts/native/erasure_caller_transaction_from_connect.json), while on a plain connection the erase [nests](receipts/native/erasure_caller_transaction_redaction.json) ([q-004](#q-004), [bug-002](bugs_issues.md#bug-002)). The same split applies to ledger commits without a caller transaction, `redact`/`enable`/`disable`/`set_strict`, FHIR graph calls, `set_multigraph`, the vector index calls and `sync()`, and to the non-indexed adjacency writes ([bug-str-015](bugs_issues.md#bug-str-015)) (A-ops method notes and (e)2; reconstruction check 2(a)1). Interpretations: (a) intended: these calls are independent of the caller's transaction, and the docs list them; (b) every write should run on the caller's connection and nest; (c) calls that cannot nest should refuse an open caller transaction. Decision needed: the transaction membership of each listed call, independent of how the engine was built. Open statement: [structure.write.engine-connection](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.write.engine-connection).

open_questions.title: Can a default-graph algorithm call use a native reader once a named graph holds edges?
open_questions.body: ### Can a default-graph algorithm call use a native reader once a named graph holds edges? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: `ArnoAccel.cls:255-256` says the readers read the `^NKG` export, which merges every graph; CONTEXT.md:267 says they read the adjacency index directly; `TraversalBuild.cls:758-760`. The native routes for PageRank, WCC, CDLP and subgraph have no `_named_graph_with_edges()` guard, unlike the R184 tiers (`iris_sql_store.py:3234, 3691, 3749`) (A-platform F-A3). Interpretations: (a) the readers read one graph and the route is safe; (b) they read the merged snapshot, so default-graph PageRank counts named-graph edges and needs the guard. Decision needed: a live check of what the 1.2.1 reader reads, and the routing rule. Open statement: [algorithms.routing.named_graphs](../ontology/features/algorithms.g5.md#algorithms.routing.named_graphs).

open_questions.title: Which write paths must strict mode govern beyond the engine's methods, and how is each classified?
open_questions.body: ### Which write paths must strict mode govern beyond the engine's methods, and how is each classified? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: `theorem_strict_paths` and `witness_undecided_paths_write_under_strict` ([prove receipt](results/platform/20261114T002651Z-prove/receipt.json)): under strict mode the undecided paths' writes commit; marking any of them exempt or covered makes the witness fail (review R3-platform R1-11). Per the sources: embedding, vector-index and BM25 writes are outside the ledger by decision (ADR-0006; spec 213 governs structural writes); BulkLoader and raw SQL, MCP `RunSQL` included (ADMIN_GUIDE §3), are documented exemptions; `bulk_delete_adjacency` and the sample API's Cypher, GraphQL and example mutations are undocumented bypasses ([bug-plt-006](bugs_issues.md#bug-plt-006), [bug-plt-005](bugs_issues.md#bug-plt-005)); no source decides FHIR sync (`_engine/fhir_graph.py:255-258`, no ledger call in `FHIRGraph.cls`), MCP `CypherQuery` (`MCPTools.cls:9-29`), `set_multigraph`, `Prop_Set`, the `Txn_*` procedures, or the migrations (`upgrade_to_4_0_0`, the temporal backfill), which rewrite tables and globals with no strict check. The guard's own gaps are the 5 s TTL ([q-plt-001](#q-plt-001)), fail-open ([q-plt-009](#q-plt-009)) and the lifetime-cached `_class_present` ([bug-plt-025](bugs_issues.md#bug-plt-025)). A Cypher write cannot reach the variable-length route before `_ledger_check` (transactional plans carry no `var_length_paths`; R3-platform A5). Sources: A-platform F-B8, F-H7; B-platform Q5. Interpretations: for each undecided path, (a) exempt like BulkLoader and raw SQL, listed in the docs; (b) refused under strict mode. Decision needed: the classification of each undecided path. Open statements: [access.ledger_strict.undecided](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.ledger_strict.undecided), [fhir.ledger](../ontology/features/fhir.g5.md#fhir.ledger).

open_questions.title: When a write without USE GRAPH creates a relationship between nodes its MATCH bound in a named graph, which graph gets it?
open_questions.body: ### When a write without USE GRAPH creates a relationship between nodes its MATCH bound in a named graph, which graph gets it? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: the decision says "`CREATE` writes the default graph" (CONTEXT l. 46-48); the edge insert uses `''` with the bound pair's IDs (`translator.py:10351-10365`); the foreign key `(graph_id, s/o_id) → nodes` (`schema.py:42-43`) refuses it when the default graph lacks those IDs, and when it has nodes of the same IDs the relationship connects those nodes, not the bound ones. The e2e matrix has no such case (`test_460_all_graphs_writes_e2e.py:133-147`) (A-cypher F5). Interpretations: (a) the decision is literal; the error is intended and should name the cause; (b) Cypher's binding wins and the relationship is created in the bound nodes' graph, as `SET`/`DELETE` already do. Decision needed: which, and the error text under (a). Open statement: [query.graph-scope.bound-create](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.graph-scope.bound-create).

open_questions.title: Should callers be able to choose a commit's kind?
open_questions.body: ### Should callers be able to choose a commit's kind? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: `commit(changeset, kind=...)` is public (`client.py:381`); a kind other than `"changeset"` skips the empty and size checks, and `"adoption"` applies through `LedgerGenesis.Adopt` (`Ledger.cls:488-509`), so a caller can forge an adoption revision that records changes the tables never had, or label a changeset `redaction` or `genesis` in the history (reconstruction check 2(b)9, correction 9; review R1-core CV-6 and R1-6). Interpretations: (a) make `kind` internal (only verify needs adoption); (b) keep it public and document the skipped checks and the audit meaning of each kind. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [ledger.commit.kind](../ontology/features/ledger.g5.md#ledger.commit.kind).

open_questions.title: May the server or the client retry a call that writes?
open_questions.body: ### May the server or the client retry a call that writes? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: no document states a retry policy. The HTTP server reruns a failed Cypher call once on a fresh engine, and the SDK's `_post` retries server errors and timeouts ([bug-plt-019](bugs_issues.md#bug-plt-019)), so a write can be applied twice; only a ledger commit with an idempotency key is protected. Open statement: [access.retries](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.retries). Interpretations: (a) retries are allowed only for reads and for idempotency-keyed commits; (b) retries stay, and writes must be made idempotent; (c) no automatic retries. Decision needed: the retry policy for writes.

open_questions.title: Should the sample API retry construction after a startup outage?
open_questions.body: ### Should the sample API retry construction after a startup outage? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Improvement iteration 7, 2026-11-15 Evidence: api.main captures no engine when automatic startup fails, so later health requests remain unavailable even if construction could now succeed. cypher_api leaves failed construction uncached and retries. Actual in-process ASGI neighbors and [health model](models/service_health/NOTES.md) derive these distinct histories; no external database recovery was tested and no auto-recovery requirement established. Working answer: recreate the sample app as built. Alternative: retry construction and consistently replace captured GraphQL/query/health ownership. Canonical owner: [recovery policy](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.health.recovery-policy). Decision needed: operator recreation versus automatic recovery contract; no owner decision inferred.

open_questions.title: Should standalone handled metadata calls expose YIELD aliases as result columns?
open_questions.body: ### Should standalone handled metadata calls expose YIELD aliases as result columns? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Improvement iteration 7, 2026-11-15 Evidence: real persisted A/B labels through db.labels and public execute_cypher give column label for YIELD label AS l, but column l with RETURN l. Bare ORDER BY l refuses; RETURN l ORDER BY l succeeds. [Native empty/nonempty neighbors](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-7/procedure-native.json), [qualified model](models/procedure_results/NOTES.md). No specific contrary metadata-only requirement was established, so this is not counted as a new bug. Working answer: document physical columns until a maintainer decides. Alternative: project standalone YIELD aliases consistently, preserving explicit RETURN and existing supported filters. Canonical owner: [alias policy](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.system-procedures.alias-policy). Decision needed: compatibility versus uniform result names; no human decision inferred.

open_questions.title: Should handled WHERE validation happen when no rows exist?
open_questions.body: ### Should handled WHERE validation happen when no rows exist? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Improvement iteration 7, 2026-11-15 Evidence: unsupported STARTS WITH and missing parameter both refuse with label data but return an empty projected result when the producer is empty. Structural MATCH still refuses on empty data. Actual Python/SQLite and [native cases](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-7/procedure-native.json) agree; [model](models/procedure_results/NOTES.md) distinguishes these branches. This exception to a broad refusal description does not establish an intended validation policy. Working answer: document row evaluation as built. Alternative: validate supported expression forms and supplied parameters before evaluating rows, so invalid queries have stable outcomes independent of data. Canonical owner: [empty validation](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.system-procedures.empty-validation). Decision needed: eager validation requirement and compatibility; no owner approval inferred.

open_questions.title: Should history text filters use binary identity or the current database comparison?
open_questions.body: ### Should history text filters use binary identity or the current database comparison? Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Run: Improvement iteration 6, 2026-11-15 Evidence: the Python API calls a correlation filter exact, but persisted fields use ordinary IRIS String columns. Actual native commits/history match ASCII case changes and trailing spaces or tabs, including in raw source JSON; interior JSON spacing still differs. Evidence and raw rows: [native comparison](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-6/history-collation-native.json), [spaces](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-6/history-collation-spaces-native.json), [interior source spacing](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-6/history-collation-interior-native.json). The as-built history_paging model represents both comparison modes; no human policy was inferred. Working answer: document current matching until a maintainer decides, preserving existing queries. Alternative: use binary identity for some or all metadata fields so distinct correlation IDs/source text do not compare equal; that can change existing queries. Decision needed: which comparison is intended for actor/type/correlation/source fields, and whether any change needs a compatibility path. Canonical owner: [history text policy](../ontology/features/ledger.g5.md#ledger.readers.history.text-policy).

open_questions.title: Which graph do rows of a mapped FHIR SQL table belong to?
open_questions.body: ### Which graph do rows of a mapped FHIR SQL table belong to? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: mapped SQL tables carry no graph column, so a Cypher query under `USE GRAPH` or across every graph reads the same mapped rows (`cypher/translator.py`; `_engine/fhir.py`). No spec or ADR states the scope; not run natively (FHIR suites skipped on this instance). Open statement: [fhir.sql_mapping.graph_scope](../ontology/features/fhir.g5.md#fhir.sql_mapping.graph_scope). Interpretations: (a) mapped rows belong to every graph (today's behaviour, documented); (b) a mapping is made per graph and only that graph's queries read it. Decision needed: the graph scope of mapped rows.

open_questions.title: Should every fusion entry point use the same text ranking?
open_questions.body: ### Should every fusion entry point use the same text ranking? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: the engine and Cypher fusions read a BM25 index built from node properties (`_engine/vector.py:1382-1451`), while the SQL `kg_RRF_FUSE` procedure ranks the documents table by full-text term counts (`schema.py:2484-2560`); the 4.0.0 migration guide calls the documents table the BM25 corpus (`docs/migration/v4.0.0.md:742-751`). Open statement: [search.fusion.text_leg](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.fusion.text_leg). Interpretations: (a) one shared contract for every entry point; (b) two contracts, each documented, with the migration guide corrected. Decision needed: whether the SQL fusion should read the BM25 index.

open_questions.title: Which ledger readers must refuse while a redaction is unfinished?
open_questions.body: ### Which ledger readers must refuse while a redaction is unfinished? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: spec 256 plan "Readers" lists `get_revision`, `diff`, `reconstruct`, `export_reconstruction` (refuse) and `verify()` (`redaction_in_progress`). Probe [redaction_readers_midrun](receipts/native/redaction_readers_midrun.json): `get_revision`, `diff`, `reconstruct`, `export_reconstruction` refused; `verify` answered `redaction_in_progress`; `history`, `stats` and the SQL `ledger_records` procedure answered. `history()`, `stats()` and the SQL procedure `ledger_records` answer mid-run with some revisions' metadata already cleared and others not. The refusing readers check the marker once and then page through SQL, so a batch can commit between pages. Interpretations: (a) only replay-style readers need protection; metadata listings may show a half-done redaction; (b) every record or metadata reader should refuse or read one consistent snapshot. Decision needed: the reader list, and whether a reader must see one moment of the ledger. Open statement: [redaction.batches.readers](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.batches.readers).

open_questions.title: Is an unsalted SHA-256 of a tenant name and of each record acceptable in the redacted history?
open_questions.body: ### Is an unsalted SHA-256 of a tenant name and of each record acceptable in the redacted history? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: ADR-0013 keeps `sha256(CanonicalRecord)` per tombstone and `sha256(graph NUL match)` in the redaction revision's source and the marker; a salted digest was rejected "for now" (ADR-0013:43, 49). Canonical records contain the entity id, attribute and values; a guessed tenant name or a low-entropy value (a boolean, a known name) can be confirmed by hashing the guess. Interpretations: (a) acceptable — the digest is an audit device and the content is already low-sensitivity; (b) unacceptable for regulated erasure — use a keyed digest held outside the namespace. Decision needed: whether confirmability of guessed content is within the redaction guarantee. Open statement: [redaction.tombstone.digest](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.tombstone.digest).

open_questions.title: How does an operator end a redaction that cannot finish?
open_questions.body: ### How does an operator end a redaction that cannot finish? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: once a run has tombstoned anything, the marker stays until that target's run completes. If the target becomes live again, a resumed call is refused at entry (`target_live`, observed in [redaction_interrupt_resume](receipts/native/redaction_interrupt_resume.json) step 4), and if it becomes live between the last batch and the final step, the final step refuses (`theorem_completion`; observed natively in the race context: in [redaction_concurrent_targets](receipts/native/redaction_concurrent_targets.json) tenant A's run ended with the final step's message "the default graph (ids starting 'tA|') became live again"; the serial case is unobserved; review round2-core R2-5). Meanwhile record readers, verify, commits into the target and every other target's redaction are refused until the content is erased again and the same target is run to completion. There is no abort. Interpretations: (a) intended — the only safe exit is to finish; (b) an abort that restores nothing (tombstones stay) but releases the marker is wanted for a target that is legitimately back in use. Decision needed: whether an abort exists and what it guarantees. Open statement: [redaction.batches.abort](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.batches.abort).

open_questions.title: What does erasure's returned count promise?
open_questions.body: ### What does erasure's returned count promise? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: CONTEXT.md and ADR-0004 say "a returned 0 means nothing matched". `EraseGraph` returns the number of `nodes` and `rdf_edges` rows removed; labels, properties, documents, vectors, temporal entries, FHIR rows and ledger statements can be removed while it returns 0. Interpretations: (a) the count means node and edge rows only, and the doc should say so; (b) 0 must mean no store changed. Decision needed: the documented meaning. Open statement: [erasure.count](../ontology/features/erasure.g5.md#erasure.count).

open_questions.title: Which control characters must a graph name refuse, and who owns the rule?
open_questions.body: ### Which control characters must a graph name refuse, and who owns the rule? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: Python's `validate_graph_name` refuses 0–31 and 127 (`_validate.py:47`); IRIS's `$ZStrip(...,"*C")` also covers 128–159. `witness_python_mirror_admits_c1_control` ([prove receipt](results/graph_structure/20261114T000451Z-prove/receipt.json)); [graph_structure_keys](receipts/native/graph_structure_keys.json): IRIS refuses 0x01, 0x1F, 0x7F, 0x80, 0x85 and 0x9F and accepts 0xA0 (`p_ctrl`), and in K3 a name with U+0085 passed Python and was refused inside IRIS as SQLCODE -400 "Fatal error occurred", nothing written (A-structure Q4; B-structure O1; review R2-data R1-14). Interpretations: (a) GraphKey owns the rule and Python asks it (or mirrors it exactly), so the refusal is a clean validation error; (b) keep both, accepting the opaque server error for C1 characters. Decision needed: one definition and its owner. Open statement: [graph.names](../ontology/concepts/graph-scope.g5.md#graph.names).

open_questions.title: In a multigraph, must create_edge always add a new edge and offer a variant that returns its ID?
open_questions.body: ### In a multigraph, must create_edge always add a new edge and offer a variant that returns its ID? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: spec 234 FR-007 says yes to both; the code returns False for an existing triple, `create_edge_returning_id` does not exist, CHANGELOG and API docs are silent, and KNOWN_ISSUES steers users to Cypher (A-structure Q2; R2-data E6). Interpretations: (a) FR-007 stands and this is unfinished work; (b) drop FR-007 and document Cypher as the way to add parallel edges. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [structure.multigraph.create_edge](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.multigraph.create_edge).

open_questions.title: Until a ledger reference can name one parallel edge, should the ledger refuse relationship operations on a multigraph triple?
open_questions.body: ### Until a ledger reference can name one parallel edge, should the ledger refuse relationship operations on a multigraph triple? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: spec 234 lists the ledger (US4) as not done and FR-013 requires an ambiguous tuple reference to fail; `LedgerApply.FindEdge` takes the first matching row with no ambiguity check (`LedgerApply.cls:144-157, 185-198`), and the delete then breaks the survivors' adjacency ([bug-str-001](bugs_issues.md#bug-str-001)) (B-structure open question; R2-data E6). Interpretations: (a) refuse with `ambiguous_tuple` until FR-013 lands; (b) apply to the first row, as today, once the adjacency defect is fixed. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [structure.multigraph.ledger](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.multigraph.ledger).

open_questions.title: After a raw purge cuts a bucket, should a later delete in that bucket keep the purged history in its statistics?
open_questions.body: ### After a raw purge cuts a bucket, should a later delete in that bucket keep the purged history in its statistics? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: ADR-0009:49 says statistics "describe the past" after a purge, while `DeleteTemporalEdge` and `EraseNodes` rebuild a bucket from its survivors (`TemporalIndex.cls:446-488`); after `purge_raw_before(tsEnd)` with `tsEnd` mid-bucket, deleting a surviving edge wipes the purged edges from `tagg` but not from `bucket` (A-temporal Q2). Interpretations: (a) the purge rule wins: a cut bucket keeps its history; (b) the rebuild rule wins: statistics describe the survivors. Decision needed: which rule, and the matching code change. Open statement: [temporal.stats.cut-bucket](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.stats.cut-bucket).

open_questions.title: Must a paged temporal window read show one consistent moment while edges are written?
open_questions.body: ### Must a paged temporal window read show one consistent moment while edges are written? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: the window reader pages over live globals, so an edge inserted behind the cursor is missed and pages can mix states; spec 255 addresses only purged events (A-temporal Q5). Interpretations: (a) a live, non-snapshot read is acceptable (document it); (b) a snapshot bound is wanted. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [temporal.window.concurrent-writes](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.window.concurrent-writes).

open_questions.title: What should an insert collision inside a changeset do?
open_questions.body: ### What should an insert collision inside a changeset do? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: since spec 254 `InsertEdge` answers 1 for a collision, and `OpCreateTemporalEdge` records `create_temporal_edge` unconditionally (`LedgerApply.cls:635-639`), so a revision claims a temporal edge that changed nothing; the changeset docstring still says "insert (fail if key exists)" (`changeset.py:334-335`) (A-temporal F5). Interpretations: (a) refuse the changeset, as the docstring says; (b) commit and record nothing for the collided op; (c) keep the record and document that it may describe no change. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [temporal.ledger.insert-collision](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.ledger.insert-collision).

open_questions.title: Should deleting the last timestamp of a temporal-only predicate keep its old structural row, as a purge does?
open_questions.body: ### Should deleting the last timestamp of a temporal-only predicate keep its old structural row, as a purge does? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: `witness_delete_and_purge_disagree_when_opted_out` ([prove receipt](results/temporal/20261114T001508Z-prove/receipt.json)); [temporal_marked_row_lifecycle](receipts/native/temporal_marked_row_lifecycle.json) K4: with the predicate registered temporal-only, deleting the last timestamp retracts the old marked row (`DeleteTemporalEdge` does not read the registry, `TemporalIndex.cls:333-341`), while a purge keeps it until the drop (`:966`; ADR-0015:144-148). Both keep the row rule (A-temporal Q4; B-temporal O3). Interpretations: (a) the asymmetry is acceptable; (b) delete should follow the purge's "leave registered predicates' rows" rule. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [temporal.optout.drop](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.optout.drop).

open_questions.title: May an explicit delete_edge remove a marked structural row while its triple still has timestamps?
open_questions.body: ### May an explicit delete_edge remove a marked structural row while its triple still has timestamps? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: the temporal model's `DeleteEdge` lets an explicit `delete_edge` remove a marked row while timestamps remain, and no source decides the case; ADR-0009 makes a structural predicate's timestamp imply its row (review R2-data R1-7). Interpretations: (a) an explicit delete wins and the triple stays without a row until its next temporal write; (b) the delete keeps (or re-asserts) the marked row while timestamps remain; (c) the delete is refused. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [temporal.structural.explicit-delete](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.structural.explicit-delete).

open_questions.title: May an undeclared writer add vectors to the default graph's table after a model has claimed it?
open_questions.body: ### May an undeclared writer add vectors to the default graph's table after a model has claimed it? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: `witness_undeclared_default_vs_named` ([prove receipt](results/search/20261114T000543Z-prove/receipt.json)): an undeclared writer is width-checked only and lands in model A's `kg_NodeEmbeddings` on the default graph, while on a named graph it gets its own route; `embedding_identity.py:85-91` and FR-010 (as quoted in code) say yes; CONTEXT.md says writes at another model are "refused rather than mixed in", a phrase added on 2026-11-04 (`267aaff1`, R039), after 4.0.0 routing, which favours refusal (A-search Q1; review R3-platform R1-9). Interpretations: (a) allowed at the same width (as built); (b) refused, as for a declared different model. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [search.embedding.undeclared_default](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.embedding.undeclared_default).

open_questions.title: May a BM25 search observe an index write that is still in progress?
open_questions.body: ### May a BM25 search observe an index write that is still in progress? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: searches read `^BM25Idx` with no lock and no isolation (spec 044 FR-019 "Search takes no lock"), so they can read uncommitted or mixed N/df/len; FR-023 guarantees snapshot-like reads only during an upgrade; a search during a Build answers `[]` (A-search Q4; B-search "Not represented"). Interpretations: (a) acceptable: scores are approximate during writes; (b) searches must see committed state only. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [search.bm25.read_isolation](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.bm25.read_isolation).

open_questions.title: Should plain text search use a BM25 index named "default" when one exists?
open_questions.body: ### Should plain text search use a BM25 index named "default" when one exists? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: spec 044 FR-012 / US5 (still "Draft") says `kg_TXT` uses `^BM25Idx("default")` when present; `kg_TXT` uses iFind/LIKE over `docs` (`vector.py:917-1054`) (A-search Q3). Interpretations: (a) the requirement is superseded; mark the spec; (b) it is unfinished work. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [search.bm25.default_index](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.bm25.default_index).

open_questions.title: In which order must the common-term cutoff list the terms it skipped?
open_questions.body: ### In which order must the common-term cutoff list the terms it skipped? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: FR-044-C4 says "alphabetical"; the code returns ObjectScript collation order, in which numeric terms sort first (A-search Q6). The rest of the cutoff contract was proved (`theorem_cutoff_contract`, [prove receipt](results/search/20261114T000543Z-prove/receipt.json)) and observed as specified ([search_bm25_cutoff](receipts/native/search_bm25_cutoff.json)). Interpretations: (a) collation order is what "alphabetical" means here (document it); (b) plain string order. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [search.bm25.cutoff](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.bm25.cutoff).

open_questions.title: When the strict-mode guard cannot read the ledger's state, should it allow the write?
open_questions.body: ### When the strict-mode guard cannot read the ledger's state, should it allow the write? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: a failed `Meta()` probe caches "never-enabled", so the guard fails open (`ledger/guard.py:55-58`; `witness_failed_probe_admits_a_write`, [prove receipt](results/platform/20261114T002651Z-prove/receipt.json)) (B-platform Q3). The related lifetime cache of the class check is decided and registered as [bug-plt-025](bugs_issues.md#bug-plt-025). Interpretations: (a) fail open, as documented in the code; (b) refuse under uncertainty when strict may be on, and re-probe the class. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [ledger.strict.fail-open](../ontology/features/ledger.g5.md#ledger.strict.fail-open).

open_questions.title: Should setup still record the schema when some classes failed to deploy?
open_questions.body: ### Should setup still record the schema when some classes failed to deploy? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: the deploy is best-effort (`_engine/schema.py:2578-2595`) and the record is written regardless (`:2309-2312`); the next engine is accepted and its writes fail with `GraphWriteError` (KNOWN_ISSUES:787-807 describes a similar symptom); on a non-default schema, earlier classes compiled for `Graph_KG` keep naming it (A-platform F-S5). Interpretations: (a) record anyway and report the failure; (b) withhold the record so the namespace counts as a stopped setup (FR-006a). Decision needed: which. Open statement: [install.setup.failed_deploy](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.setup.failed_deploy).

open_questions.title: May a data migration run before any setup has recorded the namespace's IVG Schema, and on which schema?
open_questions.body: ### May a data migration run before any setup has recorded the namespace's IVG Schema, and on which schema? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: the migrations build their engine from `IVG_SCHEMA_PREFIX` or the default and waive the schema check (`engine.py:1887-1890`, whose comment justifies only "may run before any 4.6.0 setup recorded the schema"); with a record that names another schema the waiver is a defect ([bug-plt-007](bugs_issues.md#bug-plt-007)). With no record, FR-006a's letter conflicts with the 4.0.0 upgrade's documented order. The 4.0.0 migrations take `schema=` only for the placements; the embeddings and `^KG` steps use the engine's environment or default schema (`upgrade.py:145-152, 259-268`), and none consult `^IVG.Deploy("schema")` (A-platform F-S12; review R3-platform R1-5). Interpretations: (a) with no record, a migration may run on an explicitly given schema and must not record it; (b) a migration must refuse until a setup records the schema. Decision needed: the no-record rule. Open statement: [install.migration.schema.unrecorded](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.migration.schema.unrecorded).

open_questions.title: Does read-only mode govern the MCP tools, and should Bolt honour a driver's read access mode?
open_questions.body: ### Does read-only mode govern the MCP tools, and should Bolt honour a driver's read access mode? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: MCP `CypherQuery` writes and `RunSQL` runs anything (`MCPTools.cls:9-69`), with no read-only control (A-platform F-H7); Bolt ignores the access mode (reconstruction check 2(a)13). Interpretations: (a) a read-only IRIS login is the real control and the docs say so; (b) `IVG_READ_ONLY` must cover MCP, and Bolt must refuse writes in a read session. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [access.read_only.scope](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.read_only.scope).

open_questions.title: Does a proven reader revision hold for every build and platform of the library?
open_questions.body: ### Does a proven reader revision hold for every build and platform of the library? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: routing ignores the library build and platform (FR-004), while the proof record holds one arm64 build (A-platform F-A6). Interpretations: (a) the revision is the contract across builds; (b) routing must also match the proven build. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [algorithms.proof.build](../ontology/features/algorithms.g5.md#algorithms.proof.build).

open_questions.title: Must the evidence gate also cover the other algorithms the native library speeds up?
open_questions.body: ### Must the evidence gate also cover the other algorithms the native library speeds up? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: triangle count, SCC, k-core and Leiden use the library through `arno_bridge` with no proof gate and fall back only on a library error (`iris_sql_store.py:3737-3760, 3977-4000`) (A-platform F-A7). Interpretations: (a) yes, gate them; (b) they are outside the gate by design (document it). Decision needed: which. Open statement: [algorithms.proof.ungated](../ontology/features/algorithms.g5.md#algorithms.proof.ungated).

open_questions.title: Should native readers work in namespaces other than USER?
open_questions.body: ### Should native readers work in namespaces other than USER? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: native readers run only in `USER`, while ADR-0016 makes any namespace the isolation unit, so a non-USER install never gets native routing (A-platform F-A9; spec 236 open question). Interpretations: (a) USER only, documented; (b) the library must read the calling namespace. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [algorithms.routing.namespace](../ontology/features/algorithms.g5.md#algorithms.routing.namespace).

open_questions.title: Must a repeated FHIR event leave the graph unchanged?
open_questions.body: ### Must a repeated FHIR event leave the graph unchanged? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: `/fhir-event` stamps an event without `date` with the current time, so a repeat writes again; an updated resource's codes never refresh and there is no delete; the governing spec 195 is not in the repository, and the route is due for removal in 5.0 (A-platform F-B9). Interpretations: (a) derive the time from the event so retries are harmless; (b) accept it until the route is removed. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [fhir.event.retry](../ontology/features/fhir.g5.md#fhir.event.retry).

open_questions.title: What should happen when other writers, an erase included, touch a FHIR graph during a sync?
open_questions.body: ### What should happen when other writers, an erase included, touch a FHIR graph during a sync? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: `erase_graph` does not take `^IVG.FHIRGraph(graph)`, so it can race a full re-derive (A-platform F-B10); no source says whether other writers may touch a FHIR graph. Interpretations: (a) the FHIR graph belongs to the sync alone and other writes are refused; (b) other writes, an erase included, take the sync's lock. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [fhir.sync.other_writers](../ontology/features/fhir.g5.md#fhir.sync.other_writers).

open_questions.title: In shadow mode, should a native failure be raised instead of answered by SQL?
open_questions.body: ### In shadow mode, should a native failure be raised instead of answered by SQL? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: FR-007 (fallback) and FR-006 (raise on a difference) both hold; in shadow mode a native exception is still answered by SQL with one warning (`query.py:2144-2152`), so a native defect that raises is invisible to a shadow run, TCK shadow runs included; shadow mode never compares compiled with interpreted (only `test_257_compiled_plans_e2e.py` does) (A-cypher F11). Interpretations: (a) raise in shadow mode (stricter checks); (b) keep the fallback, as specified. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [query.shadow.native-failure](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.shadow.native-failure).

open_questions.title: Should a bulk load by another process close the native query path while indexes lag the rows?
open_questions.body: ### Should a bulk load by another process close the native query path while indexes lag the rows? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: the native gate (FR-014) is per engine (`native_plan.py:530`); `BulkLoader` writes `%NOINDEX %NOCHECK`, commits per batch and rebuilds `^KG` at the end (`bulk_loader.py:1-12, 157-163`), so other engines' native reads see `^KG` and `pkprops` behind the rows; spec 253 research §H names the trap (A-cypher F7). Interpretations: (a) no: equal answers assume current indexes (document it); (b) a load publishes a namespace-wide marker that `native_gate` checks. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [query.native.index-current](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.native.index-current).

open_questions.title: Does a Cypher path value come back as JSON text or as a map, and may that depend on the driver or execution path?
open_questions.body: ### Does a Cypher path value come back as JSON text or as a map, and may that depend on the driver or execution path? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: at the baseline (Python 3.11.18, driver 5.3.2) three tests in `tests/unit/test_shortest_path.py` fail: `RETURN p` arrives as a dict and the tests call `json.loads` on it (`:164, 186, 219`), raising "the JSON object must be str … not dict"; `PRE_RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md:282` records the unit suite green with drivers 5.4.0/5.4.1 on Python 3.12 and 3.13. Interpretations: (a) the representation changed (driver or execution path) and the tests are stale; (b) a path must always come back as JSON text, and the dict is a regression on this driver or path. Decision needed: the documented representation of a path value, and whether it may vary by driver. Open statement: [query.conformance](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.conformance).

open_questions.title: Should a call to an unknown apoc, db or dbms procedure be refused?
open_questions.body: ### Should a call to an unknown apoc, db or dbms procedure be refused? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: the `db.*`/`dbms.*`/`apoc.meta.*`/`gds.*` stubs exist, and an unknown `apoc`/`db`/`dbms` name answers no rows and no error (`engine.py:1039-1740`), while an unknown `ivg.*` or `gds.*` procedure is refused (reconstruction check 2(a)4, correction 21). Interpretations: (a) answer empty for Browser compatibility; (b) refuse, as for `ivg.*`. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [query.system-procedures.unknown](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.system-procedures.unknown).

open_questions.title: Which copy of a record must an auditor keep to recompute its tombstone digest?
open_questions.body: ### Which copy of a record must an auditor keep to recompute its tombstone digest? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: `MutationRecord.from_row` normalizes graph `"\x00"` to None (`replay.py:56-74, 137-142`) while `CanonicalRecord` emits `"\u0000"` (`Ledger.cls:595-596`), and key and number formatting may differ; exports carry no records, and the canonical form is not specified outside `Ledger.cls` (A-history F18; reconstruction check G12). Interpretations: (a) the server's canonical record captured before the redaction is the only valid preimage (document it, and how to capture it); (b) the public reader must reproduce the canonical form exactly. Decision needed: which artifact an auditor keeps, and whether the canonical form is a published contract. Open statement: [redaction.tombstone.digest-source](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.tombstone.digest-source).

open_questions.title: Should the redaction receipt name IVG's own snapshot archives and the ledger rows an upgrade left behind?
open_questions.body: ### Should the redaction receipt name IVG's own snapshot archives and the ledger rows an upgrade left behind? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: `save_snapshot` archives hold `^IVG.Ledger` and the ledger storage (ADMIN_GUIDE:989-991), so restoring an earlier archive brings back tombstoned content and `idem` bindings; after an R114 upgrade the 4.5.x `Graph_KG` ledger rows "stay where they are" (`legacy.py:612-613`) with uncleared metadata. The receipt's out-of-reach list names neither (`LedgerRedact.cls:505-508`) (A-history F8). Interpretations: (a) name them in the receipt's out-of-reach list; (b) redaction must also reach them (refuse or rewrite archives it knows of; clear the legacy rows). Decision needed: which. Open statement: [redaction.out-of-reach.other-copies](../ontology/features/redaction.g5.md#redaction.out-of-reach.other-copies).

open_questions.title: What should disabling the ledger do while a redaction is unfinished?
open_questions.body: ### What should disabling the ledger do while a redaction is unfinished? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: `disable` takes no head lock and has no caller-transaction refusal; its behavior while a redaction marker exists was not checked (reconstruction check G38). Re-enabling afterwards skips the adoption silently ([bug-led-004](bugs_issues.md#bug-led-004)). Interpretations: (a) refuse `disable` while a redaction is unfinished; (b) allow it, and define what the marker means while the ledger is disabled. Decision needed: the lifecycle rule. Open statement: [ledger.lifecycle.disable-during-redaction](../ontology/features/ledger.g5.md#ledger.lifecycle.disable-during-redaction).

open_questions.title: How should the ledger's genesis record a node ID that two graphs hold?
open_questions.body: ### How should the ledger's genesis record a node ID that two graphs hold? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: genesis scans `nodes`, `rdf_labels` and `rdf_props` with no graph (`LedgerGenesis.cls:17-36`), so an ID held by two graphs gives two `create_node` records and one merged set of labels and properties; how replay and verify fold them was not checked (reconstruction check 2(b)8, G8). Interpretations: (a) acceptable: ledger nodes are graph-blind by design; (b) genesis should record one node per (graph, ID) or refuse. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [ledger.lifecycle.genesis.shared-ids](../ontology/features/ledger.g5.md#ledger.lifecycle.genesis.shared-ids).

open_questions.title: Must verify compare one consistent moment of the ledger and the tables?
open_questions.body: ### Must verify compare one consistent moment of the ledger and the tables? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift 2026-11-13 Evidence: `verify()` checks the redaction marker once, reads the ledger and the tables with no lock, and commits an adoption without `expected_head` (`replay.py:806-858`; A-ops hazard (c)2; review R1-core R1-6). The race with a redaction is registered as [bug-led-001](bugs_issues.md#bug-led-001); with ordinary commits running, a verify can report differences that existed at no single moment. Interpretations: (a) verify is best-effort; run it when writes are quiet (document it); (b) verify reads under the head lock, or retries until the head did not move. Decision needed: which. Open statement: [ledger.verify.consistency](../ontology/features/ledger.g5.md#ledger.verify.consistency).

open_questions.title: How should flat node reads preserve colliding property aliases?
open_questions.body: ### How should flat node reads preserve colliding property aliases? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift improvement iteration 1, 2026-11-15 Classification: settled as built (both keys are accepted and one is lost at the flat reader); intended replacement needs ratification. `create_node` validates key width but reserves neither `p_id` nor `p_labels`; `get_nodes` renames only `id` and `labels` (`nodes_edges.py:1013-1014,670-676`). The writer/reader unit witness and Verus witness are in [node_read](models/node_read/NOTES.md). Working answer: keep structural fields and return every property under a separate property map. Alternative: keep flat results but reserve and validate an alias namespace before writes; existing colliding data then requires a migration or explicit refusal. The product owner must choose compatibility and rollout. Owner: [structure.node.read.aliases](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.node.read.aliases); finding [bug-str-101](bugs_issues.md#bug-str-101).

open_questions.title: Must the streaming history reader bound its memory, or only its delivery?
open_questions.body: ### Must the streaming history reader bound its memory, or only its delivery? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Consolidated uplift 2026-11-14 Evidence: `reconstruct(..., stream=True)` folds every record into one in-memory state and only then yields its entities (`ledger/replay.py:550-566`); the entity bound is enforced only when `stream=False` (`:555-556`), as the contract says (`specs/213-graph-revision-ledger/contracts/ledger-api.md:30`). `export_reconstruction` passes no bound and also materializes the whole state before writing NDJSON (`ledger/client.py:731-739`), while the contract says it "streams to NDJSON; never bounded" (`ledger-api.md:31`). The requirement text behind the bound (FR-035 to FR-037) is not in the repository. Classification: settled as built (the bound applies to the materialized reader only; neither reader bounds memory); what was promised needs ratification. Working answer: "streaming" describes delivery, not memory; the bound protects callers of the materialized reader. Material alternative: the bound exists to cap memory, so the streaming reader and the export should fold incrementally (or be bounded too). Claims that depend on it: public case J03's "streaming export path under its documented scope". Lead L1 of the reviewed plan; neither arm recorded it. Iteration 2 corroboration: [reconstruction](models/reconstruction/NOTES.md) proves the bound exemption and shared structural fold; the actual named Python readers/export agree on the selected surviving-node journey and consume all records before yielding. This adds evidence to q-con-001; it is not a new streaming-memory finding. Canonical owner: [ledger.readers.bound](../ontology/features/ledger.g5.md#ledger.readers.bound).

open_questions.title: Must reconstruction's bound concern each intermediate graph or only the requested graph?
open_questions.body: ### Must reconstruction's bound concern each intermediate graph or only the requested graph? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Uplift improvement iteration 2, 2026-11-15 Classification: settled as built, intended policy needs ratification. `reconstruct` checks entity_count after each record (`replay.py:550-556`); a history create a, create b, delete b fails at bound 1 although its final graph contains only a. Streaming and export return a. [reconstruction model and Python comparison](models/reconstruction/NOTES.md) distinguish both histories. The API contract FR-035/036 references do not specify peak versus final size; available git history and tests do not settle a different policy. Working answer: preserve and document the intermediate-size check for memory protection. Alternative: check only the final size, accepting a larger temporary graph. Product maintainer owns this choice at [ledger.readers.bound.policy](../ontology/features/ledger.g5.md#ledger.readers.bound.policy); q-con-001 separately concerns whether streaming must bound memory. This is a specification/policy gap, not a confirmed product bug.

open_questions.title: Is a ledger diff an ordered script or an unordered set of net changes?
open_questions.body: ### Is a ledger diff an ordered script or an unordered set of net changes? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Consolidated uplift 2026-11-14 Evidence: `compute_diff` sorts entries by kind, ID and attribute (`ledger/replay.py:406-407`, `:535`); for one node deleted and re-created in the range the two existence entries tie and keep their forward order, so the inverse lists the creation before the deletion ([unit probe](results/unit-probes/20261115T043637Z-l2-inverse-order/receipt.json)). The contract calls the diff "sorted net, lifecycle-aware" (`ledger-api.md:29`). Classification: needs ratification. Working answer: an unordered set of net changes (the contract's "net"), in which case order does not matter but the reverse diff's attribute values still do ([bug-led-101](bugs_issues.md#bug-led-101)). Alternative: an ordered script that a client may apply, which would require the inverse to reverse the order of tied entries. Lead L2 of the reviewed plan. Iteration 3 attaches this decision to canonical ledger.readers.diff.order. Producer inspection corrects the old empty deletion prior: NodeSnapshotJson carries full labels/properties at deletion. The simple delete/recreate neighbor preserves those values in inverse existence.after; changing a property before deleting still loses its earlier range prior when that lifecycle closes. Keep two choices explicit: (1) display a set of lifecycle entries with deletion-moment snapshots, the current working interpretation; (2) provide a complete endpoint delta or an applicable script, retaining range-start values and defining tie order. Neither is owner-ratified. As-built selection/inversion and continuous-life endpoint values now have history_diff proofs; full lifecycle reconstruction remains open.

open_questions.title: Should weighted shortest path consider every parallel edge or the lowest-key representative graph?
open_questions.body: ### Should weighted shortest path consider every parallel edge or the lowest-key representative graph? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Consolidated iteration9, 2026-11-15 Governing owner: [algorithms.op.paths.weighted.parallel](../ontology/features/algorithms.g5.md#algorithms.op.paths.weighted.parallel). No provisional owner answer or human decision. Evidence: USER_GUIDE631-644 promises cheapest path by edge weight. Spec234 FR004 mandates the lowest-key scalar leaf, while its FR015/clarifications explicitly discuss collapse for Arno/PPR/BFS rather than weighted Dijkstra. Actual DijkstraJson reads only scalar leaves. The valid mode-on native fixture in [weighted-native.json](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-9/weighted-native.json) has ekey0/weight10 and ekey5/weight1, plus a two-edge alternative of cost4: both native path and cost-only routes return4, whereas the whole stored multigraph has a cost1 path. [Independent source/intent review](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-9/weighted-projection-review.md) distinguishes this from the earlier mode-off harness-oracle miss. Plausible answers: define weighted paths over the lowest-key projection for compatibility, stating that graph to callers; or optimize over all parallel rows, changing the reader to select the minimum admissible effective weight while preserving the storage layout. Neither answer is chosen here. The new queue proof is a minimum over its actual raw scalar graph and remains useful under either future producer choice; it is not a proof of the unresolved all-relationships interpretation. No new weighted bug, accepted repair or policy decision is counted.

open_questions.title: Should tiny positive PPR scores share the rounded zero tie or always precede true zeros?
open_questions.body: ### Should tiny positive PPR scores share the rounded zero tie or always precede true zeros? Severity: Low · Decision: Open Run: Consolidated iteration10, 2026-11-15 Owner: [algorithms.op.ppr.zero_ties](../ontology/features/algorithms.g5.md#algorithms.op.ppr.zero_ties). No provisional owner answer. Evidence: USER_GUIDE550-552 and rank_key define ties at12 decimal places; USER_GUIDE593 says unscored zeros come after scored nodes. The actual native/store append/early-cut reader and the fallback full-map sort implement different answers when positive1e-13 rounds to0. The [six-case native panel](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-10/root-ppr-tie-native.json) retains a limit2 selected-set difference and matching limit1/larger-score/later-zero neighbors. [Independent review](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-10/root-ppr-review-intent.md) finds no source assigning precedence between these two statements. Plausible answers: use one rounded-score/ID ordering over every node, including zeros; or put every genuinely scored positive node before unscored nodes and apply rounded ties within that group. No choice is made. [bug-plt-103](bugs_issues.md#bug-plt-103) is the independent route inconsistency, which remains a defect under either policy until both readers agree. No repair or human decision is accepted by this question.
